segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: We’re going to talk for a while; I’ve been given questions to ask you.

segments.speaker: lucy-anderson
segments.translation: OK.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: What is your name?

segments.speaker: lucy-anderson
segments.translation: Ol(i)gin(i).

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Ol(i)gin(i) … What about in English?

segments.speaker: lucy-anderson
segments.translation: Lucy Anderson.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: And how about you?

segments.speaker: emma-falling
segments.translation: Magadel(a) is my Cherokee name. In English, Emma Jean Falling, now. It used to be Osage.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Magadel(a).

segments.speaker: emma-falling
segments.text: ᎥᎥ ᏲᏁᎦ ᎬᏗ--ᏗᎬᏁ,Ꮧ: Emma Jean Falling ᏃᏊ ᎨᏒ Osage ᏥᎨᎰ
segments.transliteration: vv yonega gvdi--digvne,di: Emma Jean Falling noquu gesv Osage tsigeho
segments.translation: Yep, in English: It's Emma Jean Falling now. It was Osage.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: What does that Magadela mean?

segments.speaker: emma-falling
segments.text: ᎾᏛ ᎡᏠᎩ ᏥᎨᎲ ᎠᎩᏃᏎᎸ Ꮭ Ꮩ--ᏗᏳᎪ,Ꮫ ᏱᎩ, Ꮭ ᏯᏩᏅ,Ꮤ, “Mary Magdalene” ᏧᏛᏅ ᏙᏳ, Ꮭ ᏯᏩᏅ,Ꮤ, ᏙᏳ ᏍᎩ ᏱᎩ, ᎠᏎᏍᎩᏂ ᏯᎩᏪᏎᎸ ᏍᎩᏭ ᎢᎦ ᎠᏩᏅ,Ꮤ, ᎪᎯᎦ ᎮᎾ, ᎬᏳᎾᏂᎩᏓ,
segments.transliteration: nadv etlogi tsigehv aginoselv tla do--diyugo,dv yigi, tla yawanv,ta, “Mary Magdalene” tsudvnv doyu, tla yawanv,ta, doyu sgi yigi, asesgini yagiweselv sgiwu iga awanv,ta, gohiga hena, gvyunanigida,
segments.translation: My aunt told me, but I don’t know if it’s true or not. She said, “Mary Magdalene.” I don’t really know if that’s what it is, but that’s what she said. That’s all I know, it’s been a while since they passed.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: ᎡᎵ ᎢᏳᏍᏗ ᏱᎪᏪᎳ ᎦᎸᎳ,Ꮧ ᎪᏪᎸ ᏣᎳᎩ ᏗᎪᎵᏯ “ᎹᎦᎠᏕᎳ” ᎨᎵ ᏂᎬᏁ,Ꮧ
segments.transliteration: eli iyusdi yigowela galvla,di gowelv tsalagi digoliya “magaadela” geli nigvne,di
segments.translation: It might be written like that in the Bible. I think it does say in Cherokee, Megadeli.

segments.speaker: emma-falling
segments.text: ᏗᎪᏪᎵᏍᎩ’Ꭱ ᏥᎨᎲ ᏣᎳᎩ ᏃᏊᎴ ᏗᎪᎵᏰᏍᎩ ... Ꮟ ᏓᎩᎾ ᎪᏪᎳ -ᏧᏬᏪᎳᏅ ... ᎾᎿ ᏓᏮᎨᏩ ᏗᏛᎩᏅᏍᏗ ᎾᏍᏊ ᎪᏪᎳ ᏧᎭᎨᏓ Ꮟ ᏓᎩᎾ ᏧᏂᏙᎸ
segments.transliteration: digowelisgi’e tsigehv tsalagi noquule digoliyesgi ... si dagina gowela -tsuwowelanv ... nahna dawvgewa didvginvsdi nasquu gowela tsuhageda si dagina tsunidolv
segments.translation: She used to write Cherokee and read. I’ve still got some papers that she wrote – I forgot to bring them – and I still got the Bible that she had.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Where did she go to church?

segments.speaker: emma-falling
segments.text: Uh..ᎦᎶᏇᏗᎢᏛ ᏗᏢ ᏥᎨᎲ ᏧᏓᎴᏅᏓᏭ ᏧᏂᎳᏫᏍᏗ ᎤᏁᏓᏍᏗ ᏥᎨᎲ ... StilwellᏴ, WestvilleᎴ ᏱᎩ, ᏩᏁᏙᎰ ᏥᎨᎲ ᎠᎬᏱ ᎤᎸᏉᏗ ᏥᎨᎲ ᏧᏃᎩᏍᏗ ᏃᏊᎴ ᎤᏥ,ᏍᏆᎸ ᎣᏍᏓ ᎠᏣᎳᎩ ᎦᏬᏂᏍᎩ ᏥᎨᎲ ᎠᏣᎳᎩᎭ ᏥᏗᎧᏃᎩᏍᎪ ᏍᏊ ᏥᏍᏕᎵᏍᎨ ᏥᎨᎲ ... ᏍᎪᎯᏭ ᏯᏩᏕᏘᏴᏓ ᏥᎨᎲ ᏗᎧᏃᎩᏍᎩ ᏥᎾᏮᏁᎲ
segments.transliteration: Uh..galoquediidv ditlv tsigehv tsudalenvdawu tsunilawisdi unedasdi tsigehv ... Stilwellyv, Westvillele yigi, wanedoho tsigehv agvyi ulvquodi tsigehv tsunogisdi noquule utsi,squalv osda atsalagi gawonisgi tsigehv atsalagiha tsidikanogisgo squu tsisdelisge tsigehv ... sgohiwu yawadetiyvda tsigehv dikanogisgi tsinawvnehv
segments.translation: It was Locust Grove. They used to go to different churches. They would go to Stilwell or Westville. She really liked to sing and she was a fluent Cherokee speaker. She used to sing in Cherokee and I used to help her. When I was 10 years old she used to make me sing.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: ᏂᎯᎾ ᏣᎳᎩ ᏕᏣᏙᎥ ‘Ꮩ ᎤᏍᏗ ᎦᏓᎧ? ᏣᏅ,Ꮤ ᎨᎲ ᎣᎵᎩᏂ
segments.transliteration: nihina tsalagi detsadov ‘do usdi gadaka? tsanv,ta gehv oligini
segments.translation: What about your name? What does it mean?

segments.speaker: lucy-anderson
segments.text: ᎣᎵᎩᏂ ... Ꮭ ᎩᎶ ᏯᎩᏃᏎᎴ ᎥᎾ ᏧᎶᏒ ᎣᎵᎩᏂ ᏥᏓᏩᏙ’ Ꮭ ᏯᏩᏅ,Ꮤ, ᎡᎵᏏ ᏥᎨᎲ --ᎣᎩᎾ,ᏛᎯᏍᏔᏅ Ꮭ ᏯᎩᏃᏎᎴ ᏍᎩᏭ ᎣᎵᎩᏂᏭ ᏓᏩᏙᎠ ᎬᏩᏅ,Ꮤ, (ᎤᏰᏥᏍᎦ)
segments.transliteration: oligini ... tla gilo yaginosele vna tsulosv oligini tsidawado’ tla yawanv,ta, elisi tsigehv --ogina,dvhistanv tla yaginosele sgiwu oliginiwu dawadoa gvwanv,ta, (uyetsisga)
segments.translation: Ol(i)gin(i) – no one has ever told me where it came from – why Ol(i)gin(i) is my name. We were raised by my grandmother. She never did tell me. I just use Ol(i)gin(i) for my name.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Whereabouts did you all live? Where…Or, what do you say? Where were y’all born?

segments.speaker: lucy-anderson
segments.translation: Where was I born? Just there in Locust Grove where our house is, that’s where I was born.

segments.speaker: emma-falling
segments.translation: Me too, I was born in Locust Grove.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: The same.

segments.speaker: emma-falling
segments.text: ᎥᎥ ... ᎡᎵᏏ ᎡᏚᏓ ᏧᏁᏅᏒ ᎦᏓ ᏧᏂᎲ ᎠᏓᏯᎭ ᎦᎵᏦᏕ ᏣᏓᏁᎸ ᎢᎾ ᎠᏩᏕᏅ ᎨᎲ ᎠᏯ (ᎤᏰᏥᏍᎦ) ᎭᏍᎩᏂ ᏯᏩᏅ,Ꮦ ᎥᏍᎩᎾ ᎠᎩᏙᏗ ᎨᎲ ᎩᎳ, ᏦᏍᎪᎯ ᏦᏍᎪᎯ ᎯᏍᎩ ᏯᏩᏕᏘᏴᏓ ᏥᏄᎵᏍᏔᏅ ᎩᎳ, ᎠᏩᏕᎳᎰᏒ ᏍᎩᎾ ᎠᏯ --ᎠᎩᏙᏓ, ᎨᏎ ... ᎢᎾ ᎠᏩᏕᏅ ... ᎯᏛ ᏍᏊ ᎤᏆᏌ ᎾᏭ ᏍᏊ ᏣᏕᏁ
segments.transliteration: vv ... elisi eduda tsunenvsv gada tsunihv adayaha galitsode tsadanelv ina awadenv gehv aya (uyetsisga) hasgini yawanv,te vsgina agidodi gehv gila, tsosgohi tsosgohi hisgi yawadetiyvda tsinulistanv gila, awadelahosv sgina aya --agidoda, gese ... ina awadenv ... hidv squu uquasa nawu squu tsadene
segments.translation: My grandparents had a house built out of wood, and they had land. That’s where I was born. I didn’t know who my dad was. I didn’t find out who my dad was until I was 30 years old. That’s where I was born. And that’s where you were born, too.

segments.speaker: lucy-anderson
segments.text: ᎾᏛ ᎠᏯ ᏍᏊ ᎨᎮ Ꮭ ᏯᏩᏅ,Ꮤ ᏍᎩᎾ ᎠᎩᏙᏓ ᎨᎲ Ꮩ’ ᎨᎲ ᎾᏍᏊ ᎠᏩᏛᎯᏍᏔᏅ ᏔᎵ ᏯᏩᏕᏘᏴᏓ, ᏥᎨᎲ ᎾᎯᏳ ᎤᎴᏅᎲ ... ‘ᎡᏙᏓ’ ᏥᏲᏎᎸ Ꮩ’ ᎡᏙᏓ ᎨᎲ Ꮭ ᏯᏩᏅ,Ꮤ, ᏍᎩᎾ Ꭸ
segments.transliteration: nadv aya squu gehe tla yawanv,ta sgina agidoda gehv do’ gehv nasquu awadvhistanv tali yawadetiyvda, tsigehv nahiyu ulenvhv ... ‘edoda’ tsiyoselv do’ edoda gehv tla yawanv,ta, sgina ge
segments.translation: I also didn’t know who my dad was. The one that raised me since I was two years old, I just started calling him Dad. Who my real dad was, I didn’t know.

segments.speaker: emma-falling
segments.translation: …uh, how do you say ‘adoptive father?’

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Oh yeah, the one who raised you, yeah.

segments.speaker: emma-falling
segments.translation: The one who raised you, yeah. Chippewa, right?

segments.speaker: lucy-anderson
segments.translation: Yeah, he was Chippewa.

segments.speaker: emma-falling
segments.translation: Half.

segments.speaker: lucy-anderson
segments.text: ᎠᏰᏟᎢᏴ ᎡᏥ ᏍᎩᎾ ᎧᎵ ᎠᏣᎳᎩ ᏥᎨᎲ
segments.transliteration: ayetliiyv etsi sgina kali atsalagi tsigehv
segments.translation: Half. But my mom was full Cherokee.

segments.speaker: emma-falling
segments.text: ᎩᎳᏅ ᎣᏣᏕᎳᎰᎦ --two months ago, Ꮎ ancestory uh... our sister, ᏐᎢ ᎣᎩᏂᎸ ᎩᎶ ᎤᏍᏕᎸᎲ ᎤᎦᏒᎲᏍᏗ ᏂᎦᏓ ᎣᎦᏕᎳᎰᏒ ᏍᎩᎾ England ᏚᎾᏂᎩᏓ, ᎨᎲ Ꮟ ᎾᏁᎯ
segments.transliteration: gilanv otsadelahoga --two months ago, na ancestory uh... our sister, soi oginilv gilo usdelvhv ugasvhvsdi nigada ogadelahosv sgina England dunanigida, gehv si nanehi
segments.translation: We just found out about two months ago through Ancestry, our sister, somebody helped her check into it and they found they were from England. They still live there.

segments.speaker: lucy-anderson
segments.text: ᎥᎥ ᎩᎵ ... ᎯᎳᏴᏛᏴ August ᏥᎨᎲ ᎡᏙᏓ ᏥᎨᎲ his sister ᏙᎲ? ᏧᎾᏓᏱᎸ--ᎤᎸ ᏙᎨ?
segments.transliteration: vv gili ... hilayvdvyv August tsigehv edoda tsigehv his sister dohv? tsunadayilv--ulv doge?
segments.translation: Yeah, in August, my late father, his sister right? His sister? Sister? What would you say?

segments.speaker: emma-falling
segments.translation: No, it was his daughter.

segments.speaker: lucy-anderson
segments.text: ᎤᏪᏥ, ᎤᏪᏥ ᏧᏲᎱᏒ --ᎮᏍᏗ ᏲᎦᏅ,Ꮦ ᎡᎲ ... ᎯᎢ ᎪᏪᎵ ᏥᏚᎷᏨ ᏗᏓᏁᎸ ᏙᎲ?
segments.transliteration: uwetsi, uwetsi tsuyohusv --hesdi yoganv,te ehv ... hii goweli tsidulutsv didanelv dohv?
segments.translation: His child, his daughter…she passed away. We didn’t know she was alive. Some papers came to the house…

segments.speaker: emma-falling
segments.translation: From a lawyer’s office.

segments.speaker: lucy-anderson
segments.text: ᎥᎥ California ᏗᏢ ᏧᎶᏒ ᎾᎾᎿ ancestory ᎤᏅ,ᏔᏁ ... ᎤᎾ ᎤᎾ,ᏕᎳᎰᏒ ᎠᎭᏂ ᎣᏤᎲ Ꮭ ᏳᏅ,Ꮦ Ꮎ ᎠᎨᏯ
segments.transliteration: vv California ditlv tsulosv nanahna ancestory unv,tane ... una una,delahosv ahani otsehv tla yunv,te na ageya
segments.translation: Yeah, they were from California. They used that ancestry thing. That’s where they found out where we were from, cause that girl didn’t know.

segments.speaker: emma-falling
segments.text: ᏍᎩᎾ, ... ᎠᏂ-Merrill—Merrill ᎮᎾ, ᏚᎾ,ᏙᎥ M-e-r-r-i-l-l Merrill
segments.transliteration: sgina, ... ani-Merrill—Merrill hena, duna,dov M-e-r-r-i-l-l Merrill
segments.translation: Their name was Merrill, m-e-r-r-i-l-l, Merrill.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: Ꮎ’Ꭱ ‘Ꮩ ᎤᏟ ᎢᎦ ᏗᏍᏓᏛᏏᏙᎸ ᏥᏍᏗᏃᎮ ᎦᎶᏇᏗ ᏗᏍᏓᏕᎶᏆᎥᏛᎲ ᏍᏊ ᎥᎾᏴ ᎥᎾ ᏗᏍᏓᏕᎶᏆᎡ
segments.transliteration: na’e ‘do utli iga disdadvsidolv tsisdinohe galoquedi disdadeloquavdvhv squu vnayv vna disdadeloquae
segments.translation: You two talked about growing up in Locust Grove – is that where you went to school, too?

segments.speaker: emma-falling
segments.translation: Yeah. It was called Iron Post.

segments.speaker: lucy-anderson
segments.translation: A little bitty school.

segments.speaker: emma-falling
segments.text: ᎤᏍᏗ ᏧᎾᏕᎶᏆᏗ ᎡᎳᏗᏭ ᏥᏬᏥᎶᏍᎬ ᎥᎾ ᎡᎵᏏ ᎡᏚᏓ ᏧᏁᏅᏒ ᏌᎷᏱ ᏥᏬᎩᏅᏅ ᏬᎩᎷᎯᏍᏗ ᏌᎷᏱ ᏬᏥᎶᏍᎬ (ᎤᏂᏰᏥᏍᎦ) ᎥᎾ ᏙᎩᎾᏕᎶᏆᎥ ᎠᏎᏅ...
segments.transliteration: usdi tsunadeloquadi eladiwu tsiwotsilosgv vna elisi eduda tsunenvsv saluyi tsiwoginvnv wogiluhisdi saluyi wotsilosgv (uniyetsisga) vna doginadeloquav asenv...
segments.translation: It was a little school. We would walk to school from our grandparents’ house. We climbed over a hill to get there. We had a trail that went through the woods to get to the school. That’s where we went to school.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: To the eighth grade?

segments.speaker: emma-falling
segments.translation: Yeah, just to eighth grade.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: When you finished there…

segments.speaker: emma-falling
segments.translation: Locust Grove.

segments.speaker: lucy-anderson
segments.text: ᎠᏯ ᎨᎲ ᎦᎶᏇᏗ ᏥᏩᏩᎴᏅᎲ ᎯᎾᏃ Chilocco Indian School ᏥᏭᏕᏅ ᎪᎯᏗ
segments.transliteration: aya gehv galoquedi tsiwawalenvhv hinano Chilocco Indian School tsiwudenv gohidi
segments.translation: Locust Grove…I went to Locust Grove, but she moved to Chilocco Indian School for a while.

segments.speaker: emma-falling
segments.text: ᎥᎾ ᏂᎦᏓ ᏙᎦᏙᎵᏨ Durbin, Russell, ChrisᏅ ᎤᏍᏓᏴᎲᏍᎩ ᏗᎾᏓᎸ Ꮎ August...ᎦᎶᏂ ᎧᎸ ᏔᎵ ᏐᏁᎳᏚ ᏑᏓᎵᏍᎪᎯ ᏌᏊ ᏧᏕᏘᏴᏒ ᎾᎯᏳ...
segments.transliteration: vna nigada dogadolitsv Durbin, Russell, Chrisnv usdayvhvsgi dinadalv na August...galoni kalv tali soneladu sudalisgohi saquu tsudetiyvsv nahiyu...
segments.translation: That’s when we all got acquainted with Durbin and Russell. His wife, Chris, and her sister. It was August...August…1961.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: That’s when you graduated?

segments.speaker: emma-falling
segments.text: ᎥᎥ ... ᏅᎩ ᏧᏕᏘᏴᏓ ᎣᎦᏕᏅ ᎠᏎᏛ ᎮᏍᏗ ᏲᎩᏲᎱᏎᎸ Ꮎ friendship
segments.transliteration: vv ... nvgi tsudetiyvda ogadenv asedv hesdi yogiyohuselv na friendship
segments.translation: Yeah. We were there four years. But we never did lose our friendship.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: ᏙᏍᎪ? ᏂᎦᏓ ᏗᏣᏓᏙᎵᎦ ᎨᎰ ᎣᏍᏓ? Ꮟ ᎠᎢᏎ? ᎪᎯᏴ ᏥᎩ Ꮟ ᎠᎢᏎᏍ?
segments.transliteration: dosgo? nigada ditsadadoliga geho osda? si aise? gohiyv tsigi si aises?
segments.translation: You all still know each other? It’s still going? Nowadays, it’s still going?

segments.speaker: emma-falling
segments.translation: They are coming in a little while, right?

segments.speaker: lucy-anderson
segments.translation: They're coming sometime.

segments.speaker: emma-falling
segments.text: ... and uh... ᎮᏍᏗ bus-Ꭲ ᏲᏣᏣᎥᏍᎨ ᎡᎳᏗᏭ ᏦᏥᎶᏍᎬ Ꮭ ᏲᎩᎲ ... ᏗᎦᏚᎲ ᏍᏊ ᏲᎨᎾ
segments.transliteration: ... and uh... hesdi bus-i yotsatsavsge eladiwu tsotsilosgv tla yogihv ... digaduhv squu yogena
segments.translation: They're coming sometime… We didn’t ride the bus when we went somewhere, even when we went to town…

segments.speaker: lucy-anderson
segments.translation: On foot back then.

segments.speaker: emma-falling
segments.translation: We walked six miles.

segments.speaker: lucy-anderson
segments.text: ᏃᏊᎴ ᏥᏙᎦᏂᎩᏌ Mama ᎪᎱᏍᏗ --ᎡᏥ ᎪᎱᏍᏗ ᏳᏩᏌ taxi ᏤᎲ ᎦᎶᏇᏗ ... ᏍᎩᎾ ᏥᏙᎩᎧᎲᏍᎬ ᏗᏓᏁᎸ ... MamaᏛ ᏥᎨᎲ Ꮎ ... ᏏᏆᏛ ᏥᏚᎾᏝᎥ ᎡᏙᏗ ᏥᏚᎸᏫᏍᏓᏁᎲ ᏛᎵᏏᎢ Ꮎ week ᎢᎪᎯᏓ ᏧᏪᏙᎲ ᏃᏊᎴ Friday ᏱᎩ, ᏧᎷᎬ ... MamaᏛ ᏗᎦᏚᎲ ᏲᎨᎾ Ꮎ ᏏᏆ ᎤᏂᎩᏍᏗ ᏧᏩᏍᎬ Ꮎ Ꮭ ᏯᏩᏅ,Ꮤ, ᏱᏣᏅ,Ꮤ, ᏳᏍᏗ ᎨᎲ Ꮎ ...
segments.transliteration: noquule tsidoganigisa Mama gohusdi --etsi gohusdi yuwasa taxi tsehv galoquedi ... sgina tsidogikahvsgv didanelv ... Mamadv tsigehv na ... siquadv tsidunatlav edodi tsidulvwisdanehv dvlisii na week igohida tsuwedohv noquule Friday yigi, tsulugv ... Mamadv digaduhv yogena na siqua unigisdi tsuwasgv na tla yawanv,ta, yitsanv,ta, yusdi gehv na ...
segments.translation: And when we got ready to go home, Mama bought something. There was a taxi in Locust Grove. And it would take us home. Mama was working and our dad was working in Tulsa – stayed for a week there. And he would come home on Fridays. And Mama went to town and she bought hog food. I don’t know if you know what it is…

segments.speaker: emma-falling
segments.translation: Shorts.

segments.speaker: lucy-anderson
segments.text: shorts Ꮎ ... ᏂᎪᎯᎸ I had to...ᎠᏯᏛ ᎠᏬᏢᏗ ᏥᎨᎲ (ᎤᏂᏰᏥᏍᎦ) ᏙᏳ...
segments.transliteration: shorts na ... nigohilv I had to...ayadv awotlvdi tsigehv (uniyetsisga) doyu...
segments.translation: Shorts – I had to mix it up all the time.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: They had you two working?

segments.speaker: lucy-anderson
segments.translation: Oh yeah.

segments.speaker: emma-falling
segments.translation: Yeah. We worked.

segments.speaker: lucy-anderson
segments.text: ᎮᏍᏗ ᏙᎯᏯ--ᎮᏍᏗ ᏙᎯᏯ ᏱᏃᎦᏛᏁᎴ ᎡᏥ--Ꭱ-ᎡᎵᏏᏛ ᏥᎨᎲ ᏙᎲ? ᏙᏳ ᏦᎩᎾᏝᎥ ᏂᎪᎯᎸ ᎠᏎᏅ ᏦᏣᏕᎶᏆᏍᎬ ᎣᏍᏓ ᎠᏛᏁ,Ꮧ ᏃᏊ ᏥᎩ ᎣᎦᏅᏓᏗ ᎡᏧᎳᏛ ᏭᎪᏛ ᎦᏅᏓᏗᏍᎪ ᏙᎩᎸᏫᏍᏓᏁᎸ ᏍᎩᎾ ᎣᎩᏍᏕᎵᏍᎪ ᏃᏊ ᏥᎩ ... ᎣᏍᏓ ᎠᏛᏁ,Ꮧ
segments.transliteration: hesdi dohiya--hesdi dohiya yinogadvnele etsi--e-elisidv tsigehv dohv? doyu tsoginatlav nigohilv asenv tsotsadeloquasgv osda advne,di noquu tsigi oganvdadi etsuladv wugodv ganvdadisgo dogilvwisdanelv sgina ogisdelisgo noquu tsigi ... osda advne,di
segments.translation: We never stopped working. And Mom...Grandma had us working all the time. But we were learning to do good, now I think about all the work we did – it helps us do things today.

segments.speaker: emma-falling
segments.translation: Yeah, we weren’t lazy.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: And they didn’t let you.

segments.speaker: lucy-anderson
segments.translation: Uh-uh.

segments.speaker: emma-falling
segments.text: ᏝᏍᏊ ᎡᎵᏏ ᏥᎨᎲ ᎮᏃ ᏂᎦᏓ ᏧᎵᏏ ᏗᏂᏲᏟ ... ᏂᎦᏓ ᏧᎸᏉᏗ ᎨᎲ
segments.transliteration: tlasquu elisi tsigehv heno nigada tsulisi diniyotli ... nigada tsulvquodi gehv
segments.translation: My grandma, her grandkids – she loved them all.

segments.speaker: lucy-anderson
segments.text: ᏕᎨᏠᎲᏍᎬ ᏍᏊ ᏙᎲ? Ꮎ ᎦᏚ ᏧᏬᏢᏅ ᏚᎰ ᏂᎪᎯᎸ ᏥᏚᎰ ᎾᏅ ᏒᎩ... ᎾᏅ ...ᎣᎦᎵᏍᏓᏴᏗ ᏲᎦᏚᎵ ᏍᎩᎾ ᏥᏬᏥᎩᏍᎪ ᎦᏚ ᎾᏅ ᏒᎩ ᎾᏅ ᎠᎹ ᏃᏊᎴ ᏦᏣᏂᎩᏍᎪ ᎤᏙᏓᏩᏓ ᏙᏣᏁᎶᎲᏍᎪ ... ᎮᏍᏗᏅ ᎦᎵᏦᏕ ᏲᏥᏴᏝ ᎨᎲ Ꮎ ...
segments.transliteration: degetlohvsgv squu dohv? na gadu tsuwotlvnv duho nigohilv tsiduho nanv svgi... nanv ...ogalisdayvdi yogaduli sgina tsiwotsigisgo gadu nanv svgi nanv ama noquule tsotsanigisgo udodawada dotsanelohvsgo ... hesdinv galitsode yotsiyvtla gehv na ...
segments.translation: And she would feed them, ain’t it? She would always have biscuits and onion…When we were hungry, that’s what we would get to eat. The biscuit, onion with salt. And then we would leave and go play all day. We never did stay in the house.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: ᏍᎩᏛ ᏥᎾᎾ,ᏓᏛᏁᎲ ᎡᏘᏴ “ᏙᏱ ᏗᏣᏁᎶᏄᎦ,” ᏯᎾ,ᏓᏙᏌ ᏥᎨᎲ
segments.transliteration: sgidv tsinana,dadvnehv etiyv “doyi ditsanelonuga,” yana,dadosa tsigehv
segments.translation: That’s what they used to do, “Go play outside,” they would tell us.

segments.speaker: lucy-anderson
segments.text: ᎾᏍᏊ ᎩᎶ ᏳᏂᎷᏣ Ꮎ elders ᏳᏂᎷᏣ ... ᎮᏍᏗ ᎦᎵᏦᏕ ᏲᏥᏯᎥ “ᏙᏱ ᎢᏤᎾ!” ᏣᏗ
segments.transliteration: nasquu gilo yunilutsa na elders yunilutsa ... hesdi galitsode yotsiyav “doyi itsena!” tsadi
segments.translation: And when the elders came, we couldn’t stay in the house. “Go outside,” they’d tell us.

segments.speaker: emma-falling
segments.translation: “Only grown-ups inside the house,” they’d say.

segments.speaker: lucy-anderson
segments.text: ᎾᏅ ᏍᏊ ᏲᎦᎵ,ᏍᏓᏴᎾ ᎠᎬᏱ ᎤᎾᎵ,ᏍᏓᏴ,Ꮧ ᎨᎲ ᎠᏯᏅ ᎣᏂ ᏗᏂᏲᏟ ᎣᏂ
segments.transliteration: nanv squu yogali,sdayvna agvyi unali,sdayv,di gehv ayanv oni diniyotli oni
segments.translation: And when we ate, they ate first, and we ate last. The children last.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Ate what was left.

segments.speaker: lucy-anderson
segments.translation: The leftovers. We all fought over the leftovers.

segments.speaker: emma-falling
segments.text: Ꮎ ᎡᎵᏏᏛᏃ ᎠᏎᏛ ᎠᎵ,ᏍᏓᏴ,Ꮧ ᎤᏯᎸᏍᏗ ᎨᎰ ᏂᎪᎯᎸ Ꮎ ᎤᏲ ᏄᎾ,ᏓᏛᏅ ... ᏂᎦᏓ ᏗᏂᏲᏟ, ᏧᎵᏏ, ᏔᎷᎩᏍᎩ ᏙᎩᎰ Ꮎ ᎯᎢ ᏱᎩᏗ--
segments.transliteration: na elisidvno asedv ali,sdayv,di uyalvsdi geho nigohilv na uyo nuna,dadvnv ... nigada diniyotli, tsulisi, talugisgi dogiho na hii yigidi--
segments.translation: Grandma had to go get some food all the time because they really were poor. All the grandkids had metal buckets, this big…

segments.speaker: lucy-anderson
segments.text: lard bucketᏛ ᏥᎨᎲ ᎾᎯᏳ ᏥᎨᎲ ᎪᎢ ᏗᎦᏢᏔᏅ
segments.transliteration: lard bucketdv tsigehv nahiyu tsigehv goi digatlvtanv
segments.translation: It was a lard bucket back then, grease buckets.

segments.speaker: emma-falling
segments.text: ᎪᎢ ᏗᎦᎵ,ᏔᏅ ᏙᎩᎰ ᏂᎦᏓ, ᏙᏥᏰᎰ ᎾᎿ ᏗᎦᏘᏍᏙᏗ ᏧᏬᏢᏅ ᎤᏩᏌ ᏚᏩᏴ
segments.transliteration: goi digali,tanv dogiho nigada, dotsiyeho nahna digatisdodi tsuwotlvnv uwasa duwayv
segments.translation: Grease buckets. We all had gigs that she had that she made herself.

segments.speaker: lucy-anderson
segments.translation: We all had one.

segments.speaker: emma-falling
segments.translation: By the water…

segments.speaker: lucy-anderson
segments.text: ᎠᏰᏟ ᏑᏟᎶᏓ Ꮩ Ꭽ ᏦᏥᏁᎸ ᎦᏚᏏ, ᏗᏢ, ᎯᎢ ᏗᏢ, ᎠᎹᏱ ... ᏍᎩᎾ Spring Creek ᏧᏪᏴ ᎥᎾ ᏥᎨᎲᎨ
segments.transliteration: ayetli sutliloda do ha tsotsinelv gadusi, ditlv, hii ditlv, amayi ... sgina Spring Creek tsuweyv vna tsigehvge
segments.translation: It’s about half a mile, huh? Where we lived on the hill, this way, there's a spring creek there, right?

segments.speaker: emma-falling
segments.text: ᎥᎥ ᏃᏭᏛ “ᎠᎵ,ᏍᏓᏴ,Ꮧ ᎢᎩᏯᎸᏍᏗ,” ᎣᎪᏎᎰ ᏔᎷᎩᏍᎩ ᏙᎩᏁᎰ ᏗᎧ-- Ꮎ ... ᏗᎦ--
segments.transliteration: vv nowudv “ali,sdayv,di igiyalvsdi,” ogoseho talugisgi dogineho dika-- na ... diga--
segments.translation: Yeah. And they told us we had to go get food. They gave us the buckets and the gigs.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: The gigs.

segments.speaker: emma-falling
segments.text: Yeah, ᏗᎦᏘᏍᏗ ... ᏃᏊ ᎠᎹᏱ ᎣᏤᎪ ᏂᎬ ᎧᎵ ᏥᏍᏛᎾ ᏙᎩᎸᏙ ᎠᎵ,ᏣᏗ ... ᎤᏩᏌ ᎠᏑᎲᏍᎪ ᏙᎲ? Grandma was...
segments.transliteration: Yeah, digatisdi ... noquu amayi otsego nigv kali tsisdvna dogilvdo ali,tsadi ... uwasa asuhvsgo dohv? Grandma was...
segments.translation: Yeah, the gigs… Then we would go to the water. We would have our own buckets full of crawdads. But the fish, she would fish by herself, ain’t it?

segments.speaker: lucy-anderson
segments.translation: While we were catching the crawdads.

segments.speaker: emma-falling
segments.translation: I guess we had to do that back then, hunt for our food.

segments.speaker: lucy-anderson
segments.text: -ᎠᏎᏅ ... ᎠᏗᏗᏍᎪ real early, ᏒᎾᎴᎢ ᏱᎩ ᎦᏚ ᏕᎪᏢᏍᎪ ᏍᎩᎾ, Ꮎ bucket-Ꭲ Ꮎ ᎥᎾ ᏕᎦᏢᏍᎪ ᎦᏚ ᏓᏫᏗᏍᎪ ᏦᎩᎩᏍᏗ ... ᎤᏙᏓᏩᏓ ᎮᎾ ᏥᏬᏤᏙᎰ
segments.transliteration: -asenv ... adidisgo real early, svnalei yigi gadu degotlvsgo sgina, na bucket-i na vna degatlvsgo gadu dawidisgo tsogigisdi ... udodawada hena tsiwotsedoho
segments.translation: She got up real early in the morning and made biscuits. She would put those biscuits in a bucket to take for us to eat. Cause we were there all day.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: You guys were there all day?

segments.speaker: emma-falling
segments.translation: Yeah, all day.

segments.speaker: lucy-anderson
segments.translation: It was funny…

segments.speaker: emma-falling
segments.translation: We were bathing and washing our hair.

segments.speaker: lucy-anderson
segments.text: ᏙᏳᏛ, ... Ꮎ ᎩᏟ ᏳᎾᏕᎳᎰᏍᎬ Ꮎ ᏥᏍᏛᎾ ᏚᏯᎴᎬ Ꮎ ᏗᎦᏘᏍᏗ Ꮎ elm Tree ᏂᏚᏮᏂ,Ꮩ Ꮎ limbs-Ꭲ y’know to make... ᏗᎬᏅᎯᏗ ᏍᏊ ᏚᏩᏲ ᎥᎾ ᏂᏚᏮᏂ,Ꮩ ᎾᏅ, ᏍᏊ bucket ᎥᎾ -ᏭᎦᏙ ... ᏃᏊᏛ ᎾᏅ ᏳᏍᏗ ᏧᏓᎴ ᏳᏍᏗ ... how do you say it?
segments.transliteration: doyudv, ... na gitli yunadelahosgv na tsisdvna duyalegv na digatisdi na elm Tree niduwvni,do na limbs-i y’know to make... digvnvhidi squu duwayo vna niduwvni,do nanv, squu bucket vna -wugado ... noquudv nanv yusdi tsudale yusdi ... how do you say it?
segments.translation: When the dogs found out that Grandma was going to look for crawdads, she had those gigs on the elm tree, on the limbs. She had real long ones. That’s where she had them. And she had a bucket hanging there… Then she'd have different kinds of… How do you say it?

segments.speaker: emma-falling
segments.translation: What?

segments.speaker: lucy-anderson
segments.translation: She put her hat on?

segments.speaker: emma-falling
segments.translation: Oh her cap.

segments.speaker: lucy-anderson
segments.text: ᎤᎵ,ᏍᏚᎶ ᏳᎵ,ᏍᏚᎳᎾ,Ꮓ ᎠᎾ,ᏕᎳᎰᏍᎪ ᎠᎹᏱ ᎣᏤᎬ ᎠᎾᏕᏲᎰᏙ ᎠᎦ,ᏖᏃ ... ᎠᏂᏬᏂᏍᎪ ᏳᏪᎵᏍᏗ ... Oooh! ᎤᏟ ᎤᏂᏤᎸᏐᏃ ᏲᎨᎾ ‘ᏑᏗ ᏕᎨᏠᎰ ᎩᏟ ᎦᏚ
segments.transliteration: uli,sdulo yuli,sdulana,no ana,delahosgo amayi otsegv anadeyohodo aga,teno ... aniwonisgo yuwelisdi ... Oooh! utli unitselvsono yogena ‘sudi degetloho gitli gadu
segments.translation: …put her cap on. The dogs realized we were going to the creek. They would go around in circles. Like they were talking. Oooh! They were really happy we were going to the creek. She also fed them biscuits.

segments.speaker: emma-falling
segments.text: ᏃᏊ ᏲᎦᏂᎩᏌ Ꮎ Roy ᎤᏚᏓ, ᎦᏁᎸ ᎥᎾ ... ᎢᎾ ᏬᏥᎶᏍᎪ ᎨᏓᎵ ᎮᎾ, ᎤᏍᏓᎦᎸ ᎮᎾ ᎤᏬᏚᏨ ᏧᏍᏓᎦᎸ ᎠᎹ ᎦᏅᎪᎬ ᎤᏬᏚᏨ ᎾᏅ, ᎠᏥᎳ, ᎡᎯ, ᏂᎬ ᎤᏬᏚᎯ, ᏥᏄᏍᏙ
segments.transliteration: noquu yoganigisa na Roy ududa, ganelv vna ... ina wotsilosgo gedali hena, usdagalv hena uwodutsv tsusdagalv ama ganvgogv uwodutsv nanv, atsila, ehi, nigv uwoduhi, tsinusdo
segments.translation: When we left, Roy’s grandpa lived there, and we went down the hollow, because there was a pond. It was a pretty pond. There was a spring there and there was watercress there. It is pretty.

segments.speaker: lucy-anderson
segments.text: ᎤᏬᏚᏨ ᏥᏄᏍᏛ ... ᎯᎢ ᏗᏢ ᎤᏟ ᏗᏢ ᎥᎾ ᎠᎹ ᏫᎦᎶᏍᎬ ᏗᏢ ... Ꮎ “slough” ᏣᎾ,Ꮧ Ꮭ ᏯᏩᏅ,Ꮤ
segments.transliteration: uwodutsv tsinusdv ... hii ditlv utli ditlv vna ama wigalosgv ditlv ... na “slough” tsana,di tla yawanv,ta
segments.translation: It was pretty. If the water isn’t running, they call it a “slough.”

segments.speaker: emma-falling
segments.translation: Like a pond.

segments.speaker: lucy-anderson
segments.text: ᎥᏓᎵ ᏳᏍᏗ ... ᎤᏔᎾ, ... ᎠᏣᏗ ᏣᏂᏯᎥ ᎠᏎᏅ Ꮭ ᏱᏗᎨᎯᏂᏱ ... ᏣᏅ,Ꮤ Ꮸ! Ꮭ ᏯᏩᏅ,Ꮤ ᎭᎳᏛ ᏳᏩᎦ,Ꮣ --ᎣᎦᏁᎵ,ᏔᏅ ᏦᏥᏂᏱ,Ꮧ Ꮎ ᎠᏣᏗ
segments.transliteration: vdali yusdi ... utana, ... atsadi tsaniyav asenv tla yidigehiniyi ... tsanv,ta tsv! tla yawanv,ta haladv yuwaga,da --oganeli,tanv tsotsiniyi,di na atsadi
segments.translation: Like a pond. And there were a lot of big fish in there, but you could not catch them. I don’t know how many times we tried to catch them.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: They were wild, weren’t they?

segments.speaker: lucy-anderson
segments.translation: They're wild, yeah, really! [unclear] Yeah, they’re still in there.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Really still?

segments.speaker: emma-falling
segments.text: Yeah. ᎥᎾ ᏬᏥᎶᏍᎪ ᏬᏥᏍᎬᏓᏃ ᎠᎹ-- ᏔᎵ ᎮᎾ Ꮎ “slough” ᏥᎪᏎᎠ, ... ᎠᎬᏱ ᎥᎾ ᏦᎩᏐᏍᏗ ᎨᎰ ᏙᏳ Ꮸ,ᏛᎩ ᏥᎨᎰ ... ᏭᏟ ᏗᏢᏃ ᏥᏍᏛᎾ ᎤᏪᏴ ᎥᎾ ᏙᎩᏩᏍᏗ ᏥᏍᏛᎾ ᏙᎩᏲᎰ ᎠᏣᏗᏅ
segments.transliteration: Yeah. vna wotsilosgo wotsisgvdano ama-- tali hena na “slough” tsigosea, ... agvyi vna tsogisosdi geho doyu tsv,dvgi tsigeho ... wutli ditlvno tsisdvna uweyv vna dogiwasdi tsisdvna dogiyoho atsadinv
segments.translation: We go there, and we cross the water where she calls the slough first. And the water was deep and on down there was that crawdad creek where we looked for them and fish.

segments.speaker: lucy-anderson
segments.text: ᎾᏛ Ꮎ ᏣᏅ,ᏗᎲ “seine” ᏣᎾ,ᏗᎰ Ꮎ ᏗᎬᏅᎯᏓ, ᎯᎢ ᏗᏢ ᏗᏂᏠᏍᎪ ... ᏗᏁᏙᎰ Ꮎ ᏧᎾ,ᏔᎾ, ... “ᎠᎢ ᏗᏂᏲᏟ ᎯᎢ ᏗᏢ ᏫᏥᎶᎭ, ... ᎥᎾ ᏫᏣᏚᎲᎦ ᎡᏍᎦ ᏗᏣᎢ--ᏗᏣᎢᏎᏍᏗ,” ᎣᎪᎮᎰ Ꮎ ᎠᏣᏗ ᏓᏂᏂᏱᏍᎬ Ooh! ᎾᏛ ᏥᏍᏛᎾ ᎯᎢᏛ ᏓᏂᏁᏆ ᎯᎢᏛ Ꮣ--blue! They’re blue! Ꮟ ᎠᏂᏯ!
segments.transliteration: nadv na tsanv,dihv “seine” tsana,diho na digvnvhida, hii ditlv dinitlosgo ... dinedoho na tsuna,tana, ... “ai diniyotli hii ditlv witsiloha, ... vna witsaduhvga esga ditsai--ditsaisesdi,” ogoheho na atsadi daniniyisgv Ooh! nadv tsisdvna hiidv daninequa hiidv da--blue! They’re blue! si aniya!
segments.translation: They were using that, seine they call it, and it was real long. The grown-ups were on the one side. They would tell us kids, “Walk from the other side, toward older ones” that were dragging the seine. They were catching fish and also big crawdads. They said they were so big they looked blue. They’re still in there.

segments.speaker: emma-falling
segments.text: ᎠᏂᎬᎿᎨ ᎠᏂᏌᎪᏂᎨ ᏥᏍᏛᎾ ᏥᎨᎲ ᎥᎾᏛ ᎢᎦ ᎠᏁᎯ, ᎣᎦᏅ,Ꮫ ... ᎠᏎᏃ Ꮭ ᎪᎯᏥᎩ Ꮭ ᏱᎬᎯᏴᎯ, ᎠᏂᏲᏁᎦ...
segments.transliteration: anigvhnage anisagonige tsisdvna tsigehv vnadv iga anehi, oganv,dv ... aseno tla gohitsigi tla yigvhiyvhi, aniyonega...
segments.translation: They were black ones and blue ones. That’s the only place we knew they were. But you can’t go in there today, the white people…

segments.speaker: lucy-anderson
segments.translation: …they closed it up.

segments.speaker: emma-falling
segments.translation: Yeah, they closed it.

segments.speaker: mitch-holcomb
segments.text: ᎾᏅ “slough” ᏣᏗᏍᎬ ... ᏝᎨ ᎠᎹ ᎠᏨᎾ,Ꭸ ᎠᎾ,ᏗᏍᎪ ᏍᎩᎾᎾ?
segments.transliteration: nanv “slough” tsadisgv ... tlage ama atsvna,ge ana,disgo sginana?
segments.translation: That slough you said, don’t they call it “ama atsvna – (backwater)”?

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: That’s what I was thinking they say…

segments.speaker: lucy-anderson
segments.text: ᎠᎹ ᎠᏨᎾ like it’s backed up?
segments.transliteration: ama atsvna like it’s backed up?
segments.translation: Ama atsvna like it’s backed up?

segments.speaker: emma-falling
segments.translation: Oh, OK.

segments.speaker: mitch-holcomb
segments.translation: Backwater.

segments.speaker: lucy-anderson
segments.translation: Oh, backwater.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Yeah, ama atsvna.

segments.speaker: emma-falling
segments.text: Oh! Ꮟ --ᎾᏮᎨᏫᏒᎾ Sycamore ‘Ꮩ ᎠᏓ ᎠᏣᎳᎩ ᎬᏗ,?
segments.transliteration: Oh! si --nawvgewisvna Sycamore ‘do ada atsalagi gvdi,?
segments.translation: Oh, before I forget, how do you say Sycamore in Cherokee?

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Sycamore, what is that?

segments.speaker: lucy-anderson
segments.translation: We can’t find it…

segments.speaker: emma-falling
segments.text: ...ᎠᎭᏂ ᎪᏪᎸ ᎮᎾ, ᎠᎭᏂ Durbin ᏗᎩᏅᏁᎸ ᎪᏪᎵ,
segments.transliteration: ...ahani gowelv hena, ahani Durbin diginvnelv goweli,
segments.translation: …it is written in the books that Durbin gave us…

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: I forget it.

segments.speaker: emma-falling
segments.text: ᎠᎩᏄᎸᎲᏍᎬ ᎣᏍᏓ ᏱᎦᏪᏍᏗ,--ᏲᎩᏂᏪᏍᏗ, ... Can you guys read it?
segments.transliteration: aginulvhvsgv osda yigawesdi,--yoginiwesdi, ... Can you guys read it?
segments.translation: …but we can’t pronounce it. Can you guys read it?

segments.speaker: mitch-holcomb
segments.translation: Kotsunega…

segments.speaker: emma-falling
segments.text: Let me go to this other one.
segments.transliteration: Let me go to this other one.
segments.translation: Let me go to this other one.

segments.speaker: mitch-holcomb
segments.translation: Kowatsunega.

segments.speaker: emma-falling
segments.text: *You see, to me, that sounds like Mulberry.*
segments.transliteration: *You see, to me, that sounds like Mulberry.*
segments.translation: You see, to me, that sounds like mulberry.

segments.speaker: mitch-holcomb
segments.translation: Oh, it is mulberry!

segments.speaker: emma-falling
segments.text: *Yeah, to me, that’s mulberry I’ll get it—I’ll get it. Uh oh, I lost my marker.*
segments.transliteration: *Yeah, to me, that’s mulberry I’ll get it—I’ll get it. Uh oh, I lost my marker.*
segments.translation: Yeah, to me, that’s mulberry. I’ll get it—I’ll get it. Here. Uh oh, I lost my marker.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: ᎥᏍᎩᏛ Ꭷ ᎠᏣᎳᎩ ᏚᏙᎥ ᏣᏗᏍᎬ ᎢᎸᏍᎩ ᏳᏩᎦ,Ꮣ ᏍᏊ ᎠᎩᎪᎵᏰᎥ ᎪᏪᎸ ᏣᎳᎩ
segments.transliteration: vsgidv ka atsalagi dudov tsadisgv ilvsgi yuwaga,da squu agigoliyev gowelv tsalagi
segments.translation: Yeah, that is mulberry. I have read it a lot of times in Cherokee.

segments.speaker: emma-falling
segments.text: ᎪᏧ...ᎤᏪᏅᎦ No... ᎤᏁᎦ ... Ꮎ “bark” ᎤᏁᎦ ᎮᎾ,
segments.transliteration: gotsu...uwenvga No... unega ... na “bark” unega hena,
segments.translation: Kotsu…uu….uwenvga. No. Unega. The bark is white.

segments.speaker: lucy-anderson
segments.text: ᎠᏎᏅ, Ꮭ ᎢᎸᎯᏳ ᏱᏦᎩᎸᏫᏍᏓᏁᎸ Ꮎ uh...
segments.transliteration: asenv, tla ilvhiyu yitsogilvwisdanelv na uh...
segments.translation: We never work on it…

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: Boy! ᎠᏮᎨᏫ,Ꮞ ᎩᎳ ᏍᏊ ᎠᏭ ᏣᎩᎪᎵᏰᎥ ᎠᏣᎳᎩ
segments.transliteration: Boy! awvgewi,se gila squu awu tsagigoliyev atsalagi
segments.translation: Boy! I forgot, maybe if I read it somewhere..

segments.speaker: emma-falling
segments.text: ᏏᏊ ᎾᏛᏅ ᎠᎭᏂ ᏍᏊ ᎠᏩᏠ,Ꭼ ... David ᏓᏥᏯᏛᏛᏂ, ᎨᎵᎲ Sycamore
segments.transliteration: siquu nadvnv ahani squu awatlo,gv ... David datsiyadvdvni, gelihv Sycamore
segments.translation: That’s what it says here, too. I think I’m going to ask David…Sycamore...

segments.speaker: mitch-holcomb
segments.translation: He knows it.

segments.speaker: emma-falling
segments.text: *There’s 2 or 3 other things in this book that’s...not quite right to me. The other one is elm tree, I couldn’t remember elm tree*
segments.transliteration: *There’s 2 or 3 other things in this book that’s...not quite right to me. The other one is elm tree, I couldn’t remember elm tree*
segments.translation: There’s two or three other things in this book that’s…not quite right to me. The other one is elm tree – I couldn’t remember the elm tree.

segments.speaker: lucy-anderson
segments.translation: This right here…

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: ᎢᎸᏍᎩ ᏄᏒ ᎩᎶ ᏧᏪᏙᎸ elm Tree ᏚᏙᎥ ᏣᎳᎩ
segments.transliteration: ilvsgi nusv gilo tsuwedolv elm Tree dudov tsalagi
segments.translation: Somebody came, and their name was Elm Tree.

segments.speaker: mitch-holcomb
segments.translation: Dawatsil(v).

segments.speaker: emma-falling
segments.translation: Dawatsil(v)!

segments.speaker: lucy-anderson
segments.translation: That’s it!

segments.speaker: emma-falling
segments.translation: We almost had it!

segments.speaker: lucy-anderson
segments.text: ᏓᏩᏥᎸ ... ᏍᎩᎾ ᏓᏩᏥᎸ ᏥᏕᏡᎬ ᏗᏓᏁᎸ Grandma Grandpa-Ꭲ ᎡᏚᏓ, ᎡᎵᏏ ᏧᎾ,ᏕᏅ --ᎠᏭ,Ꮻ ᏥᏕᏡᎬ ᎥᎾ ᏥᎩ ... ᎤᎾ ᏥᏚ...I don’t know how you say it ‘his bed’?
segments.transliteration: dawatsilv ... sgina dawatsilv tsidetlugv didanelv Grandma Grandpa-i eduda, elisi tsuna,denv --awu,wi tsidetlugv vna tsigi ... una tsidu...I don’t know how you say it ‘his bed’?
segments.translation: Dawatsil(v). Yeah, there were elm trees where Grandma and Grandpa’s used to live. There, trees right by the house…right by…how do you say, ‘his bed’?

segments.speaker: emma-falling
segments.translation: Grandpa’s bed? Doyi Tsunitlv.

segments.speaker: lucy-anderson
segments.translation: They had beds outside.

segments.speaker: emma-falling
segments.translation: And that’s where we slept.

segments.speaker: lucy-anderson
segments.text: ᎾᏅ ᏳᏓᎭ ᎩᎶ ᏳᏂᎷᏨ ᎦᎵᏦᏕ... y’know other family ᏳᏂᎷᏨ ᏙᏱ ᏥᏗᎦᏅᏍᎪ Ꮎ feathered mattress Ꮎ ᎡᎵᏏ ᏥᎨᎲ ᏂᎦᏓ ᏦᏥᏅᏁ ᏙᏱ ᏗᏢ ᏑᎾᎴ ᏱᏄᎵ,ᏍᏔᎾᏃ Ꮎ ... dew! ᎤᎯᏌᏔ we was wet! (ᎤᏰᏥᏍᎦ) ᏙᏳ ᎤᏬᎵ,Ꮧ ᏙᎦ--ᏙᎦᏛᏒᎢ
segments.transliteration: nanv yudaha gilo yunilutsv galitsode... y’know other family yunilutsv doyi tsidiganvsgo na feathered mattress na elisi tsigehv nigada tsotsinvne doyi ditlv sunale yinuli,stanano na ... dew! uhisata we was wet! (uyetsisga) doyu uwoli,di doga--dogadvsvi
segments.translation: And when somebody came to visit somebody like other family, Grandma would put the feathered mattress outside and that’s where we all were. When it was morning the…uh…dew, uhisatv was on us. We grew up being real silly.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: ᏙᏳ,Ꮫ ᎠᏯ ᏍᏊ ᏍᎩᎾ ᏱᏃᏣᏛᏅ ᏥᎨᎲ ᎠᎬᏱ ᏙᏱ ᏗᏢ
segments.transliteration: doyu,dv aya squu sgina yinotsadvnv tsigehv agvyi doyi ditlv
segments.translation: That’s what we used to do, too. We would sleep outside.

segments.speaker: lucy-anderson
segments.translation: Grandpa always had his bed outside.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Nowadays it’s too dangerous.

segments.speaker: lucy-anderson
segments.translation: Yeah, that’s right.

segments.speaker: emma-falling
segments.translation: It’s really dangerous.

segments.speaker: lucy-anderson
segments.text: ᏱᏣᏰᏣ ᎢᎾᏓ ᎠᏭ ᏯᏯ ᎩᎶ ᏱᎦᏙᎦ
segments.transliteration: yitsayetsa inada awu yaya gilo yigadoga
segments.translation: When you wake up, a snake might be in there or somebody standing by your bed.

segments.speaker: emma-falling
segments.text: ᎾᎮᎾ ᏣᏅ,ᏔᏍ Ꮎ Boy Scouts ᏥᎩ ᎦᎶᏇᏗ? ᎥᎾ ᎮᎾ ᎦᏅᏅ ᎥᎾ ᎮᎾ ᎦᏅᏅ ᏫᎦᎶᎯᏍᏗ Boy Scouts ᎢᎾ ... -ᎤᎦᎾᏩ ᏗᏢ ᏫᎦᎶᎯᏍᏗ, ᎡᎵᏏ ᎡᏚᏓ,Ꮕ ᏧᏁᏅᏒ ... ᎾᏅ ᎠᎬᏱ ᎡᎯ, ᎡᏠᎩ Roy ᏚᏙᎥ ᎤᏴᏢ ᏗᏢ ᎦᏁᎳ ᏍᎩᎾ ... ᏍᎩ ᎠᏩᏛᎯᏍᏔᏅ ᎾᏅ ᎣᎩᏂᏥ ᏍᏊ ‘ᎧᎸᎬ ᏗᏢ ᎦᏁᎸ ᏑᏟᎶᏓᏭ ᏂᎨᏒᎾ ᏄᎾᏓᏅ...
segments.transliteration: nahena tsanv,tas na Boy Scouts tsigi galoquedi? vna hena ganvnv vna hena ganvnv wigalohisdi Boy Scouts ina ... -uganawa ditlv wigalohisdi, elisi eduda,nv tsunenvsv ... nanv agvyi ehi, etlogi Roy dudov uyvtlv ditlv ganela sgina ... sgi awadvhistanv nanv oginitsi squu ‘kalvgv ditlv ganelv sutlilodawu nigesvna nunadanv...
segments.translation: Do you know where the Boy Scouts is in Locust Grove? That’s where you go past, going south, and that’s where Grandma and Grandpa’s house was. My aunt, the first born, her name was Roy. She lived north of there. She’s the one that raised me. And our mom, she lived just about a mile away toward the east.

segments.speaker: lucy-anderson
segments.text: ᎤᏒᎯ ᏬᏍᏗᎶᏍᎪ ᎤᏒᎯ ooh! ᏥᎦᎾ,ᏰᎪ ᎠᏎᏅ ᏥᏬᏍᏓᎢᏐ ᏗᏓᏁᎳ ᎣᏍᏕᎪ ᏃᏊᎴ
segments.transliteration: usvhi wosdilosgo usvhi ooh! tsigana,yego asenv tsiwosdaiso didanela osdego noquule
segments.translation: We would walk that at night and it’d be real dark and scary. We just kept walking toward the house.

segments.speaker: emma-falling
segments.text: ᎮᏍᏗᏅ ᏙᏆᎴᎳ ᏱᏚᏂᎮ ᎰᏩ ᏌᏊ... Ꮎ Roy ᎤᏚᏚ ᎤᏩᏌ ᏙᏆᎴᎳ ᏧᎲ Spartan-Ꭲ ᎮᎾ ᏧᎸᏫ,ᏍᏓᏁᎮ ᎥᎾ ᏛᎵ,Ꮟ ᎾᏅ ᎠᏩᏛᎯᏍᏔᏅ ᎠᏂᏁᎳ ᏍᏊ ᎥᎾ ᏚᎸᏫ,ᏍᏓᏁᎲ ᏍᏊ ... ᏍᏊ ᏙᏆᎴᎳ ᎤᎲ ᏃᏊᏅ ᎣᎩᏂᏥ ᎡᎳᏗ ᏲᏣᎢ ᎪᏢ ᏲᎨᎾ ᎥᎾ ᏥᏳᎪ,ᏗᏭ ᏌᎷᏱ ᏙᎩᏅᏅ ᎣᎩᎶᎯᏍᏗ ᎥᎾᏛ ... ᏂᎪᎯᎸ ᎥᎾᏭ ᎢᎸᏍᎩ ᏳᏒ ᏔᎵ, ᎢᏳᎾᏙᏓᏩᏍᏗ ᏳᏓᎵᎭ, ᏬᏤᏙᎰ ᎡᎵᏏ...
segments.transliteration: hesdinv doqualela yidunihe howa saquu... na Roy ududu uwasa doqualela tsuhv Spartan-i hena tsulvwi,sdanehe vna dvli,si nanv awadvhistanv aninela squu vna dulvwi,sdanehv squu ... squu doqualela uhv noquunv oginitsi eladi yotsai gotlv yogena vna tsiyugo,diwu saluyi doginvnv ogilohisdi vnadv ... nigohilv vnawu ilvsgi yusv tali, iyunadodawasdi yudaliha, wotsedoho elisi...
segments.translation: They didn’t always have a car. Roy’s grandpa had one because he worked at Spartan at Tulsa. And the one that raised me, her husband, that’s where he worked, too, and he also had a wagon. And our mom, we were always walking when we went somewhere. We had a road that went right through the woods. Every two weeks, we went to Grandma’s.

segments.speaker: lucy-anderson
segments.text: ...ᎣᏣᎢᏐ ᏂᎦᏓ ᎪᎱᏍᏓ ᎣᏥᏰᎰ Mama would say, “ᎯᎢᏛ ᎯᏫᏓ!” ᏣᏓ “ᎠᏯ Ꮎ ᎤᏍᏗ ᏫᏓᏥᏯᏁᏌ,” ᎣᏣᎢᏐ ᏂᎦᏓ ᎪᎱᏍᏗ ᎣᏥᏰᎰ ... ᎣᏥᏰᎰᎪ ᎣᏣᎢᏐ
segments.transliteration: ...otsaiso nigada gohusda otsiyeho Mama would say, “hiidv hiwida!” tsada “aya na usdi widatsiyanesa,” otsaiso nigada gohusdi otsiyeho ... otsiyehogo otsaiso
segments.translation: We would all be carrying something as we walked. Mama would say, “Take this. I’ll be carrying the baby.” But all of us would be carrying something, walking along.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: You all would be walking in a line?

segments.speaker: lucy-anderson
segments.translation: Yeah, we’d be in a line.

segments.speaker: emma-falling
segments.text: ᏃᏊᎴ ᏗᎦᏚᎲ ᎤᏪᏅᏍᏗ ᏱᏄᎵ,ᏍᏔᏅ ᎡᏥ Ꮎ Mail Carrier
segments.transliteration: noquule digaduhv uwenvsdi yinuli,stanv etsi na Mail Carrier
segments.translation: And when Mom went to town she caught a ride with the mail carrier.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Yeah, that’s what some people did.

segments.speaker: emma-falling
segments.translation: ᏩᏓᏣᏁᎰ yeah

segments.speaker: lucy-anderson
segments.translation: ᏩᏓᏣᏁᎰ yeah

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: That's what my mom did.

segments.speaker: emma-falling
segments.text: ᎥᎥ ᏙᏳ,Ꮫ ᏍᎩ ᎾᎾᏛᏁᎲ ... ᏍᏓᏱ ᎣᎩᎶᏒ ᎠᏎᏃ Ꮭ ᎪᏍᏓ ᏲᎦᏅ,Ꮦ ᏓᏤᏢ ... Ꮭ ᎪᏍᏓ ᏲᎦᏅ,Ꮦ ... ᏃᏊᎴ ᏒᎩ ... ᏒᎩ ᎢᎾᎨ ᏥᏈᏍᏗ...
segments.transliteration: vv doyu,dv sgi nanadvnehv ... sdayi ogilosv aseno tla gosda yoganv,te datsetlv ... tla gosda yoganv,te ... noquule svgi ... svgi inage tsiquisdi...
segments.translation: Yeah, that’s what they did. We went through hard times and were poor, but we didn’t realize that then. There was wild onion by the house…

segments.speaker: lucy-anderson
segments.text: Oooh! ᏥᏈᏍᏙᏒ ᏗᏓᏁᎸ ᎾᎥ ... ᎣᏍᏓ ᏃᎬᏁᎸ MamaᏛ ᏥᎨᎲ ᎡᏥ ᏥᎨᎲ ᏥᎦᎾ,ᏕᎬ ᏍᎩᎾ ᏙᎲ ᏒᎩ
segments.transliteration: Oooh! tsiquisdosv didanelv nav ... osda nogvnelv Mamadv tsigehv etsi tsigehv tsigana,degv sgina dohv svgi
segments.translation: There was a lot of it by the house. We picked a lot it and fixed it. Mom would sell it, the wild onion.

segments.speaker: emma-falling
segments.text: ᏳᏓᎭ ᏦᏍᎪᎯᏥᏊ ᎠᏕᎳ ᏧᎬᏩᎵᏛ ᏥᎦᎾᏕᎬ ᏛᎵᏏ ᏒᎩ
segments.transliteration: yudaha tsosgohitsiquu adela tsugvwalidv tsiganadegv dvlisi svgi
segments.translation: Sometimes she would sell it and make $300 in Tulsa.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: They really bought it.

segments.speaker: emma-falling
segments.text: ᎾᏅ ᏍᎩᎾ ᎠᎯ ᎠᏓ y’know what that is? ᎠᎯ ᎠᏓ ... ᏂᎯᎾ Ꮭ ᏱᏣᏅ,Ꮤ ᏳᏍᏗ ᎨᎲ? ᎠᎯ ᎠᏓ it’s like a vine. ᎠᏤ ᎢᏳᏍᏗ ᎦᎵᏙᎰ ... ᎣᏍᏓ ᎠᎩᏍᏗ Ꭺ.ᎯᏥᎩ Ꮭ ᎢᎸᏢ ᏲᎩᎪᎰ ... Durbin’Ꭱ ᏍᏊ ᏧᏅ,Ꮫ ᏍᎩ ᏳᏍᏗ ᎠᎯ ᎠᏓ ᏚᏙᎠ,
segments.transliteration: nanv sgina ahi ada y’know what that is? ahi ada ... nihina tla yitsanv,ta yusdi gehv? ahi ada it’s like a vine. atse iyusdi galidoho ... osda agisdi go.hitsigi tla ilvtlv yogigoho ... Durbin’e squu tsunv,dv sgi yusdi ahi ada dudoa,
segments.translation: And that ahiade, do you know what that is? What about you, you don’t know what that is? Ahiad. It’s like a vine. It’s green and climbs the tree. And it’s good to eat. Nowadays, you don’t see it. Durbin knew about it, too. Ahiad is its name.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Ahiad.

segments.speaker: emma-falling
segments.translation: Ahiad.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: And in English, do you know?

segments.speaker: emma-falling
segments.text: Ꮭ ᏯᏩᏅ,Ꮤ, ᏲᏁᎦ ᎬᏗ, Ꮭ ᏲᎩᎾᏅ,Ꮤ, Durbin ᎣᎩᏂᏃᎮᏢ ᏥᎨᎲ
segments.transliteration: tla yawanv,ta, yonega gvdi, tla yoginanv,ta, Durbin ogininohetlv tsigehv
segments.translation: I don’t know how to say it in English. Durbin and I talked about it, too.

segments.speaker: lucy-anderson
segments.text: ᎪᏧᏁᎦ ᏍᏊ ᏍᏓᏅ,Ꮤ ᎣᏥᎩᏍᏗ ᏥᎨᎲ ... ᎠᏎᏅ ‘Ꮲ Arkansas ᏗᏢ ᏥᏩᎩᏍᎬ ᏙᎲ?
segments.transliteration: gotsunega squu sdanv,ta otsigisdi tsigehv ... asenv ‘tlv Arkansas ditlv tsiwagisgv dohv?
segments.translation: We also ate Kotsunega. He used to go get it in Arkansas.

segments.speaker: emma-falling
segments.translation: Toward Watts.

segments.speaker: lucy-anderson
segments.text: ᏩᏗ,Ꮟ ᏗᏢ ᏣᏲᎯᎲ ... ᏌᏊ ᏳᏩᎦ,Ꮣ ᏧᏲᏢ ᎠᎹᏳᎵ,Ꮧ ᎾᎥ ᏥᏭ--...planted it... ᎥᎾ ᏧᏛᏒ ᏍᏊ ᎪᎯᏗ ᏥᎨᎲ ᎥᎾ ᏥᏩᎩᏍᎬ ᎠᏎᏅ...
segments.transliteration: wadi,si ditlv tsayohihv ... saquu yuwaga,da tsuyotlv amayuli,di nav tsiwu--...planted it... vna tsudvsv squu gohidi tsigehv vna tsiwagisgv asenv...
segments.translation: Towards Watts. He would bring it. One time, he put it by the river. He planted it and it grew, too. It was there a long time. He would go harvest it there.

segments.speaker: lucy-anderson
segments.translation: But then there was a flood.

segments.speaker: emma-falling
segments.translation: But then there was a flood.

segments.speaker: lucy-anderson
segments.translation: …everything.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: It all floated away.

segments.speaker: lucy-anderson
segments.translation: It floated away.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: I remember that Kotsunega. My grandma used to go get it nearby.

segments.speaker: emma-falling
segments.translation: Yeah, kotsunega.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: My late grandmother would pick just right there.

segments.speaker: emma-falling
segments.text: ᏙᏳ,Ꮫ ᎣᏍᏓ ᎠᎩᏍᏗ Ꮟ ᎠᏩᏛᏗᏪ Ꮎ Chris and Durbin ᏣᏂᏩᏘᏍᎬ ᏳᏓᎭ
segments.transliteration: doyu,dv osda agisdi si awadvdiwe na Chris and Durbin tsaniwatisgv yudaha
segments.translation: It’s good to eat. You can still find it. Chris and Durbin used to find it sometimes.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: ᏣᏅ,Ꮫ Ꮭ ᎩᎶ ᏱᎧᏁᎮᎰ ᏗᎨᎬ ᏗᏢ ᎠᎩᏍᎬ ᏍᎩ ᏳᏍᏗ
segments.transliteration: tsanv,dv tla gilo yikaneheho digegv ditlv agisgv sgi yusdi
segments.translation: Nobody talks about eating something like that, where I’m from.

segments.speaker: emma-falling
segments.text: ᏍᏓᏱᎢᏛ ᎠᏩᏛᏗᏃ ᎠᏂᏲᏁᎦ Ꮭ ᏳᎾ,ᏚᎵᎰ ᎠᏴᏍᏗ Ꮎ ᎦᏙᎯ, ᏚᏂᎲ
segments.transliteration: sdayiidv awadvdino aniyonega tla yuna,duliho ayvsdi na gadohi, dunihv
segments.translation: It’s hard to find it now. The white people don’t want you to go in their land.

segments.speaker: lucy-anderson
segments.translation: And also, what was it called?

segments.speaker: emma-falling
segments.translation: Ahiad … and poke salad?

segments.speaker: lucy-anderson
segments.translation: Yeah.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Is it dlayidvke?

segments.speaker: lucy-anderson
segments.text: ᏜᏱᏛ ᎥᎥ ᏍᏊ ᏧᎲ ᏙᎲ Nan?
segments.transliteration: dlayidv vv squu tsuhv dohv Nan?
segments.translation: Yeah poke salad. They also had that.

segments.speaker: emma-falling
segments.text: ᎾᏅ ᏂᎪᎯᎸ ᏦᎩᏲᎲ ᏌᎷᏱ ᎪᏍᏓ ᎠᎩᏍᏗ ... ᏂᎯᏍᏊᏛ ... ᏂᎯᏍᏊ ᏣᏛᏁᎸ ᎠᏎ
segments.transliteration: nanv nigohilv tsogiyohv saluyi gosda agisdi ... nihisquudv ... nihisquu tsadvnelv ase
segments.translation: We would always be looking for food in the woods. I guess y’all did that, too.

segments.speaker: lucy-anderson
segments.text: What about that? ... What about that? Ꮎ ᎢᏡᎬ ᏥᎦ,ᏕᏍᎬ...
segments.transliteration: What about that? ... What about that? na itlugv tsiga,desgv...
segments.translation: What about that…tree.

segments.speaker: emma-falling
segments.translation: Oak balls.

segments.speaker: lucy-anderson
segments.text: L: No, no, no. Ꮎ Grape ᏥᎪᏢᏍᎪ
segments.transliteration: L: No, no, no. na Grape tsigotlvsgo
segments.translation: No, no, no…grapes it makes.

segments.speaker: emma-falling
segments.translation: Oh, possum grapes.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Possum grapes.

segments.speaker: lucy-anderson
segments.translation: What are they called?

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: What do they call those?

segments.speaker: emma-falling
segments.translation: Possum grape?

segments.speaker: lucy-anderson
segments.text: ᏍᎩᏭ ᏂᎦ ... Ꮎ Nan ᏥᎨᎲ ᎤᏛᎯᏍᏔᏅ ᎯᎢ ᏍᎩᎾ ᏗᎾ,ᏓᎸ Mama ᏥᎨᎲ ... ᏍᎩᎾ ᎤᏔᎾ ᏥᏡ,Ꭼ Ꮷ--ᏧᎴᏴᏍᏔᏅ ᏍᎩᎾ grapes—possum grapes ᏂᎦᏓ Ꮷ--
segments.transliteration: sgiwu niga ... na Nan tsigehv udvhistanv hii sgina dina,dalv Mama tsigehv ... sgina utana tsitlu,gv tsu--tsuleyvstanv sgina grapes—possum grapes nigada tsu--
segments.translation: That’s it…Nan, who’s passed, she’s the one that raised this One (Emma). That was Mama’s sister. There was a big tree, and she cut it down, the possum grapes. All of them…

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: They all fell off.

segments.speaker: lucy-anderson
segments.translation: They fell off…

segments.speaker: emma-falling
segments.text: ᎠᏎᏅ Ꮟ ᎣᎩᏁᎰ ᎣᎦᏗᏔᏍᏗ, ᎪᎳ ᏱᏄᎵ,ᏍᏔᏅ
segments.transliteration: asenv si ogineho ogaditasdi, gola yinuli,stanv
segments.translation: But we still had it to drink at wintertime.

segments.speaker: lucy-anderson
segments.text: ᏥᏈᏍᏗ ᏧᏂᏁᎰ ᎥᎾ ᎦᎵᏦᏕ ᏥᎦᏁᎸ ᎭᏫᏂ ᏗᏢ ᏧᏃᏢ cellar ᎢᏳᏍᏗ ᎤᏴᏜ ᏥᎨᎲ ᏂᎪᎯᎸ ᎤᎦᎾᏩ ᎴᏱᎦ ... ᎤᎾ ᏧᏓ--ᏧᏓᎲᏍᎬ ᏍᎩᎾᎾ Ꮎ grapes.
segments.transliteration: tsiquisdi tsunineho vna galitsode tsiganelv hawini ditlv tsunotlv cellar iyusdi uyvdla tsigehv nigohilv uganawa leyiga ... una tsuda--tsudahvsgv sginana na grapes.
segments.translation: They a lot of it under the house in a cellar and it was cool or warm in there. That’s where she kept the possum grapes.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Possum grapes.

segments.speaker: lucy-anderson
segments.text: Possum grapes. Dumplings ᏥᏕᎪᏢᏍᎪ ᎪᎳ ᏳᏓᎭ
segments.transliteration: Possum grapes. Dumplings tsidegotlvsgo gola yudaha
segments.translation: Possum grapes. She made dumplings in the wintertime.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: They were the best, weren’t they?

segments.speaker: emma-falling
segments.text: ᏳᏓᎭ ᎪᎯᏓ ᎪᎪᏢᏅ ᏃᏊᎴ ᏍᏊ ᎧᏄᎦᏟ ᏍᏊ ᏥᏈᏍᏙᏒ ᏥᏙᏣᏕᏍᎪ ᎫᏩᏯᏅ ᎠᏎᏅ ᎫᏩᏯ ᎥᎾ ᏧᏪᏅᏒ ᎥᎾ ᎦᏓ ᏙᎩᏂᎭ, ᎤᎪᏗ ᏙᎩᎭ, ᎦᏗᏅ Ꮟ ... ᎠᏯ Ꮭ ᏱᏥᏁᎳ ᎥᎾ ᎠᏯ ᎨᎰ ... ᎫᏩᏯ ᏥᏈᏍᏗ ᎡᎯ, ᎠᏎᏅᎿ ᏧᏂᎦ,ᏔᏥᏍᏓᏟ, ᏥᏈᏍᏗ ᎠᏁᎯ,
segments.transliteration: yudaha gohida gogotlvnv noquule squu kanugatli squu tsiquisdosv tsidotsadesgo guwayanv asenv guwaya vna tsuwenvsv vna gada doginiha, ugodi dogiha, gadinv si ... aya tla yitsinela vna aya geho ... guwaya tsiquisdi ehi, asenvhna tsuniga,tatsisdatli, tsiquisdi anehi,
segments.translation: Yeah, we haven’t made them in a while. Also, we picked blackberries and huckleberries. Huckleberries right by where she lives. We still have land, but I don’t live there. There are a lot of huckleberry trees, but there are a lot of copperheads there.

segments.speaker: lucy-anderson
segments.translation: Down the hill.

segments.speaker: emma-falling
segments.translation: Down the hill.

segments.speaker: lucy-anderson
segments.text: ᎠᏎᏅ ᎠᏯ ᎣᏥᏁᎸ ᎨᎲ Ꮭ ᏍᎩ ᎢᎦ ᏅᏲᏃ ᏙᏳ, ᎤᏟᎢ ᏗᏢᏴᏃ ... ᎦᎾᏰᎩ
segments.transliteration: asenv aya otsinelv gehv tla sgi iga nvyono doyu, utlii ditlvyvno ... ganayegi
segments.translation: There are a lot of rocks there. But, where I live, there are hardly any rocks. But on down from us there are rocks and that’s where the snakes are. Dangerous.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Me too, that's dangerous.

segments.speaker: emma-falling
segments.translation: Long time ago, we hardly ever saw a snake.

segments.speaker: lucy-anderson
segments.text: ᎾᏛ ᏍᏊ ᎧᏄᎦᏟ, ᏥᏈᏍᏗ ᏥᎨᎰ ᎥᎾ ... ᏍᏊ--ᏍᏊ ᏥᏕᎦᎵ,ᏗᎰ Mama ᏥᎨᎲ ᎡᏥ ᏥᎨᎲ ᏥᏕᎦᎵ,ᏗᎰ ... ᎠᎪᎳ ᎮᎾ,Ꮓ dumplings ᏍᏊ pieᎴ ᏱᎦ ᏥᏕᎪᏢᏍᎪ
segments.transliteration: nadv squu kanugatli, tsiquisdi tsigeho vna ... squu--squu tsidegali,diho Mama tsigehv etsi tsigehv tsidegali,diho ... agola hena,no dumplings squu piele yiga tsidegotlvsgo
segments.translation: Also, where there are a lot of blackberries. Mama used to can them. In the wintertime, she would make dumplings or pies…

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Or…cobbler.

segments.speaker: lucy-anderson
segments.text: ᎾᏍᏊ ᏦᎩᎾ,ᏕᏅ ᎡᎵᏏ, ᎡᏚᏓ, --ᏧᏁᏅᏒ --ᏅᏃᎯ, ᏗᎦᎾ,ᏗᏫ,Ꮢ ᎤᏍᏗ ᎣᏍᏓ ᎤᏂᏅᎦᎸᏓ ᏥᎨᎲ ᎠᏎᏅ ᏭᏟ ᏗᏟ ᏗᏏᎳ,Ꮫ ᎾᎥ ᎤᏔᎾ, ᏥᏡ,Ꭼ Ꮎ ᏆᎾ,
segments.transliteration: nasquu tsogina,denv elisi, eduda, --tsunenvsv --nvnohi, digana,diwi,sv usdi osda uninvgalvda tsigehv asenv wutli ditli disila,dv nav utana, tsitlu,gv na quana,
segments.translation: But also, where we used to live. My grandparents’ house, across the road from there was a little clearing and there by the fence was a big tree, peach.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Oh yeah.

segments.speaker: lucy-anderson
segments.text: ᎮᏍᏗ, ᏲᎦᏅ,Ꮤ, ᎥᎾ ᏧᎶᏒ ... ᎮᏍᏗ ᏍᏊ ᏆᎾ, ‘Ꮲ ᏯᏁᎰ ᎥᎾ ᎤᏩᏌ, ... ᎮᏍᏗ ᏧᎾ,ᏔᎾ, ᏱᎨᎮ ᎯᎢᏛ Ꮟ ᏧᏂ,ᏍᏗ
segments.transliteration: hesdi, yoganv,ta, vna tsulosv ... hesdi squu quana, ‘tlv yaneho vna uwasa, ... hesdi tsuna,tana, yigehe hiidv si tsuni,sdi
segments.translation: We don’t know where it came from. Cause there were hardly any peaches there. They weren’t big,

segments.speaker: emma-falling
segments.translation: And they were white.

segments.speaker: lucy-anderson
segments.text: Ooh! Ꮫ ᏓᏃᏍᏓ, ᏥᎨᎲ ... ᏃᏊ, ᏯᏃᎲᏍᎦ Grandma ᏥᎨᎲ ᎡᎵᏏ, ᏥᎨᎲ “ᏫᏗᏧᏖᎦ, ᏗᎾ!” ᏣᏓ
segments.transliteration: Ooh! dv danosda, tsigehv ... noquu, yanohvsga Grandma tsigehv elisi, tsigehv “widitsutega, dina!” tsada
segments.translation: Ooooh they were good. When they were getting ripe Grandma used to say, “Go pick them up, then!”

segments.speaker: emma-falling
segments.translation: So we had to pick the peaches.

segments.speaker: lucy-anderson
segments.text: ᎤᏍᏗ ᏥᏕᎦᎵ,ᏗᎰ jars ᎯᎢ ᏗᎩᏗ ᏥᏚᎲ Ꮎ ᎠᎪᎳ, ᏦᎬ,ᏙᏗ ᎪᎱᏍᏓ,
segments.transliteration: usdi tsidegali,diho jars hii digidi tsiduhv na agola, tsogv,dodi gohusda,
segments.translation: She would can them in little jars that she had, for us to use in the winter.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: ᎠᏯ ᏍᏊ ᎡᏥ ᏥᎨᎲ Mason Jars ...
segments.transliteration: aya squu etsi tsigehv Mason Jars ...
segments.translation: Us, too. My mom had mason jars.

segments.speaker: lucy-anderson
segments.translation: Yeah. That’s what she had.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: She was putting things in them.

segments.speaker: emma-falling
segments.text: ᏃᏊ ᎾᎾ ᎭᏫᏯ ᏳᎾ,ᏚᎵᏃ ᎠᏎᏛ ᏌᎶᎵ ᏙᎩᎭᎴᎪ Ꮎ ᎡᏠᎩ ᎠᏩ,ᏛᎯᏍᏔᏁ ᎤᏍᏆᎸᏅ ᎤᏍᎦᏎᏗ ᏥᎨᎲ ᎦᎶᏇ ᎤᏙᏗ
segments.transliteration: noquu nana hawiya yuna,dulino asedv saloli dogihalego na etlogi awa,dvhistane usqualvnv usgasedi tsigehv galoque udodi
segments.translation: And when they want meat, we would go hunt for squirrels. My aunt that raised me, she was real good with a gun.

segments.speaker: lucy-anderson
segments.translation: One time, I remember…

segments.speaker: emma-falling
segments.translation: …she had a .22 rifle.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: Boy. ᏙᏳ,ᎮᎾ ᎾᎯᏳ ᏥᎨᎲ ᏌᎶᎵ, ᏥᏍᏚᏃ...
segments.transliteration: Boy. doyu,hena nahiyu tsigehv saloli, tsisduno...
segments.translation: Boy. Yeah, back then there squirrel and rabbits…

segments.speaker: lucy-anderson
segments.translation: Crawdads.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: …but nobody hunts them these days.

segments.speaker: emma-falling
segments.translation: Uh-uh.

segments.speaker: lucy-anderson
segments.translation: They don’t.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: Ꮎ ‘ᏓᏁᎸ ... ᏜᏱᎪ ᏗᎦᏚᎲ ᎣᏍᏗᏁᎳ--ᎣᏥᏁᎳ ᎠᏭᏴ ᎠᎾᏝᎢᏙᎰ ᏌᎶᎵ,
segments.transliteration: na ‘danelv ... dlayigo digaduhv osdinela--otsinela awuyv anatlaidoho saloli,
segments.translation: At home – we live in Jay – squirrels are running by our house.

segments.speaker: lucy-anderson
segments.translation: My house, too, they do that.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: ᎡᏘᏴ ᏥᎨᎲ Ꮭ ᏍᎩ ᏱᎬᎾᏛᏁᎮ ... ᎦᏳ,Ꮃ ᎨᎬᏂᏍᏔᏁ ᏱᎨᎵ
segments.transliteration: etiyv tsigehv tla sgi yigvnadvnehe ... gayu,la gegvnistane yigeli
segments.translation: They couldn’t do that years ago. They would’ve already been cooked.

segments.speaker: emma-falling
segments.text: (ᎤᏰᏥᏍᎦ) Ꮎ ᏍᎩᎾ, ᎠᏫ ᎤᏩᏌ, ᏞᏍᏗ ᏙᏥᎩᏍᎩ ᏱᎨᎮ ... deer meat ... huh uh ᏌᎶᎵᏭ ᏥᏍᏚ ᎤᏅᏌ ᏏᏆᏅ ᎾᎾ ᏂᎦᏓ Ꮎ ᎠᎪᎳ ᏱᏄᎵ,ᏍᏔᏅ ᎡᏚᏓ, ᎮᎾ, ᏏᏆ ᏥᏚᏩᎧᎲ ᏓᏦᎯᏍᏗᎮ ᏂᎦᏓᏅ ᏗᏂᏲᏟ ᏚᏩᎧᎲ ᎣᎩᏂᏥ ᎾᏅ Roy ᎤᏙᏓ--ᎤᏚᏓ, ᎠᏂᏐᎢᏅ ᏂᎦᏓ ᏙᏓᏈᏕᎾ ᏑᎾᎴᎢ ᎠᏂᎷᎪ ᎠᎪᎵ Ꮎ ᏏᏆ ᏓᏂᎯᎲ ᏂᎦᏓ ᎾᎾ smokehouse..
segments.transliteration: (uyetsisga) na sgina, awi uwasa, tlesdi dotsigisgi yigehe ... deer meat ... huh uh saloliwu tsisdu unvsa siquanv nana nigada na agola yinuli,stanv eduda, hena, siqua tsiduwakahv datsohisdihe nigadanv diniyotli duwakahv oginitsi nanv Roy udoda--ududa, anisoinv nigada dodaquidena sunalei anilugo agoli na siqua danihihv nigada nana smokehouse..
segments.translation: And we did not eat deer meat. Just squirrel and rabbit. And pig. At wintertime, Grandpa had hogs, he would fatten them. All his kids, our mom, Roy’s dad, grandpa, and all others came real early on Saturdays in the wintertime to kill the hogs. Smokehouse…

segments.speaker: lucy-anderson
segments.translation: We would all look for wood.

segments.speaker: emma-falling
segments.text: Smokehouse ᎮᏅ, ᏧᏃᏢᏒ ᎥᎾ ᏓᎾ--ᏕᎦᏙ ᏏᏆ ᎥᎾᏭᏅ ᏂᎦᏓ ᏓᏁᏠᎰ ᏴᏫ
segments.transliteration: Smokehouse henv, tsunotlvsv vna dana--degado siqua vnawunv nigada danetloho yvwi
segments.translation: They had a smokehouse. That’s where they hung the hogs. And they would feed all the people.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: ‘Ꮩ ᏍᎩᎾ ᎾᎯᏳ ᏥᎨᏒ smokehouse ᏧᎦ,ᏒᏍᏗ ᏥᏍᏓᏗᎲ ᏣᏓᏁᎴ Ꮭ ᏱᎬᏲᎦ ᏥᎨᎲ
segments.transliteration: ‘do sgina nahiyu tsigesv smokehouse tsuga,svsdi tsisdadihv tsadanele tla yigvyoga tsigehv
segments.translation: I wonder why way back... the smokehouse tsugasvsdi, it wouldn’t spoil there.

segments.speaker: lucy-anderson
segments.text: Huh uh! ᏥᏕᎦᏓ ᎭᏫᏯ ᎪᎯᏓ Ꮎ ᏍᎩᎾ ᎠᎹ ᏥᏓᏂᏅᎵᏰᏍᎬ ... Ꮎ ham ᏥᎦᏓᎥ ᏙᏳ...
segments.transliteration: Huh uh! tsidegada hawiya gohida na sgina ama tsidaninvliyesgv ... na ham tsigadav doyu...
segments.translation: Uh-uh. The meat that was hanging. A long time, too. How they would put salt on them. That ham that was hanging…

segments.speaker: emma-falling
segments.text: Yeah. ᏚᏯᏅ, ᏥᏙᏣᏕᏍᎪ ᏥᏈᏍᏗ ᏚᏯ ᏚᏳᏂ,ᏍᏗ ᏥᏙᎩᎰ ᎠᎪᎵ ... ‘Ꮲ ᎡᎵᏏ, ᏙᎦᏘᏁᎪ ᏦᎦᏕᏍᏗ ᏥᎨᎲ ... ᏥᏈᏍᏗᎨ ᎣᏍᏗᏬᏂᎯ?
segments.transliteration: Yeah. duyanv, tsidotsadesgo tsiquisdi duya duyuni,sdi tsidogiho agoli ... ‘tlv elisi, dogatinego tsogadesdi tsigehv ... tsiquisdige osdiwonihi?
segments.translation: We used to pick beans. We had a lot of green beans in the winter. Our grandma used to take us to pick them. Are we talking too much?

segments.speaker: mitch-holcomb
segments.translation: No, no. It’s good.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: No, no. It’s good.

segments.speaker: mitch-holcomb
segments.translation: Just keep talking.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Just keep talking.

segments.speaker: lucy-anderson
segments.text: ᎾᏍᏊ ᎠᏂ ᏥᏙᏣᏕᏍᎬ Arkansas ᏗᏢ SiloamᏛ ᎤᏟ ᏗᏢ ᏙᎲ?
segments.transliteration: nasquu ani tsidotsadesgv Arkansas ditlv Siloamdv utli ditlv dohv?
segments.translation: We used to pick strawberries. In Arkansas. It was past Siloam, wasn’t it?

segments.speaker: emma-falling
segments.translation: Uh-huh.

segments.speaker: lucy-anderson
segments.text: Ꮎ ᎠᏍᎦᏯ ᏥᎦᏁᎸ Peggs-Ꭲ ᏥᏕᎦ--How would you say?
segments.transliteration: na asgaya tsiganelv Peggs-i tsidega--How would you say?
segments.translation: That man that lived in Peggs… How would you say?

segments.speaker: emma-falling
segments.translation: He had a big truck.

segments.speaker: lucy-anderson
segments.text: ᎤᏔᎾ, ᎣᏂ, ᏗᏢ ᎣᏣᏣᎣ ᏩᎧ, ᏳᏪᎵᏍᏗ
segments.transliteration: utana, oni, ditlv otsatsao waka, yuwelisdi
segments.translation: It was big. We used to ride in the back, just like cows.

segments.speaker: emma-falling
segments.text: ᏂᎦᏓ ᏴᏫ ᎠᏂᏣᎳᎩ ᎣᎦᏣᏅ ᏙᎦ,ᏘᏁᎪ ᎠᏂ ᏬᏣᏕᏍᎪ ᏚᏯᎴ ᏱᎦ
segments.transliteration: nigada yvwi anitsalagi ogatsanv doga,tinego ani wotsadesgo duyale yiga
segments.translation: All of us Cherokees, it would take us and we would go pick strawberries or beans.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Yeah, us, too.

segments.speaker: lucy-anderson
segments.translation: And we were there all day.

segments.speaker: emma-falling
segments.translation: Have you ever done that?

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Yeah.

segments.speaker: lucy-anderson
segments.text: ᎢᎦ ᏱᎩᏃ ᏲᏍᏗ-- ᎠᏎᏛ ᎣᏍᏗᏍᏕᎵ,Ꮧ ᏥᎨᎲ ᎡᎵᏏ, ᏥᎨᎲ ᏙᎲ?
segments.transliteration: iga yigino yosdi-- asedv osdisdeli,di tsigehv elisi, tsigehv dohv?
segments.translation: And at noon time, we always had to help Grandma, ain’t it?

segments.speaker: emma-falling
segments.translation: M-hm.

segments.speaker: lucy-anderson
segments.text: ᏥᏙᎩᎾ,ᏘᏁᎪ ᎢᎦᏅᏃ ᏦᎩᏂᏲᏏ Ꮎ bologna sandwich mustard-Ꮕ strawberry pop ᏥᏓᏂᎾ,ᏕᎬ Ꮎ ᏍᎩᎾ ᏥᏙᎩᏂᏁᎸ
segments.transliteration: tsidogina,tinego iganvno tsoginiyosi na bologna sandwich mustard-nv strawberry pop tsidanina,degv na sgina tsidogininelv
segments.translation: She took us. And at noon time, when we were hungry, we had bologna sandwiches with mustard and strawberry pop they were selling. That’s what she bought for us.

segments.speaker: emma-falling
segments.text: ᎤᎦᎾᏩ ᏳᏍᏗ ᏥᎨᎲ bolonga. Boy, it was good.
segments.transliteration: uganawa yusdi tsigehv bolonga. Boy, it was good.
segments.translation: It was kinda warm, the bologna. Boy, it was good.

segments.speaker: lucy-anderson
segments.text: ᎤᏍᎦᏍᏗ ᏥᏃᏣᏛᏁᎰ ᎣᏥᎩᏍᎬ ... ᏌᏊ ᏳᏩᎦ,Ꮣ ᎣᏣᏂᎩᏍᎬ ᏂᎦᏓ ᎣᎦᏣᎾ ᏙᏣᎢᏒ ᏥᏈᏍᏗ’ᎣᎲ ᏧᎦᎿᏅ ... ᏂᎦᏓ...
segments.transliteration: usgasdi tsinotsadvneho otsigisgv ... saquu yuwaga,da otsanigisgv nigada ogatsana dotsaisv tsiquisdi’ohv tsugahnanv ... nigada...
segments.translation: We sure was eating good. One time, we went home, we were going down the road in the truck. It just started raining a whole lot. We all got…

segments.speaker: emma-falling
segments.translation: Soaked.

segments.speaker: lucy-anderson
segments.translation: …soaked.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Riding in the back of the truck.

segments.speaker: lucy-anderson
segments.translation: We were in the back of the truck.

segments.speaker: emma-falling
segments.text: ᎠᏂᏍᏆᏂ ᏳᏪᎵᏍᏗ ᏃᎦᏛᏅ ᏍᎩ ᏄᎾ,ᏛᏃ ᎠᏂᏍᏆᏂ ᎪᎯᏥᎩ
segments.transliteration: anisquani yuwelisdi nogadvnv sgi nuna,dvno anisquani gohitsigi
segments.translation: We were just like the Hispanics. That’s what they do today, ain’t it, the Hispanics?

segments.speaker: lucy-anderson
segments.text: ᎾᎮᏅ, truck it was high, ᏙᎲ ᏥᏂ,ᏚᏮᏂ,Ꮫ
segments.transliteration: nahenv, truck it was high, dohv tsini,duwvni,dv
segments.translation: Because the truck was high.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: He had the racks?

segments.speaker: lucy-anderson
segments.translation: Yeah, racks. We were riding back there.

segments.speaker: emma-falling
segments.text: Y’know ᏍᏓᏱ ᏙᎩᎸᏫᏍᏓᏁᎸ ᎠᏎᏃ ᎤᏬᎵ,Ꮧ ᏥᎨᎲ
segments.transliteration: Y’know sdayi dogilvwisdanelv aseno uwoli,di tsigehv
segments.translation: We worked hard, but we had fun.

segments.speaker: lucy-anderson
segments.text: ᎠᏎᏅ ᏣᏅ,Ꮤ ᎣᎯᏍᏗ ᏦᎩᏂᏍᏕᎸᏛ ᎡᏥ ᎡᎵᏏ Ꮎ ᎡᏚᏓ ᏥᎨᎲ Ꮎ railroad ᏥᏚᎸᏫ,ᏍᏓᏁᎲ ‘ᎸᏢ ᏥᏪᎰ ᎢᎪᎯᏗ ᏃᏊᎴ ᏥᎦᎷᎪ ᎠᏎᏃ Ꮭ Ꮩ’...
segments.transliteration: asenv tsanv,ta ohisdi tsoginisdelvdv etsi elisi na eduda tsigehv na railroad tsidulvwi,sdanehv ‘lvtlv tsiweho igohidi noquule tsigalugo aseno tla do’...
segments.translation: But we really did help Mom and Grandma a lot. And Grandpa, he worked on the railroad and was gone for a while, and then he would come home.

segments.speaker: emma-falling
segments.text: ᎡᏚᏓ Ꮭ ᎰᏩ ᏥᎪᎥ ᏱᎩ ᎠᏯ,
segments.transliteration: eduda tla howa tsigov yigi aya,
segments.translation: I hardly ever saw my grandpa.

segments.speaker: lucy-anderson
segments.text: Uh-uh. Ꮭ Ꮩ’ ᎡᎵᏏᏍᎩᏂ, ᏙᏳ ᏦᎩᎾᏛᎯᏍᏔᏅ ᏍᎩᎾ
segments.transliteration: Uh-uh. tla do’ elisisgini, doyu tsoginadvhistanv sgina
segments.translation: Uh-uh, not really. But Grandma, she raised us.

segments.speaker: emma-falling
segments.translation: Yeah.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: Yeah. ᏙᏳ,Ꮫ Ꮩ’ ᎤᏟ ᎢᎦ ᏕᎦᏛᎯᏍᏔᏅ ᎢᎾᎨ ᎡᎯ ᏃᏊᎴ -ᎠᏂᎦᏔᎾᎥ ᎤᏅᏂᏍᏗ--ᏅᏅᏂᏍᏙᏗ ᎠᏂᎦᏴᎳ ᏣᏁᎲ ... ᎠᏯᏃ ᎨᏒ Ꮭ ᏱᏗᎦᏔᎯ ᏍᎩᏳᏍᏗ G: Ꮭ ᎰᏩ
segments.transliteration: Yeah. doyu,dv do’ utli iga degadvhistanv inage ehi noquule -anigatanav unvnisdi--nvnvnisdodi anigayvla tsanehv ... ayano gesv tla yidigatahi sgiyusdi G: tla howa
segments.translation: Yeah. They’re the ones that raised us more. And they knew a lot about gathering food from the woods and knew how to cook it, the old people back then. But us, today, we don’t know how to do that. Not really.

segments.speaker: emma-falling
segments.text: Ꮎ ... Ꮎ ᏥᏚᎾ,ᏠᏒ ᎠᎭᏂ, ... Ꮟ ᎯᎳᏴ ᏥᎧᎸ? ᏃᏭ, October ᎤᏩᏌ ᎠᎩᏄᎸᎲᏍᎪ ᏣᎳᎩ, ᎬᏂ,Ꮧ ᏱᎦᏪᏍᏗ ‘Ꮩ ᎠᏓ, October?
segments.transliteration: na ... na tsiduna,tlosv ahani, ... si hilayv tsikalv? nowu, October uwasa aginulvhvsgo tsalagi, gvni,di yigawesdi ‘do ada, October?
segments.translation: That meeting they had last July... Only one I don’t know how to say is October. How do you say it, October?

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: October.

segments.speaker: emma-falling
segments.translation: Uh. Du--…du--…something. D-u-n-i--something.

segments.speaker: mitch-holcomb
segments.translation: Dunin(i)di.

segments.speaker: emma-falling
segments.translation: Dunin(i)di.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Dulisdi.

segments.speaker: lucy-anderson
segments.translation: Dulisd(i)…dulisd(i).

segments.speaker: emma-falling
segments.translation: Oh yeah!

segments.speaker: lucy-anderson
segments.translation: Dulisd(i)!

segments.speaker: mitch-holcomb
segments.translation: Dunin(i)di…Dunin(i)di.

segments.speaker: lucy-anderson
segments.translation: Dunin(i)di.

segments.speaker: emma-falling
segments.text: Well, I study them...anyway. ᏦᎩᏁᏙᎸ the presentation ᎾᎯᏳ Ꮎ ᏣᏂᏍᏚᎢᏍᎬ October ᏥᎧᎸ or NovemberᎨ ᏥᎧᎸ?
segments.transliteration: Well, I study them...anyway. tsoginedolv the presentation nahiyu na tsanisduisgv October tsikalv or Novemberge tsikalv?
segments.translation: Well, I study them…anyway, when we went, the presentation, when they were opening, last October, or was it in November?

segments.speaker: mitch-holcomb
segments.translation: Or December?

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Yeah, that’s about when it was.

segments.speaker: emma-falling
segments.translation: We went.

segments.speaker: mitch-holcomb
segments.translation: To that one.

segments.speaker: emma-falling
segments.text: ᎥᎥ ᏂᎦᏓ Ꮎ Durbin Chris ᎤᏍᏓᏴᎲᏍᎩ ᏂᎦᏓ ᎠᎬᏱ ᏗᏢ ᏦᏥᏅ RussellᏅ ᏌᏊ ᏧᏓᏌᏅᎢᏅ
segments.transliteration: vv nigada na Durbin Chris usdayvhvsgi nigada agvyi ditlv tsotsinv Russellnv saquu tsudasanvinv
segments.translation: All of us. Durbin. His wife, Chris. We were all sitting together up front. And Russell, too. He won one…

segments.speaker: lucy-anderson
segments.translation: A big cooker.

segments.speaker: emma-falling
segments.translation: Pot.

segments.speaker: lucy-anderson
segments.text: ᏧᎳᏍᎩ, ᏍᎩᎾ ᏳᏍᏗ ᏥᏚᏂᎲ ᏙᎲ? ᎪᎯᎦ ᏥᎨᎲ ᏧᎳᏍᎩ ᎤᏔᎾ ᏱᎩᏗ
segments.transliteration: tsulasgi, sgina yusdi tsidunihv dohv? gohiga tsigehv tsulasgi utana yigidi
segments.translation: Pot…That’s what they used to have way back. They had big pots.

segments.speaker: emma-falling
segments.translation: They had three that they were putting stuff in.

segments.speaker: lucy-anderson
segments.text: ᎾᏅᏛ ᏣᏅ--ᏣᏅᏂᏍᏗᎲ ᎭᏫᏯ ᏙᎲ ᏏᏆ ᎭᏫᏯ ᏒᏃᏱᏴ ᏦᏣᎵ,ᏍᏓᏴᎲᏍᎬ ᏌᏊ ᏳᏩᎦ,Ꮣ, ᏧᏂᏢ ... Grandma ᏥᎨᎲ Ꮎ ‘head cheese’ ᏣᏃᏎᎰ ᏥᎪᏢᏗᎰ ᎾᏅ Ꮎ ᎠᏍᎪᎵ ᏧᏝᎥ Ꮎ kitchen table-Ꭲ ᏧᏂᏝᎥ ᏍᎩᎾ
segments.transliteration: nanvdv tsanv--tsanvnisdihv hawiya dohv siqua hawiya svnoyiyv tsotsali,sdayvhvsgv saquu yuwaga,da, tsunitlv ... Grandma tsigehv na ‘head cheese’ tsanoseho tsigotlvdiho nanv na asgoli tsutlav na kitchen table-i tsunitlav sgina
segments.translation: And they used that to cook the hog meat. One time, they cooked, and we were eating real late, at about midnight. And one time they killed it, and Grandma, she used to make what they call head cheese. Using the head of the hog. They had it sitting on the kitchen table.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Its head.

segments.speaker: lucy-anderson
segments.text: ᎥᎥ! ᏥᏴᏁᎲ I was...Ꮭ Ꮩ’ I guess ᏐᏁᎳ
segments.transliteration: vv! tsiyvnehv I was...tla do’ I guess sonela
segments.translation: Yeah. I was touching it. I was.. about…nine.

segments.speaker: emma-falling
segments.translation: We were probably about eight.

segments.speaker: lucy-anderson
segments.text: ᏣᏁᎳ,Ꮫ Ꮟ ᏯᏩᏕᏘᏴᏓ, ᎨᎲ Grandma ᏣᏓᏍᏓᏴᎲᏍᎨ ᎠᎢ ᏥᎦᎦ,ᏙᏗᎲ Ꮎ ᏏᏆ ... ᎠᏍᎪᎵ ᎯᎢ ᏂᏥᏴᏁᎲ (ᎤᏰᏥᏍᎬ) ... ᎧᏴᏐᎵ ... my grandma ᎤᏍᎦᏎᏗ ᎠᎩ,ᏐᎮᎸ “Ooh! ᎣᎵ,ᎩᏂ, ᎤᏁᎵ,Ꮧ ᎿᏛᏁᎠ ᏙᏱ ᏪᎾ!” ᏣᏬᏌ
segments.transliteration: tsanela,dv si yawadetiyvda, gehv Grandma tsadasdayvhvsge ai tsigaga,dodihv na siqua ... asgoli hii nitsiyvnehv (uyetsisgv) ... kayvsoli ... my grandma usgasedi agi,sohelv “Ooh! oli,gini, uneli,di hnadvnea doyi wena!” tsawosa
segments.translation: I was eight years old. Grandma was cooking and I was just watching the pig head. I was messing with it. …and his nose…Grandma got on to me. “Ooh! Ol(i)gin(i) that’s nasty. Go outside!” she told me.

segments.speaker: lucy-anderson
segments.text: ᎾᏅ eyelids ᎯᎢ ᏥᏂ,ᏕᎬᏁᎲ ᎠᎩᎦ,ᏛᎲᏍᎬ ‘Ꮩ ᏄᏍᏛ
segments.transliteration: nanv eyelids hii tsini,degvnehv agiga,dvhvsgv ‘do nusdv
segments.translation: I was doing this to the eyelids. I was checking how they were.

segments.speaker: emma-falling
segments.text: ᎾᏛ ᏧᎵᎦ,Ꮟ, ᏦᎩᏂᏅᎦᎵ,Ꮧ ᏥᎨᎲ ... gah ᎤᏁᎵ,Ꮧ ᏥᎨᎰ ... Ꮭ ᎪᎯᏥᎩ, ᏍᎩᏳᏍᏗ ᏱᎬᏥᎩ ᏏᏆ ᏍᏊ Ꮭ ᏱᎬᏥᎩ ᎠᎩᏄᎸᎾ
segments.transliteration: nadv tsuliga,si, tsogininvgali,di tsigehv ... gah uneli,di tsigeho ... tla gohitsigi, sgiyusdi yigvtsigi siqua squu tla yigvtsigi aginulvna
segments.translation: And we had to clean the guts. Gah, that was gross. I can’t eat it today. I can’t even eat the hog meat, either. I can’t do it.

segments.speaker: mitch-holcomb
segments.translation: I like to eat that.

segments.speaker: emma-falling
segments.translation: Oh, you like that?

segments.speaker: lucy-anderson
segments.translation: Oh, you like that?

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: ᎠᏯ ᏍᏊ ᏗᎩᎸᏉᏗ ᎨᎲ ᎠᏎᏅ Boy ᏯᏅᏂᏍᏗᏃ ᎦᎵ,ᏒᎬ
segments.transliteration: aya squu digilvquodi gehv asenv Boy yanvnisdino gali,svgv
segments.translation: I liked it, too. Boy, but when they were cooking it, it smelled.

segments.speaker: lucy-anderson
segments.translation: That’s right.

segments.speaker: emma-falling
segments.translation: It smells.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: When they finished cooking it, it sure was good to eat.

segments.speaker: emma-falling
segments.translation: I can’t eat it.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: It smells good when they cooked anything.

segments.speaker: mitch-holcomb
segments.text: ᎦᏅᏓᏗᏍᎬ --ᏏᏆ ᏣᏓᏅᎯᏍᏗᏍᎬᏃ ᎠᏣᏗ, ᏥᏓᏂᏅᎦᎵᏍᎬ ᏧᎵᎦ,ᏏᏅ ᏃᏊᎴ ᏥᏚᏮᏂᏍᏔᏅ ᏙᏱ ᏥᏚᏮᏂᏍᏔᏅ ᏥᎨᏎ ᎡᏠᎩ, Ꮟ ᎦᎵ,ᏒᎬ ᏥᎨᎲ
segments.transliteration: ganvdadisgv --siqua tsadanvhisdisgvno atsadi, tsidaninvgalisgv tsuliga,sinv noquule tsiduwvnistanv doyi tsiduwvnistanv tsigese etlogi, si gali,svgv tsigehv
segments.translation: I remember when they killed a hog, and they were cleaning fish, they would clean the guts. And my aunt would be cooking them outside and they still smelled.

segments.speaker: emma-falling
segments.translation: Yeah, they sure did smell.

segments.speaker: lucy-anderson
segments.text: ᏍᎩᏛ ᏃᎦᎵ,ᏍᏓᏁᎰ Ꮎ deer. How do you say ‘deer’?
segments.transliteration: sgidv nogali,sdaneho na deer. How do you say ‘deer’?
segments.translation: That’s what happens, too, with deer. How do you say deer?

segments.speaker: emma-falling
segments.translation: Deer meat, ahwi.

segments.speaker: lucy-anderson
segments.text: Deer meat. ᏍᎩ ᎠᏫ Ooh, I can’t.
segments.transliteration: Deer meat. sgi awi Ooh, I can’t.
segments.translation: Deer meat, ahwi. Ugh, I can’t.

segments.speaker: emma-falling
segments.translation: It smells.

segments.speaker: lucy-anderson
segments.translation: It smells, I can’t eat it.

segments.speaker: emma-falling
segments.text: ᎠᏎᏃ ᎪᎨᏱ ᏂᎦᎵ,ᏍᏔᏅ ᏙᏨᏂᏍᏔᏅ Ꭴ--ᏧᏓᏌᏅ ... ᏧᎳᏍᎩ ... ᏙᏱ ᎮᎾ ᏃᏊᎴ ᏍᏊ ᎠᏓᏍᏓᏴᏗ ᎣᎩᎭ, ᎥᎾ ᎠᏓ ᏗᎦ’ᏙᏗ
segments.transliteration: aseno gogeyi nigali,stanv dotsvnistanv u--tsudasanv ... tsulasgi ... doyi hena noquule squu adasdayvdi ogiha, vna ada diga’dodi
segments.translation: But when summertime comes, we’re going to cook using that big pot he won. We also have a woodstove we use outside.

segments.speaker: lucy-anderson
segments.translation: Woodstove.

segments.speaker: emma-falling
segments.translation: We use it outside.

segments.speaker: lucy-anderson
segments.text: ᎣᏣᏓᏍᏓᏴᎲᏍᎪ ᏗᏓᏁᎸ Ꮎ ᎠᏭᏴ ᏥᏈᏍᏗ ᏓᏁᏙᎰ ᎥᎾ ᏙᎲ?
segments.transliteration: otsadasdayvhvsgo didanelv na awuyv tsiquisdi danedoho vna dohv?
segments.translation: We cook outside nearby the house. And there are a lot of people there who come eat, ain’t it?

segments.speaker: emma-falling
segments.text: M-hm. Roy Cooksey ᏏᏓᏁᎸ ᏂᎦᏓ ᏧᏠᎩ ᎠᏂᎷᎪ
segments.transliteration: M-hm. Roy Cooksey sidanelv nigada tsutlogi anilugo
segments.translation: M-hm. Roy Cooksey and his family, his aunts all come.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: ᎡᏘᏴ ᏧᎳᏍᎩ ᏧᏩᏒ ᎠᎩ,ᏍᏓᏴᎲᏍᎩ, Ꮎ’Ꭱ ᏙᏳ, ᏍᏊ Ꮎ ᏧᎭᎨᏓ ᏥᎨᎰ ᏳᏍᏗ ᎨᎲ ... ᎤᏩᏒ “’ᏙᎲ ᏛᏔᎾ? ‘Ꮩ ᏛᏁᎳ?” ... “ᏔᏕᎳᎰᏌᏛ” ... ‘Ꮲ ᎩᎶ ᏧᎾᏢᏁ ᏧᎳᏍᎩ ᎭᏫᏂ ᏗᏢ ᏭᏔᎴᏎ ᏃᏊᎴ ᎦᏓ, ᏭᏢᏁ ᏧᏂ,ᏥᎸᏍᎩ ᏚᏛᎯᏍᏔᏁ ... ᏭᏢᏛ ᎣᏍᏓᏅ ᎨᏎ ᏧᎳᏍᎩ ... Man! ᎠᏂᎷᎪᏛ ᏦᎦᎵ ... “Ꮒ! ᏧᏂ,ᏥᎸᏍᎩ ᏙᏚᎳ Guy,” ᎠᎾᏗᎰ “ᏙᎯᏳᎲ ᏣᎷᎶᏣ Guy,” ᎠᎾᏗᎲ “ᎠᎩ,ᏍᏓᏴᎲᏍᎩᏛ ᎤᏛᏁᎸ,” ᎦᏥᏲᎮᎸ
segments.transliteration: etiyv tsulasgi tsuwasv agi,sdayvhvsgi, na’e doyu, squu na tsuhageda tsigeho yusdi gehv ... uwasv “’dohv dvtana? ‘do dvnela?” ... “tadelahosadv” ... ‘tlv gilo tsunatlvne tsulasgi hawini ditlv wutalese noquule gada, wutlvne tsuni,tsilvsgi dudvhistane ... wutlvdv osdanv gese tsulasgi ... Man! anilugodv tsogali ... “ni! tsuni,tsilvsgi dodula Guy,” anadiho “dohiyuhv tsalulotsa Guy,” anadihv “agi,sdayvhvsgidv udvnelv,” gatsiyohelv
segments.translation: A few years ago, my wife bought one of these pots. The one that is real heavy. “What’re you going to use it for? What’re you going to do with it?” “You’re going to find out,” she said. She got somebody to drill a hole in the bottom of the pot, she put dirt in it, and she planted flowers in it. And it was a good pot, too. Our friends came by and said, “Look, Guy has got flowers in that pot. You must be crazy, Guy,” they said. I told them it was my wife that had done it.

segments.speaker: emma-falling
segments.translation: She was the one that done it.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: ᎣᏍᏓᏅ ᎨᎲ ᏧᎳᏍᎩ ... ᎤᏩᏌ ᏍᏊ ᎤᏩᏒ ᎨᎲ ... ᎠᏯ ᎮᎾ ᎠᎩᏩᏒ ᏱᎨᎮ Ꮭ ᏍᎩ ᏱᎬᏳᎵᏍᏙᏗ
segments.transliteration: osdanv gehv tsulasgi ... uwasa squu uwasv gehv ... aya hena agiwasv yigehe tla sgi yigvyulisdodi
segments.translation: It was a good pot, too. She bought it on her own. If I had bought it, it wouldn’t be used like that.

segments.speaker: emma-falling
segments.text: ᏐᎢ ‘Ꮩ ᎤᏍᏗ ᏣᏚᎵ ᏣᏕᎳᎰᏍᏙᏗ? ᎪᏪᎵ ᏦᏪᎳ? ‘Ꮩ ᎤᏍᏗ?
segments.transliteration: soi ‘do usdi tsaduli tsadelahosdodi? goweli tsowela? ‘do usdi?
segments.translation: Is there something else you wanted to find out, that you’ve got written on the paper?

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: We are all doing good so far.

segments.speaker: emma-falling
segments.text: Oh ᎭᏩ Ꮭ ᏲᎩᎾᏅ,Ꮦ ‘Ꮩ ᏳᎵ,ᏍᏙᏗ ᎪᎯᎢᎦ
segments.transliteration: Oh hawa tla yoginanv,te ‘do yuli,sdodi gohiiga
segments.translation: Oh, OK! We didn’t know what to expect today.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: ᏙᏳ, ᎮᎾ, ᏑᏟᎶᏓ, ᏱᎪᎯᏓ ᎢᎩᏬᏂᎯᏍᏗ ᎣᏍᏓ ᏂᏍᏓᏛᏁᎠ, ᎣᏍᏓ ᏂᏍᎩᏂᏯᏔᏁ
segments.transliteration: doyu, hena, sutliloda, yigohida igiwonihisdi osda nisdadvnea, osda nisginiyatane
segments.translation: We’re supposed to talk for an hour, y’all are doing good. Y’all are answering me well.

segments.speaker: emma-falling
segments.translation: We are not shy.

segments.speaker: lucy-anderson
segments.text: ᎭᏗ ... ᎾᏛ ᎡᎵᏏ, ᏥᎨᎲ Ꮎ ᏥᎩᏁᎸᏅ ᎠᎹᏳᎵ,Ꮧ, ᏦᏍᏗ-- ... ᏥᏳᎪ,Ꮧ, South ᏗᏢ... ᎥᎾ ᏥᎨᎲ
segments.transliteration: hadi ... nadv elisi, tsigehv na tsiginelvnv amayuli,di, tsosdi-- ... tsiyugo,di, South ditlv... vna tsigehv
segments.translation: Nope. Where our late grandma used to live, by the creek. Straight toward south.

segments.speaker: emma-falling
segments.translation: Uganawa.

segments.speaker: lucy-anderson
segments.text: ᎤᎦᎾᏩ ᏗᏢ --ᏧᏪᏴ ᎤᏔᎾ Mount—hills ᏥᏂ,ᏚᏍᏛ ᎥᎾ’Ꭱ ... Ꮎ ᏅᏱ ᏧᏔᎾ slabs ᏥᏓᏃᏎᎰ real thick. BIG slabs...that granite. Granite, isn’t it?
segments.transliteration: uganawa ditlv --tsuweyv utana Mount—hills tsini,dusdv vna’e ... na nvyi tsutana slabs tsidanoseho real thick. BIG slabs...that granite. Granite, isn’t it?
segments.translation: South…there was a creek and big mount--hills and there were real big rocks, slabs they call them. Y’know real thick slabs? Granite, isn’t it?

segments.speaker: emma-falling
segments.translation: Big rocks.

segments.speaker: lucy-anderson
segments.translation: Big rocks.

segments.speaker: emma-falling
segments.translation: Cliff…in the creek!

segments.speaker: lucy-anderson
segments.text: They would fall off ... ᎥᎾ ᎡᎳᏗ ᏳᏗᏅᏒ ᎠᎹᏱ ᎥᎾ...
segments.transliteration: They would fall off ... vna eladi yudinvsv amayi vna...
segments.translation: They would fall off into the water. That’s where.

segments.speaker: emma-falling
segments.translation: …where we had a swimming place…

segments.speaker: lucy-anderson
segments.text: ...ᎤᏬᏚ ᏥᎨᎲ ... ᏌᏊ ᏳᏩᎦ,Ꮣ, ᏂᎦᏓ ᎣᏤᏙᎲ ᎥᎾ ...our cousins. ᎠᎹᏳᎵ,Ꮧ ᏦᏤᏙᎲ ᏂᎪᎯᎸ ᎣᎦᏓᏬᏍᏗ ᏥᎨᎲ ... ᎥᎾ ᏦᏣᏓᏬᏍᎬ ᎥᏛ ᎠᎩ,ᏍᎦᏍᏗ ᎠᏩᏤᎸᏒ “ᏃᏊᏛ I’m gonna dive in,” ᎦᏥᏲᎮᎸ ... ᏃᏭ ᎠᎹᏱ ᏩᏩᏕᎵᏨ ... (ᎤᏰᏥᏍᎬ) ᎭᎴ...ᏎᎦᏨ ᏥᎬᎦ
segments.transliteration: ...uwodu tsigehv ... saquu yuwaga,da, nigada otsedohv vna ...our cousins. amayuli,di tsotsedohv nigohilv ogadawosdi tsigehv ... vna tsotsadawosgv vdv agi,sgasdi awatselvsv “noquudv I’m gonna dive in,” gatsiyohelv ... nowu amayi wawadelitsv ... (uyetsisgv) hale...segatsv tsigvga
segments.translation: …it was real pretty. One time, we were all there. My cousins, we were there by the creek. And we would always swim. We were there swimming, and I was just showing off. “I’m going to dive in,” I told them. I went into the water and I almost drowned. [laughing]

segments.speaker: emma-falling
segments.translation: She almost drowned.

segments.speaker: lucy-anderson
segments.text: ᎭᎴ ᎠᎩᎬᏨ ... ᎬᎩ,ᏍᏕᎸᎲ I was going: “(panting sound)” (ᎤᏰᏥᏍᎬ) ᏃᏊᎴ ᏍᏊ ᏙᏳ ᎤᏬᎵ,Ꮧ, ᏥᎨᎮ ᎡᎵ--Mama ᏥᎨᎲ --ᎧᏃᎮᏍᎩ, ooh! ᏙᏳᎧ ᏧᏅ,Ꮫ ᎪᎱᏍᏗ ᏧᎶᏒ ᎪᎯᎦ, ᏥᎨᎲ ᏦᎩᏲᏎᎲ ᏍᎩᎾ ᏧᏍᏗ ᏥᎨᎲ ᎠᏎᏅ ‘ᏢᏛ ᏂᎦᏚ ᏳᏕᏘᏴᏓ ᎨᎮ ᏍᎩᎾ ᎡᏚᏥ ᎠᏂᏔᎵ, ᎡᏚᏥ Uncle Tony Uncle Jimmy ᏥᏚᎾ,ᏙᎥ ... ‘ᏲᎾ’ was Tony, ᏙᎲ? JimᏃ ᎤᏍᏗ ᎥᎾᏛ ᎠᎹᏳᎵ,Ꮧ, ᏩᏁᏙᎲ Ꮎ ᏥᏗᏃᎮᏍᎬ Ꮎ ᏥᏡ,Ꭼ
segments.transliteration: hale agigvtsv ... gvgi,sdelvhv I was going: “(panting sound)” (uyetsisgv) noquule squu doyu uwoli,di, tsigehe eli--Mama tsigehv --kanohesgi, ooh! doyuka tsunv,dv gohusdi tsulosv gohiga, tsigehv tsogiyosehv sgina tsusdi tsigehv asenv ‘tlvdv nigadu yudetiyvda gehe sgina edutsi anitali, edutsi Uncle Tony Uncle Jimmy tsiduna,dov ... ‘yona’ was Tony, dohv? Jimno usdi vnadv amayuli,di, wanedohv na tsidinohesgv na tsitlu,gv
segments.translation: I almost drowned. They helped me. I was breathing hard. And then, one time, it was real funny. Our late mother, she really knew a lot of things as she was growing up. She would tell us about it. When she was young, about 14 years old, my uncles – my two uncles. Uncle Tony, Uncle Jimmy, was their names. Yon(a) was Tony, ain’t it? Jim was the one that was little – they were by the creek. What we were talking about…

segments.speaker: emma-falling
segments.translation: David, that we were talking about?

segments.speaker: lucy-anderson
segments.translation: No, that tree from earlier.

segments.speaker: emma-falling
segments.translation: Oh. Kotsunega.

segments.speaker: lucy-anderson
segments.text: ᎪᏧᏁ-- ᎦᏳ,Ꮃ, ᎠᏮᎨᏩ (ᎤᏰᏥᏍᎬ) ᏥᏡ,Ꭼ ... ᏥᏡ,Ꭼ ᏣᏗᎲ
segments.transliteration: gotsune-- gayu,la, awvgewa (uyetsisgv) tsitlu,gv ... tsitlu,gv tsadihv
segments.translation: Sycamore tree. I already forgot. [laughs] There was a tree like that there.

segments.speaker: mitch-holcomb
segments.translation: Dawatsil(a)…dawatsil(a).

segments.speaker: emma-falling
segments.translation: Dawatsil(a)…no, that’s elm tree.

segments.speaker: lucy-anderson
segments.text: It’s that sycamore. ᎢᎾ--ᎠᎹᏱ ᎤᏔᎾ ᎢᏡᎬ ᏣᏗᎲ ᏧᏔᎾ limbs ᏂᏚᏍᏛ ᎦᎸᎳᏗᏴ whole underneath-Ꭲ ᎢᎾ ...sand-ᏳᏍᏗ Ꮎ really ᏧᏍᏗ ᎨᎲ ᏅᏱ ᏣᏗᎲ ᏂᎬ
segments.transliteration: It’s that sycamore. ina--amayi utana itlugv tsadihv tsutana limbs nidusdv galvladiyv whole underneath-i ina ...sand-yusdi na really tsusdi gehv nvyi tsadihv nigv
segments.translation: It’s that sycamore. Down there by the creek, there was a big sycamore tree with big limbs. Way up there, underneath it was sand-like, there was little rocks…

segments.speaker: emma-falling
segments.translation: Gravel.

segments.speaker: lucy-anderson
segments.text: Ooh, yes, gravel real soft. ᎤᎾᏛ ᏚᎾᏁᎶᏅ ᏣᏗᎲ ᎾᏛ ᎡᏚᏥ ᏥᎨᎲ “Haw,” ᏣᏓ “ᎾᏛ judge ᏓᏥᎦᏘᏁᏌ ‘ᎨᎢ ᏫᎦᎸᎳᏗ, ᏗᏯ” ᏣᏓ ᏃᏅ ᎫᏩᏳ ᎤᏂᏰᎸᏍᏔᏅ courthouse-Ꭲ “That’s it! ᏫᏓᏥᏃᎮ--ᏫᏓᏥᏝᏃᎮᏔᎾ!” ᎤᏛᏅ ᏣᏗᎲ Mama-Ꮫ ᎠᏭ ᏗᏢ ᎠᏁᏙᎲ ᏣᏗᎲ ᏭᎦ,ᏍᏓ ᏃᏊᎴ ᎤᎴᏅᎲ ᎦᎸᎳᏗ ᏣᏓ ᎪᎱᏍᏗ ᏄᎵᏍᏔᏂᏙᎸ ᏚᎶᏒ ᏣᏗᎲ ... *thump* ᎤᏛᏅ ᏣᏗᎲ (ᎤᏰᏥᏍᎬ) “ᏝᏍᏊ ᏯᏩᏅ,Ꮤ, if he’s alive,” ᎤᎾ,ᏛᏅ ᏣᏓ “ᎦᎵᏬᎦᎨ?” ᎣᎩᎾ,ᏛᏅ ᏣᏓ ᏗᎾᏓᎸ Momma-Ꮕ ᎤᏂᏍᎦᏍᏓᏁᎸ --ᎤᎾᏂᎩᏎ Ꮟ ᏗᎦᎾᏭ ᏣᏗᎲ (ᎤᏰᏥᏍᎬ)
segments.transliteration: Ooh, yes, gravel real soft. unadv dunanelonv tsadihv nadv edutsi tsigehv “Haw,” tsada “nadv judge datsigatinesa ‘gei wigalvladi, diya” tsada nonv guwayu uniyelvstanv courthouse-i “That’s it! widatsinohe--widatsitlanohetana!” udvnv tsadihv Mama-dv awu ditlv anedohv tsadihv wuga,sda noquule ulenvhv galvladi tsada gohusdi nulistanidolv dulosv tsadihv ... *thump* udvnv tsadihv (uyetsisgv) “tlasquu yawanv,ta, if he’s alive,” una,dvnv tsada “galiwogage?” ogina,dvnv tsada dinadalv Momma-nv unisgasdanelv --unanigise si diganawu tsadihv (uyetsisgv)
segments.translation: It was gravel, real soft. He said they played there, my uncle. “Haw, I’m going to go see the judge at his fancy office.” They pretended they were in Jay at a courthouse. “That’s it, I’m going to go talk to him,” he said. Momma and them were beside them. Now, way up there something happened, and he fell. He made a sound, “Thump!” … “I don’t know if he’s alive,” they said. “No, he’s dead,” Momma and her sister got scared and they went home. He was just laying there.

segments.speaker: emma-falling
segments.translation: It was Roy, Grandpa, that she was talking about.

segments.speaker: lucy-anderson
segments.text: ᏍᎩ ᏥᎨᎲ ... “ᎪᎯᏴ ᎤᎷᏨ” ᏣᏗᎲ ᏲᎾ (ᎤᏰᏥᏍᎬ) “ᎤᏢᏅ ᏳᏪᎵᏍᏗ ᎨᎲ” ᏣᏗᎲ Mama ‘ᏍᎦᏍᏗ ᎢᎦᏪ ᏄᏛᏁᎴ Grandma ᎣᎩᏍᎦᏍᏛ ᏣᏗᎰᎢᏅ
segments.transliteration: sgi tsigehv ... “gohiyv ulutsv” tsadihv yona (uyetsisgv) “utlvnv yuwelisdi gehv” tsadihv Mama ‘sgasdi igawe nudvnele Grandma ogisgasdv tsadihoinv
segments.translation: Way after a while, Yon(a) came. He looked like he had been asleep, Momma said. Grandma did something brave. It scared us.

segments.speaker: emma-falling
segments.text: ᎾᏛᏍᏊ ... ᎤᎵᎪᎲᏍᏗ ᏱᏗ’ᎢᎵᏃ ᏎᏗ, ᏙᏍᏚ-- ᏙᏍᏚᏖᏍᎬ ᏥᏈᏍᏗ ᎮᎾ ᏤᎲ ᏕᏡ,Ꭼ ᎪᎯᎦ ᏥᎨᎲ ᏗᎦᎾ,ᏗᏅᏍᏔᏃ ᏥᎨᎲ ᏎᏗ, ...wheelbarrow ᏦᎩᏂᎲ ᏃᏊᎴ Ꮎ ᎦᎾ,ᏏᏅᏍᏗ--wagon ᏦᎩᏂᎲ ᏍᎩᎾ ᎧᎵ ᏙᎩᏂᏠ ᏎᏗ ... ᏙᎩᏂᏗᎨᏯᎶ ᏦᎩᏂᎾ,ᏗᏅᏗ ᎯᎢᏛ ᏥᏈᏍᏗ ᏙᎩᏂᏠ ᏍᎩᎾ ᎠᏕᎳ, ᎣᎩᏃᏢᏅ ᏍᎩᎾ ᎣᏍᏛᏗᎲ ᏦᎩᎾ--ᏦᎩᎾᎳᏑᎶ ᏦᎩᎾᎿᏬ ᏦᎩᏂᏩᎯᏍᏙᏗ ᏙᏍᏓᏕᎶᏆᏍᎬ ᏍᏊ ᏳᏩᎦ,Ꮣ Ꮎ’Ꭱ ᎤᏍᏗ ᏎᏗ ᎯᎢ ᎤᏍᏗ ᏗᎧᎾ,Ꮧ ᎢᏡ,Ꭼ Ꮭ Ꮩ’ ᎢᎾ ᏂᎦᏘ, ᏱᎨᏎ ᏥᏳᎪ,Ꮧ ᏃᏊᎴ ᎯᎢ ᏗᏢ ᏄᏍᏛ ᏐᎢ, ᎯᎢᏭ ᏗᏢ ᏄᏍᏛ Ꮎ ... ᎧᏃᏌᏛ ᏳᏍᏗ ᎯᎢ ᏗᏢ Ꮎ ᎥᎾ ᎤᎿᏑᎦ ᏍᏊ ᏄᏍᏛ
segments.transliteration: nadvsquu ... uligohvsdi yidi’ilino sedi, dosdu-- dosdutesgv tsiquisdi hena tsehv detlu,gv gohiga tsigehv digana,dinvstano tsigehv sedi, ...wheelbarrow tsoginihv noquule na gana,sinvsdi--wagon tsoginihv sgina kali doginitlo sedi ... doginidigeyalo tsoginina,dinvdi hiidv tsiquisdi doginitlo sgina adela, oginotlvnv sgina osdvdihv tsogina--tsoginalasulo tsoginahnawo tsoginiwahisdodi dosdadeloquasgv squu yuwaga,da na’e usdi sedi hii usdi dikana,di itlu,gv tla do’ ina nigati, yigese tsiyugo,di noquule hii ditlv nusdv soi, hiiwu ditlv nusdv na ... kanosadv yusdi hii ditlv na vna uhnasuga squu nusdv
segments.translation: In the fall, we picked up walnuts. There were a lot of walnut trees. And you could sell the walnuts back then. We had a wheelbarrow and also a wagon to pull, and we had it full of walnuts. We had a pile to sell and we had a whole bunch of them. What money we made selling walnuts, that’s what we used to buy shoes and clothes for school. One time, there was a little walnut tree, it wasn’t really tall. There was another one leaning this way, like a nose. There were also possum grapes there.

segments.speaker: lucy-anderson
segments.translation: It was about this time [of year] they sprout.

segments.speaker: emma-falling
segments.text: “ᎯᎢᏛ ᏓᏥᎢᎴᏏ ᎢᏡ,ᎬᎢ!” ... “ᎭᏩ” ᏥᏲᏎᎸ Ꮎ ᏗᏓᏟᎶᏍᏙᏗ ᎣᎩᏂᎲ “ᏗᏍᏆᏟᎶᏍᏔᏅ ᏗᎾ” ᎤᏛᏅ “ᎭᏩ” ᏥᏲᏎᎸ ᏃᏭ ᎤᎩᎸᏅᏭ ᏃᏭᏅ ᎯᎢ ᏗᏢ ᏄᏍᏛ ᎯᎢ ᏗᏢ ᏄᏍᏛ ᎢᎾ “ᎯᎢ ᏓᎦᏛᏁᎵ” ᎤᏛᏅ ᎯᎢ ᏗᏢ ᏄᏛᏁᎸ ᏚᎶᏎ (ᎤᏂᏰᏥᏍᎬ) ...ᏚᎶᏎ ... ᎦᎶᏍᎬ ᏕᏥᏂᏴᎲ ᎣᎩᏂᎭ ᏍᏊ ᏍᎩᎾ (ᎤᏂᏰᏥᏍᎬ) ᎠᏎᏛ--ᏎᏗᏭ ᏕᎦᏝᏭ
segments.transliteration: “hiidv datsiilesi itlu,gvi!” ... “hawa” tsiyoselv na didatlilosdodi oginihv “disquatlilostanv dina” udvnv “hawa” tsiyoselv nowu ugilvnvwu nowunv hii ditlv nusdv hii ditlv nusdv ina “hii dagadvneli” udvnv hii ditlv nudvnelv dulose (uniyetsisgv) ...dulose ... galosgv detsiniyvhv oginiha squu sgina (uniyetsisgv) asedv--sediwu degatlawu
segments.translation: “I’m going to climb this tree,” she said. “Go ahead,” I told her. We had a camera. She said, “Be sure and take my picture.” “OK,” I told her. She climbed the one that was leaning [like this]. “I’m going to do this [gestures],” she said. So, she leaned over and she fell off. [laughter] I took a picture of her falling. And we still have it. She landed on the walnuts.

segments.speaker: lucy-anderson
segments.translation: “I barely survived.”

segments.speaker: emma-falling
segments.translation: “It’ll just hang there,” she said. She thought she was good, but she fell off.

segments.speaker: lucy-anderson
segments.translation: We thought it was funny.

segments.speaker: emma-falling
segments.translation: We went through funny times.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
