segments.translation: Did it scare you all?

segments.speaker: lucy-anderson
segments.translation: Yeah, it really did.

segments.speaker: emma-falling
segments.text: Ꮭ ᎩᎶ ᏲᎩᏂᏃᎮᏞ ᏲᎩᏂᎸᏂᎴ ᏳᎾᏕᎳᎰᏒ ᎩᎶ ᏲᏍᏗᏃᏎᎴ
segments.transliteration: tla gilo yogininohetle yoginilvnile yunadelahosv gilo yosdinosele
segments.translation: We didn’t tell anybody. We would’ve got a whooping if they found out. So we didn’t tell.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: It would’ve been real funny if that happened.

segments.speaker: lucy-anderson
segments.text: ᎾᏛ ᏍᏊ ᏥᏙᏍᏚᏖᏍᎬ ᏎᏗ ‘ᎨᎢ ᏗᏢ ᏥᎨᎲ ᏗᏓᏁᎸ Ꮎ ᎠᏍ--‘Ꮲ ᎠᏂᏲᏁᎦ,Ꭷ ᏣᏂᏁᎸ ᏍᎩᎾ ᏦᎩᎾᎵ,ᏍᎪᎳ,ᏓᏁᎸ ᏦᎩᏄᏖᏍᏗ ᎾᎮᎾ ᏩᎧ ᏗᏛᎯᏍᏗᏍᎩ, ᏥᎨᎲ ᏍᎩᎾ Ꮭ ᏳᏚᎵᎮ Ꮎ ᏎᏗ y’know “ᏕᏍᏚᏖᏒᎢ” ᏦᎩᏃᎮᎸ Ꮎ “gunny sacks” ᏥᏓᏃᎮᎰ Ꮭ ᏯᏩᏅ,Ꮤ, ᏚᏙᎥ ᏍᎩᎾ ᎧᎵᎢ ᏥᏂᏙᏍ---ᏥᏂ,Ꮩ--we filled them up ᏙᎲ? ᎧᎵ ... ᏙᏍᏗ,---
segments.transliteration: nadv squu tsidosdutesgv sedi ‘gei ditlv tsigehv didanelv na as--‘tlv aniyonega,ka tsaninelv sgina tsoginali,sgola,danelv tsoginutesdi nahena waka didvhisdisgi, tsigehv sgina tla yudulihe na sedi y’know “desdutesvi” tsoginohelv na “gunny sacks” tsidanoheho tla yawanv,ta, dudov sgina kalii tsinidos---tsini,do--we filled them up dohv? kali ... dosdi,---
segments.translation: When we were picking walnuts over there by a house – white people lived there, but they gave us permission to pick the walnuts up. He used to raise cattle, and he didn’t want them to eat the walnuts. “Pick them up!” he told us. He gave us those gunny sacks – I don’t know what they’re called. We would fill them up, real full. We...

segments.speaker: emma-falling
segments.translation: We dragged them around.

segments.speaker: lucy-anderson
segments.text: ᏙᏍᏗᏏᏙᎰ ᎠᎢ ᏬᏍᏗᎶᎯ, ... ᎥᎾ ᏦᎩᏂᎶᏒ ᏭᏓᎾᏅᏅ (unintelligible)
segments.transliteration: dosdisidoho ai wosdilohi, ... vna tsoginilosv wudananvnv (unintelligible)
segments.translation: We dragged them around. Where we walked, we made a trail.

segments.speaker: emma-falling
segments.text: ᏓᏬᎵ’Ꭱ ᏍᏊ ᏦᎩᏲᏗ ᏥᎨᎲ ᏥᏈᏙᎲ ᏥᎨᎲ ᏓᏬᎵ ᎪᎯᏥᎩ Ꮭ ᏯᏁᎯ,
segments.transliteration: dawoli’e squu tsogiyodi tsigehv tsiquidohv tsigehv dawoli gohitsigi tla yanehi,
segments.translation: We used to look for mushrooms, too. There used to be a whole bunch of mushrooms. But they’re not around today.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Uh-uh.

segments.speaker: emma-falling
segments.text: Ꮎ ᎤᏂᏁᎦ, ᎤᏂᎫᎫ ᏥᏓᏃᏎᎰ Ꭿ’Ꭱ--Ꮎ ᏌᏊ ᏳᏩᎦ,Ꮣ, ᎯᎢ ᏱᎩᏓ, ᏦᎩᏩᏛᎮ
segments.transliteration: na uninega, unigugu tsidanoseho hi’e--na saquu yuwaga,da, hii yigida, tsogiwadvhe
segments.translation: That white one, the one they call Ugugu. We found one, this big.

segments.speaker: lucy-anderson
segments.translation: There was some Wisi, too. Isn’t that right?

segments.speaker: emma-falling
segments.text: ᎥᎥ ᏫᏏ Ꮎ ᏌᏊ ᏳᏩᎦ,Ꮣ, ᏫᏏ, ᎦᏚᏏᏭ ᎾᎥ ᎯᎢ’Ꭱ ᏧᏂᎧᎾ,Ꮧ
segments.transliteration: vv wisi na saquu yuwaga,da, wisi, gadusiwu nav hii’e tsunikana,di
segments.translation: One time we found one, Wisi, and it was on a hill. And it was this [gestures] big.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: My gosh.

segments.speaker: emma-falling
segments.text: Gah ᎤᏔᎾ ᎨᎮ ᏫᏏ, ᏙᏳ ᏍᏊ ᎣᏍᏓ ᎠᎩᏍᏗ ᏥᎨᎲ
segments.transliteration: Gah utana gehe wisi, doyu squu osda agisdi tsigehv
segments.translation: It was a big Wisi, and it was good to eat.

segments.speaker: lucy-anderson
segments.text: ᏂᎪᎯᎸ ᏦᎦᎵ,ᏍᏓᏴᏅ ᏙᎲ? ᏂᎪᎯᎸ ᏣᎾ,ᏓᏍᏓᏴᎲᏍᎬ Ꮎ ᏳᏂᎷᏣ ᏃᏊᎴ ᎩᎶ ᏱᏓᏳᎷᏣ,Ꮓ Grandma ᏥᎨᎲ kitchen-Ꭲ ᏥᏩᏴᏍᎪ ᏣᏓᏍᏓᏴᎲᏍᎪ “ᎢᏣᎵ,ᏍᏓᏴᎲᎦ ᏗᎾ!”
segments.transliteration: nigohilv tsogali,sdayvnv dohv? nigohilv tsana,dasdayvhvsgv na yunilutsa noquule gilo yidayulutsa,no Grandma tsigehv kitchen-i tsiwayvsgo tsadasdayvhvsgo “itsali,sdayvhvga dina!”
segments.translation: We were always eating. And they were always cooking. When somebody came, Grandma went into the kitchen and started cooking. “Y’all eat!” she’d tell everybody.

segments.speaker: emma-falling
segments.text: ᎤᏂᏠᎦ,Ꭷ ᏥᏚᎾ,ᏙᎥ (...unintelligible...) ᏓᏅᏍᏔᏅ ᎤᏂᏠᎦ, ᏥᏈᏍᏙᎲ ᏥᎨᎰ
segments.transliteration: unitloga,ka tsiduna,dov (...unintelligible...) danvstanv unitloga, tsiquisdohv tsigeho
segments.translation: There were ones called Unitlog, there used to be a whole bunch of them.

segments.speaker: lucy-anderson
segments.translation: But you can’t find them today.

segments.speaker: emma-falling
segments.translation: Uh-uh.

segments.speaker: lucy-anderson
segments.text: ᏒᎩᏅ ᏍᏊ ᏃᏊ ᏥᎩ, ᎡᎯ ᏥᏈᏍᏙᎲ ᎨᎰ
segments.transliteration: svginv squu noquu tsigi, ehi tsiquisdohv geho
segments.translation: There is wild onion right now. A whole lot of it.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: What y’all talked about…the mushroom, the Wisi.

segments.speaker: emma-falling
segments.text: ᏍᏓᏱ ᏗᎩᎾᏛᏗ ᎪᎯᏥᎩ, ... Yeah, ᏥᏈᏍᏙᎲ ᏥᏙᎩᎾᎣ
segments.transliteration: sdayi diginadvdi gohitsigi, ... Yeah, tsiquisdohv tsidoginao
segments.translation: They’re hard to find today. Yeah, we used to have a whole bunch.

segments.speaker: lucy-anderson
segments.text: ᎨᏍᏗ’Ꭱ ... ᏙᏳ Ꮭ ᏲᎩᎾᏅ,Ꮩ ᎦᏓᏅᏖᏍᎪ ᏳᏓᎭ ‘ᏙᎲ ᎠᏛᏁᎰ ᎡᎵᏏ ᏥᎨᎲ ᎣᎨᏠ,ᏗᎰ Ꮎ ᎠᎪᎳ ᏱᎩ ᏂᎪᎯᎸ ᎪᏍᏗ ᏧᎰ ᏣᏓᏍᏓᏴᎲᏍᎪ ᏑᎾᎴᎢ ᏱᎩ biscuits ᏥᏚ--ᏥᏚᎲ ᏧᏔᎾ woodstove-Ꭲ ᏧᏮ--ᏧᏮᏔᏅ ... ᏃᏭᏅ ᏃᏊᏛ gravy ᏳᏬᏢᏅ ᎠᏑᏍᏗ ᏳᏬᏢᏅ Ꮎ stove-Ꭲ Ꮎ lid ᏥᏂ,ᏕᎬᏂ,ᏗᏍᎪ Ꮎ pan—uh...ski—frying pan ᎥᎾ ᏥᏂ,ᎬᏂ,ᏗᎰ where that fire is ... ᎣᏍᏓ, ᏥᏂ,ᎬᏂᏗᎰ that water gravy. ᎾᏛ ᎠᎹ,ᏳᏍᏗ ᏳᏍᏚᏞ Ꮎ gravy ᏂᎬ it just ᎦᎵ,ᏦᏕᏭ ᏃᏭ ᎣᎩᏰᏍᏗᎰ ᎩᎳ ᏱᎪᎯᏓ, ᏙᏣᏗᏓᏂᏓ ᎣᏥᏗᏁᏍᎪ “ᎠᎵ,ᏍᏓᏴ,Ꮧ,” ᏣᏓ (ᎤᏰᏥᏍᎬ) ᏙᏳ, ᏍᏊ ᎤᏲ ᏙᏳ,--ᏙᏳ, ᎤᏲ ᎣᎩᏲᏝ, ᎾᎮᎾ --ᎡᎵᏏ, ᏥᎨᎲ Ꮎ ᎦᎵ,ᏦᏕ ᎠᎪᎳ ᏱᎩ, ᎯᎢ ᏗᏢ north side ᏗᏢ
segments.transliteration: gesdi’e ... doyu tla yoginanv,do gadanvtesgo yudaha ‘dohv advneho elisi tsigehv ogetlo,diho na agola yigi nigohilv gosdi tsuho tsadasdayvhvsgo sunalei yigi biscuits tsidu--tsiduhv tsutana woodstove-i tsuwv--tsuwvtanv ... nowunv noquudv gravy yuwotlvnv asusdi yuwotlvnv na stove-i na lid tsini,degvni,disgo na pan—uh...ski—frying pan vna tsini,gvni,diho where that fire is ... osda, tsini,gvnidiho that water gravy. nadv ama,yusdi yusdutle na gravy nigv it just gali,tsodewu nowu ogiyesdiho gila yigohida, dotsadidanida otsidinesgo “ali,sdayv,di,” tsada (uyetsisgv) doyu, squu uyo doyu,--doyu, uyo ogiyotla, nahena --elisi, tsigehv na gali,tsode agola yigi, hii ditlv north side ditlv
segments.translation: We really don’t know – I think about it sometimes – how Grandma fed us. But she always had something to eat. And when it’s winter, she always had something to cook. Early in the morning she had big biscuits using the wood stove to cook. When she made gravy, there’s that lid on the stove, she took it off and put a pan…frying pan where the fire is to make water gravy. When she put the water in the pan, the smell woke everybody up. And we would all get up real quick. “It’s time to eat!” she’d say. We were really poor. Granny’s house – when it was winter, on the north side [of the house].

segments.speaker: emma-falling
segments.translation: The north side.

segments.speaker: lucy-anderson
segments.text: ᎤᏴᏜ ᏗᏢ Ꮎ ᎥᏂ,Ꮵ ᏥᏗᏴᎯᎰ ᎦᎵ,ᏦᏕ ᏗᏢ ᎣᏥᏂ,ᏝᎣ Ꮎ ᎡᏥ ᏥᎨᎲ Ꮎ ᏂᎦᎵ,ᏍᏗᏭ ᎪᎱᏍᏗ ᎣᏍᏓ, ᏱᏂ,ᎬᏂ,ᏗᎰ ᏙᏳ ᏍᏓᏱ ᎣᎩᎶᏒ ᎾᏅ ᏲᎦᎵ,ᏍᏓᏴᏅ ᏑᎾᎴ ᎬᏅᎯᏗ, ᏣᏓ--ᏧᎾ,--
segments.transliteration: uyvdla ditlv na vni,tsi tsidiyvhiho gali,tsode ditlv otsini,tlao na etsi tsigehv na nigali,sdiwu gohusdi osda, yini,gvni,diho doyu sdayi ogilosv nanv yogali,sdayvnv sunale gvnvhidi, tsada--tsuna,--
segments.translation: The north side. Snow would come in the house. We would be laying there. And Mom used to just put anything there. We sure went through hard times. When we ate in the morning in the…

segments.speaker: emma-falling
segments.translation: In the kitchen.

segments.speaker: lucy-anderson
segments.text: ᎠᏓᏍᏓᏴᏗ ᏗᏢ, ᎬᏅᎯᏗ, ᏥᎨᎲ Ꮎ ... --ᏣᏓᏍᏓᏴᎲᏍᎪ ᏑᎾᎴ ᏱᎩ, --ᎡᎵᏏ,Ꮫ ᎡᏥᏛ ᏍᏊ ᏣᏍᏕᎵᏍᎬ Ꮎ ... ᏯᎵ,ᏍᏓᏴ,ᏗᎢ ᎡᏚᏓ, ᏥᎨᎲ Ꮭ ᏯᏩᏅ,Ꮤ, ᏳᏍᏗ Ꭼ,ᏗᎲ ᎪᏍᏗ ᏥᏩᎩᏍᎪ Ꮎ ᎠᏥᎳ, ᎤᏢ,ᏙᏗ Ꮎ woodstove-Ꭲ ᏥᎦᎴᏍᎬ ᏍᏗᎩᏗ ᎭᏫᏂ, ᏗᏢ, table-Ꭲ ᏣᎲᏍᎪ so it’d be warm.
segments.transliteration: adasdayvdi ditlv, gvnvhidi, tsigehv na ... --tsadasdayvhvsgo sunale yigi, --elisi,dv etsidv squu tsasdelisgv na ... yali,sdayv,dii eduda, tsigehv tla yawanv,ta, yusdi gv,dihv gosdi tsiwagisgo na atsila, utlv,dodi na woodstove-i tsigalesgv sdigidi hawini, ditlv, table-i tsahvsgo so it’d be warm.
segments.translation: In the kitchen, Grandma had a long [table] toward the kitchen side and that is where Mom cooked EARLY in the morning. I mean Grandma, but Mom would help her, too. When it was time to eat. Grandpa – I don’t know what he used but – he put something there to put the coals in when he got them out. He put it under the table so we’d be warm.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: Yeah. ᎠᏯ ᏍᏊ ᏣᏗ ᎡᎵᏏ, ᏥᎨᎲ ᎪᏪᎵᏭ’Ꭱ ᏥᏕᎦᏯᎸᏍᎬ
segments.transliteration: Yeah. aya squu tsadi elisi, tsigehv goweliwu’e tsidegayalvsgv
segments.translation: What you’re saying. My late grandmother she would stick papers up [on the wall].

segments.speaker: emma-falling
segments.translation: That’s what she used to do.

segments.speaker: lucy-anderson
segments.text: ᏍᎩᏛ ᏥᏄᏛᏁᎸ ᏌᏊ ᏳᏩᎦ,Ꮣ, kitchen-Ꭲ ᏗᏢ, ᎣᏍᏓ ᏥᏄᏩᏅ --Ꮭ ᏯᏩᏅ,Ꮤ, ᏳᏍᏗ ᏳᏍᏛ ᎢᏌ, ᏙᎲ? ᎠᎻᏅ, Ꮎ paste ᏄᏮᏁᎸ Ꮎ paper ᏄᏮᏂ,ᏔᏅ Ꮎ that roll paper y’know ᏳᏍᏗ ... ᏑᎾᎴ ᎠᏰᏟ, ᎢᎦ ᏥᏍᏕᏥᏛ ᎤᏂᎨ ᎠᏰᏟ, ᎢᎦ --ᎤᏂᏲᏢᏅ ᏥᎨᎲ (ᎤᏰᏥᏍᎬ) “Ꮒ! Ꮎ ᏄᏍᏛ!” ᏣᏓ,
segments.transliteration: sgidv tsinudvnelv saquu yuwaga,da, kitchen-i ditlv, osda tsinuwanv --tla yawanv,ta, yusdi yusdv isa, dohv? aminv, na paste nuwvnelv na paper nuwvni,tanv na that roll paper y’know yusdi ... sunale ayetli, iga tsisdetsidv unige ayetli, iga --uniyotlvnv tsigehv (uyetsisgv) “ni! na nusdv!” tsada,
segments.translation: That’s what she did one time, Grandma. In the kitchen, she got flour and water and she was making paste. She put the paste on the paper on the roll paper. Then the next morning, half of it was off. I guess some mice ate it. They had eaten half of it. [laughter] … ”Look at that!”

segments.speaker: emma-falling
segments.translation: She used flour to make paste.

segments.speaker: lucy-anderson
segments.text: Roll paperᏅ ᏧᏮ,ᏔᏅ Ꮭ ᏯᏅ,Ꮤ, ᎭᏢᏴ ᎤᏁᏒ ᎠᏎᏅ ᎠᏰᏟ, ᎢᎦ ᎤᏂᎬ (ᎤᏰᏥᏍᎬ) ᎾᏅ, ᏍᏊ ᎤᎾ ... (ᎤᏰᏥᏍᎬ) kitchen-Ꭲ how do you say it?
segments.transliteration: Roll papernv tsuwv,tanv tla yanv,ta, hatlvyv unesv asenv ayetli, iga unigv (uyetsisgv) nanv, squu una ... (uyetsisgv) kitchen-i how do you say it?
segments.translation: She made a wallpaper, but they ate half of it. Kitchen…how do you say it?

segments.speaker: emma-falling
segments.translation: Adasdayvdi.

segments.speaker: lucy-anderson
segments.text: ᎠᏓᏍᏓᏴ,Ꮧ ᎠᎩᏄᎸᎲᏍᎬ ... ᏍᎩᎾ ᏧᏩᎧᎲ Ꮎ --stoveᎢ ᏗᏢ, ᎠᎭᏂ ᏗᏢ,Ꮕ window ᎠᏦᎳᏂ, ᏥᏄᏮᏂ,Ꮫ ᎮᏍᏗ screen ᏱᏂ,ᏚᏮᏂ,Ꮫ ᎾᎯᏳ ᏥᎨᎲ ᎢᎦᏛ ᏱᎩ ... ᏳᏓᏍᏓᏴᏅ Grandma ᏐᏈᎵ ᏧᎾᏝᎥ ᎾᎥ ᎡᎲ ᎠᏍᎦᏯ ᏍᎩᎾ ‘Ꭺ’ᎢᎸ ᏤᏙᎲ ᏐᏈᎵ ᎥᎾ’Ꮲ ᏌᏊ ᏳᏩᎦ,Ꮣ, Grandma ᎡᎵᏏ, ᏥᎨᎲ biscuits ᏧᏬᏢᏅ ᏚᏝᎾᎥ ... ᎠᎭᏂ window ᎠᎭᏂ ᎥᎾ ᎠᏓᏍᏓᏴ,Ꮧ ᏧᎲ ᎯᎢ ᏗᏢ, ᏚᏝᎲ ᎦᏚ ᎤᎦ,ᏛᎲᏎ ᏃᏭᏛ ᏐᏈᎵ --ᏚᎴᏒ ᎦᏚ (ᎤᏰᏥᏍᎬ) ᏃᏭ ᎦᏙᎬ ᏓᎩᏍᎬ ᎦᏚ Grandma ᏥᎨᎲ ᎪᎱᏍᏗ, -- Ꮭ ᏯᏩᏅ,Ꮤ, ᏳᏍᏗ ᎨᎲ
segments.transliteration: adasdayv,di aginulvhvsgv ... sgina tsuwakahv na --stovei ditlv, ahani ditlv,nv window atsolani, tsinuwvni,dv hesdi screen yini,duwvni,dv nahiyu tsigehv igadv yigi ... yudasdayvnv Grandma soquili tsunatlav nav ehv asgaya sgina ‘go’ilv tsedohv soquili vna’tlv saquu yuwaga,da, Grandma elisi, tsigehv biscuits tsuwotlvnv dutlanav ... ahani window ahani vna adasdayv,di tsuhv hii ditlv, dutlahv gadu uga,dvhvse nowudv soquili --dulesv gadu (uyetsisgv) nowu gadogv dagisgv gadu Grandma tsigehv gohusdi, -- tla yawanv,ta, yusdi gehv
segments.translation: Adasdayvdi. I can’t [say it]… She had a stove on this [gestures] side and had a window on that [gestures] side. We didn’t have screens back then. And when Grandma cooked – her neighbor had a horse and it was always around Grandma’s house. One time Grandma made some biscuits, and she had them by the window and the stove is on this [gestures] side, that’s where she had the biscuits. She turned around and the horse got the biscuits. It was standing there eating the biscuits and Grandma picked up a... I don’t know what it was…

segments.speaker: lucy-anderson
segments.translation: …a pan and hit the horse on the head. [laughter]

segments.speaker: emma-falling
segments.translation: A pan.

segments.speaker: emma-falling
segments.text: Ooh! ᎤᏓᏈᏍᏗ ᏥᎨᎰ ᏐᏈᎵ, ᏂᎪᎯᎸ ᏙᎦᏕᏙᏗᎲ
segments.transliteration: Ooh! udaquisdi tsigeho soquili, nigohilv dogadedodihv
segments.translation: It was annoying. The horse was always bothering us.

segments.speaker: lucy-anderson
segments.translation: They wouldn’t even lock it up. It was always there.

segments.speaker: emma-falling
segments.text: ᎠᏎᏃ, ᎤᎾ,ᏓᎾ,Ꮫ ᏥᎨᎲ ᎠᏂᏲᏁᎦ ᏣᏂᏁᎸ ᎾᎥ
segments.transliteration: aseno, una,dana,dv tsigehv aniyonega tsaninelv nav
segments.translation: But they were nice, the white people that lived nearby.

segments.speaker: lucy-anderson
segments.text: Grandma-Ꮫ frying pan *boom!* (ᎤᏰᏥᏍᎬ) ᎠᏥᏍᎫᏴ ... Ꮭ ᏯᏩᏅ,Ꮤ, ᏳᏍᏗ ᏄᏍᏓᏁᎸ ᏐᏈᎵ,
segments.transliteration: Grandma-dv frying pan *boom!* (uyetsisgv) atsisguyv ... tla yawanv,ta, yusdi nusdanelv soquili,
segments.translation: [laughter] She hit it on the head. I don’t know if something happened to the horse.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: ᎠᏯᏛ ᏍᏊ ᎡᎵᏏ, ᏥᎨᎲ ᎠᏓᏍᏓᏴ,Ꮧ ᏗᏢ, ... ᎮᏍᏗ ᏯᏖᎾ, ᏱᎨᏎ ᎦᏓᏭ, ᏥᎨᎲ ᎾᎿ ᎣᏏ, ᎠᏓᏍᏓᏴ,Ꮧ ᏧᏩᎧᎲ ᎠᎢ ᏗᏢ, ᎥᎾ ᏣᎾ,ᏓᏍᏓᏴᎲᏍᎬ ᎤᎦᎾᏮ ᏥᎨᏒ ᎦᏓ, ᎦᏓ, ᎥᎾ ᎤᎾ,ᏓᏍᏓᏴ,Ꮧ ᏗᏢ, ᎤᎦᎾᏮ ᎨᎲ ᏃᏊᎴ ᏣᏅᏃᏌᏍᎬ ᎡᏧᎳᎭ ᎦᎵ,ᏦᏕ ᎾᏅᏁᎲ
segments.transliteration: ayadv squu elisi, tsigehv adasdayv,di ditlv, ... hesdi yatena, yigese gadawu, tsigehv nahna osi, adasdayv,di tsuwakahv ai ditlv, vna tsana,dasdayvhvsgv uganawv tsigesv gada, gada, vna una,dasdayv,di ditlv, uganawv gehv noquule tsanvnosasgv etsulaha gali,tsode nanvnehv
segments.translation: My late grandmother, in her kitchen there wasn’t floorboards. It was all dirt. She had a stove and cooked there. The ground was real warm toward the kitchen. It was WARM. And they would sweep just like they do in the house.

segments.speaker: emma-falling
segments.translation: …like in a house. It was hard wasn’t it?

segments.speaker: lucy-anderson
segments.translation: She had one like that…

segments.speaker: emma-falling
segments.translation: Great Grandma. That’s what it was like.

segments.speaker: lucy-anderson
segments.translation: That’s what it was like, wasn’t it? Where she lived.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: She had one like that, too?

segments.speaker: emma-falling
segments.text: ᎥᎥ Ꮎ ᎠᏓᎭ ᏭᏓᏁᎸ ᎠᏓᏍᏓᏴ,ᏗᏭ ᎢᎦ ᏧᏩᎧᎲ ᎠᏓᏍᏓᏴ,ᏗᎢᏅ ᏍᏊ ᎦᏓᏭ ᏥᎨᎲ ... ᏝᏍᎩᏂ, ᎰᏩ ᏱᏬᎩᏁᏙᎸ ᎥᎾᎾ ᏗᏢ ooh! ᎤᎵ,ᏍᎦᏂᏍᏗ ᏥᎨᎲ ᎠᎦᏴᎵᎨ ᎡᎵᏏ’Ꭱ ᎤᏥ ᎨᎲ ᎤᎵ,ᏍᎦᏂᏍᏗ ᏥᎨᎲ ... ᎮᏍᏗ ᏗᏂᏲᏟ ᏱᏚᎸᏉᏕ
segments.transliteration: vv na adaha wudanelv adasdayv,diwu iga tsuwakahv adasdayv,diinv squu gadawu tsigehv ... tlasgini, howa yiwoginedolv vnana ditlv ooh! uli,sganisdi tsigehv agayvlige elisi’e utsi gehv uli,sganisdi tsigehv ... hesdi diniyotli yidulvquode
segments.translation: Yeah, it was a wood house. All she had was a stove. The eating area was all dirt. We hardly went over there because the old lady was real mean. It was our grandma’s mom. She was mean. She didn’t like kids.

segments.speaker: lucy-anderson
segments.text: Uh-uh. ᏍᏗ ᎤᏁᎫᏥᏓ, ᏥᎨᎲ ᏱᏙᏣᏁᎶᎲᏍᎬ ᎥᎾ ᏲᏣᏟᏙᎲ ... safety pin ᏥᏄᏮᏅᏛ ᎯᎢ ᏄᏍᏛ Ꮭ ᏯᏩᏅ,Ꮤ, ᏄᏰᎵ,Ꮫ
segments.transliteration: Uh-uh. sdi unegutsida, tsigehv yidotsanelohvsgv vna yotsatlidohv ... safety pin tsinuwvnvdv hii nusdv tla yawanv,ta, nuyeli,dv
segments.translation: She was a little bit crazy. If we were playing, running around, she had a safety pin on her. We didn’t know why.

segments.speaker: emma-falling
segments.translation: I know. I said she was mean. If it falls…

segments.speaker: lucy-anderson
segments.translation: By where we were playing…

segments.speaker: emma-falling
segments.translation: The pins she talked about. She would put them on us.

segments.speaker: lucy-anderson
segments.text: Ꮎ ᏲᏣᏟᏙᎲ ᎯᎢ ᏥᏂ,ᏙᎬᏁᎲ ooh! It hurt.
segments.transliteration: na yotsatlidohv hii tsini,dogvnehv ooh! It hurt.
segments.translation: When we ran, she put those on us and ooh! It hurt.

segments.speaker: emma-falling
segments.text: ᏍᎩᎾ Ꮩ ᎮᏍᏗ ᏲᎩᎸᏉᏕ ᎥᎾ ᏬᎨᏓᏍᏗ ... Ꮭ ᎰᏩ ᏱᏬᎨᏙᎴ
segments.transliteration: sgina do hesdi yogilvquode vna wogedasdi ... tla howa yiwogedole
segments.translation: So we didn’t like to go over there. We hardly ever went over there.

segments.speaker: lucy-anderson
segments.text: eww ᏍᏗ ᎤᏁᎫᏥᏙ ᏲᎨᎵᎰ ᏲᏥᏅ Ꮭ ᏯᏩᏅᏔ...
segments.transliteration: eww sdi unegutsido yogeliho yotsinv tla yawanvta...
segments.translation: She was sort of crazy. We'd be sitting there thinking.

segments.speaker: emma-falling
segments.text: Ꮭ ᎢᎸᎯᏳ ᎣᏍᏓ ᏱᎨᎮ Ꮭ ᏯᏩᏅ,Ꮤ, ‘Ꮩ
segments.transliteration: tla ilvhiyu osda yigehe tla yawanv,ta, ‘do
segments.translation: She was never right. I don’t really know.

segments.speaker: lucy-anderson
segments.text: ᎮᏍᏗ’Ꭳ ᎤᎪᏓ, ᎣᎨᏙᎸ ᏱᎨᎮ ᎥᎾ ᏳᏓᎭᏭ
segments.transliteration: hesdi’o ugoda, ogedolv yigehe vna yudahawu
segments.translation: Yeah, we hardly went over there. Just every now and then.

segments.speaker: emma-falling
segments.translation: M-hm.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Every now and then. She was always like that?

segments.speaker: lucy-anderson
segments.translation: M-hm.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: If you all went there.

segments.speaker: lucy-anderson
segments.translation: M-hm, yeah.

segments.speaker: emma-falling
segments.translation: M-hm, yeah.

segments.speaker: emma-falling
segments.translation: I don’t know…

segments.speaker: lucy-anderson
segments.translation: …what was wrong with her. If she was sick or something.

segments.speaker: emma-falling
segments.translation: It was really sad to go there.

segments.speaker: lucy-anderson
segments.text: Ꮎ ᏍᏊ ᏥᎩ ᏍᎩ ᏄᏍᏗ, ᎤᎯᏐᏓ ᎥᎾ
segments.transliteration: na squu tsigi sgi nusdi, uhisoda vna
segments.translation: But even now today, it’s really sad.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: ‘Ꮲ ᏥᏁᎸ ᏥᎨᎰ ᎤᎯᏐᏗ ᎡᏓᏍᏗ ᎨᎰ ᏗᎧᏂᏓᏍᏗ’ᏛᎲ ᏍᏊ
segments.transliteration: ‘tlv tsinelv tsigeho uhisodi edasdi geho dikanidasdi’dvhv squu
segments.translation: When you go where you used to live, it is really sad there? Even just to look around?

segments.speaker: lucy-anderson
segments.translation: It’s scary at night.

segments.speaker: emma-falling
segments.text: ᎾᎿ ᎦᎵ,ᏦᏕ Ꮎ ᏗᎧᏃᎩᏍᏙᏗ ᏧᎲ Ꮎ ᎯᎢ ᏗᎬᏁ,Ꮧ Ꮎ “organ” ᏣᏃᏎᎰ ᏍᎩ ᏳᏍᏗ ᏥᏕᎧᏃᎩᏍᏛ ooh! ᎤᎯᏐᏗ ᏥᎨᎰ
segments.transliteration: nahna gali,tsode na dikanogisdodi tsuhv na hii digvne,di na “organ” tsanoseho sgi yusdi tsidekanogisdv ooh! uhisodi tsigeho
segments.translation: In the house, at night, whoever would play music – the one they call organ – and it was sad music.

segments.speaker: lucy-anderson
segments.text: Ꮵ,ᎩᎵ ᏳᏪᎵᏍᏗ ᎤᏂᏴᏢ--ᎤᏴᏞ ᏄᏍᏙ ᏍᎩᎾ ... ᏌᏊ ᏳᏩᎦ,Ꮣ, ᏥᏩᎩᏯᏅᎲ “ᎡᎮᎾ!” ᎠᏬᎮᎸ Grandma ᏥᎨᎲ ᎮᏍᏗ ᏯᏩᏚᎸ ᎠᏪᏅᏍᏗ ᏙᏳ, ᏥᏍᎦᏰᎰ ᎢᎾ ᏍᎩ ᏳᏍᏗ ᏧᏃᎩᏍᏔᏅ ᏒᏃᏱ ᏥᏙᏗᎧᏃᎩᏍᏗᎰ ᏥᎦᎾ,ᏰᎪ ᏙᏳ,
segments.transliteration: tsi,gili yuwelisdi uniyvtlv--uyvtle nusdo sgina ... saquu yuwaga,da, tsiwagiyanvhv “ehena!” awohelv Grandma tsigehv hesdi yawadulv awenvsdi doyu, tsisgayeho ina sgi yusdi tsunogistanv svnoyi tsidodikanogisdiho tsigana,yego doyu,
segments.translation: It felt like the boogers came in. One time she came and got me, Grandma. “Come on,” she said. I didn’t want to go, cause I was afraid. She played that kind of music at midnight. She’d be playing it and it was really scary.

segments.speaker: emma-falling
segments.translation: It was real scary to go there. I was scared.

segments.speaker: lucy-anderson
segments.translation: It’s still like that today.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: It’s the same as when she lived there?

segments.speaker: lucy-anderson
segments.translation: Yeah.

segments.speaker: emma-falling
segments.translation: Yeah.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Does anyone live there now?

segments.speaker: lucy-anderson
segments.translation: and

segments.speaker: emma-falling
segments.translation: One

segments.speaker: lucy-anderson
segments.translation: Yeah, one great-great grandson lives there now.

segments.speaker: emma-falling
segments.text: ᎥᎾ ... Ꮭ ᎥᎾ ᎦᎵ,ᏦᏕ ᏱᏓᏓᏁᎳ, ... ᏄᏓᎴ
segments.transliteration: vna ... tla vna gali,tsode yidadanela, ... nudale
segments.translation: But it’s not the same house.

segments.speaker: lucy-anderson
segments.text: Huh uh, ᏄᏓᎴ ᎠᏓᏁᎳ, ᏃᏊ ᏥᎩ,
segments.transliteration: Huh uh, nudale adanela, noquu tsigi,
segments.translation: It’s a different house now.

segments.speaker: emma-falling
segments.translation: Uh-uh. We didn’t go there all the time.

segments.speaker: lucy-anderson
segments.translation: But it’s still the same way.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Is that right?

segments.speaker: lucy-anderson
segments.text: ᎾᏍᏊ ᏣᏂᏁᎳ,Ꮓ ᏍᏊ ᎤᏠᏱ ᏄᏍᏗ, ... Mary Belle ᏧᏛᏅ ᏙᎲ?
segments.transliteration: nasquu tsaninela,no squu utloyi nusdi, ... Mary Belle tsudvnv dohv?
segments.translation: It’s still the same way for the ones living there, that’s what Mary Belle said, ain’t it?

segments.speaker: emma-falling
segments.translation: Uh-huh. Their name was Bluebirds.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Oh, Bluebirds.

segments.speaker: emma-falling
segments.text: ᏙᏳ ... John Lee ᎤᏲᏢ ᏧᏲᎱᏒ --ᏑᏕᏘᏴᏓ,Ꮫ ᏥᎨᎲ John Lee Bluebird ᎤᏍᏆᎸᏅ ᎤᏬᏚᎯ, ᎠᏣᎳᎩ ᎤᏬᏂᎯᏍᏗ ᏥᎨᎲ
segments.transliteration: doyu ... John Lee uyotlv tsuyohusv --sudetiyvda,dv tsigehv John Lee Bluebird usqualvnv uwoduhi, atsalagi uwonihisdi tsigehv
segments.translation: Really…John Lee…it was real sad when he died, a year ago. John Lee Bluebird. He really spoke Cherokee beautifully.

segments.speaker: lucy-anderson
segments.translation: Yeah, that’s true.

segments.speaker: emma-falling
segments.text: Y’know, ᎢᎦᏓ Ꭴ:ᏬᏚᏨ ᎠᏂᏬᏂᎲ ᎢᎦᏓᏅ, Ꮭ
segments.transliteration: Y’know, igada u:wodutsv aniwonihv igadanv, tla
segments.translation: Y’know some of them can speak [Cherokee] real beautiful. And some of them don’t.

segments.speaker: lucy-anderson
segments.translation: That’s how it was.

segments.speaker: emma-falling
segments.text: ᎣᏍᏓᏭᏛ ... ᎤᏬᏚᎯ, ᎦᏬᏂᏍᎨ ... Ꮟ ᏌᏊ ... ᎠᏂᏔᎵ, ᏗᎾ,ᏓᏅᏟ, Ꮟ ᎠᏁᎯ, ... ᏌᏊ Jim ᏚᏙᎠ, ᎠᏎᏅ --ᎠᏂᎦᏴᎳ, ᎤᏂᏴᏍᏗ ᏩᏯ ᎤᎶᏒᏍᏔᏅ ᎤᏬᏚᎯ, ᎠᏣᎳᎩ, ᎦᏬᏂᏍᎩ, Ꮎ ᏧᎾ,ᏓᏂᏐᏗ ᏦᎩᏂᎸᏫ,ᏍᏓᏁᎭ, Ꮎ McClain ᎦᎶᏇᏗ ᏗᏢ, ᎥᎾ ᏂᎦᏓ, ᏏᏓᏁᎸ ᏙᎩᎸᏫ,ᏍᏓᏁᎰ ᎥᎾ ᏍᎩᎾ, ᎦᎷᎪ Jim ᎠᏣᎳᎩᎭ ᎣᏥᏬᏂᏍᎪ ᏳᎷᏣ,
segments.transliteration: osdawudv ... uwoduhi, gawonisge ... si saquu ... anitali, dina,danvtli, si anehi, ... saquu Jim dudoa, asenv --anigayvla, uniyvsdi waya ulosvstanv uwoduhi, atsalagi, gawonisgi, na tsuna,danisodi tsoginilvwi,sdaneha, na McClain galoquedi ditlv, vna nigada, sidanelv dogilvwi,sdaneho vna sgina, galugo Jim atsalagiha otsiwonisgo yulutsa,
segments.translation: It was good. He could speak good and he still has two brothers that are alive. One of them is named Jim – he lives in a nursing home now, but he speaks Cherokee real well. We worked at McClain Cemetery in Locust Grove. We worked with their family, and Jim would come. When he came, we would only speak Cherokee.

segments.speaker: lucy-anderson
segments.translation: We didn’t speak any English.

segments.speaker: emma-falling
segments.translation: Uh-uh. We only spoke Cherokee.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Is he still living?

segments.speaker: lucy-anderson
segments.translation: Yeah, but he is sickly.

segments.speaker: emma-falling
segments.translation: He is sickly.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Can he still speak?

segments.speaker: lucy-anderson
segments.text: ᎡᎵᏭ ᏱᎦᏬᏂᎯ, ᎾᎮᎾ, ...his hip...ᎨᎵ ᏣᎾ,ᏗᎲ ᎾᏅ ...his stomach... ᎪᎱᏍᏗ, ᏳᏍᏗ, ᏣᎾ,ᏗᎲ ᎠᏎᏃ, ...nursing home-Ꭲ... Salina ᎡᎯ, ᎠᏎᏃ, ᏙᏳ, ᎤᏬᏚᎯ, ᎦᏬᏂᏍᎩ,
segments.transliteration: eliwu yigawonihi, nahena, ...his hip...geli tsana,dihv nanv ...his stomach... gohusdi, yusdi, tsana,dihv aseno, ...nursing home-i... Salina ehi, aseno, doyu, uwoduhi, gawonisgi,
segments.translation: Yeah, he can still speak. They say something is wrong with his hip and stomach. He stays in Salina, but he still can speak beautifully.

segments.speaker: emma-falling
segments.translation: It’s good.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: So, he’s in Salina?

segments.speaker: emma-falling
segments.text: ᎥᎥ Salina ᎠᏯ ... ᎠᏩᏚᎵᎰ ᎩᎶ ᎤᏛᏓᏍᏗ ᎦᏬᏂᏍᎬ ᎤᏬᏚᎯ, ᎦᏬᏂᏍᎩ, ᎢᎦᏓ,Ꮕ, y’know ᎯᎢᏭ ᏳᏍᏗ ᏂᎦᎵ,ᏍᏗᎰ ᎠᏂᏬᏂᏍᎬ ᏃᎴ -- ᎯᎾ just ᎣᏍᏓ,
segments.transliteration: vv Salina aya ... awaduliho gilo udvdasdi gawonisgv uwoduhi, gawonisgi, igada,nv, y’know hiiwu yusdi nigali,sdiho aniwonisgv nole -- hina just osda,
segments.translation: Yeah, he stays in Salina. I wish someone would listen to him speak, he sure can speak real pretty. But some now speak however they think it should be. But him, it’s just good.

segments.speaker: emma-falling
segments.translation: And his parents were Cherokee speakers.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: What was his name?

segments.speaker: emma-falling
segments.translation: His name is Jimson Bluebird.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Jim Bluebird.

segments.speaker: emma-falling
segments.translation: And he’s in a nursing home.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: I wonder if they’d let somebody visit him.

segments.speaker: lucy-anderson
segments.translation: Uh-huh. Yeah, uh-huh.

segments.speaker: emma-falling
segments.translation: We haven’t been there yet..

segments.speaker: lucy-anderson
segments.translation: Peggs-Ꭲ uh... yeah…

segments.speaker: emma-falling
segments.translation: Because he lives in Peggs by himself.

segments.speaker: lucy-anderson
segments.translation: He fell there and something happened to him.

segments.speaker: emma-falling
segments.text: ᏓᏂᏍᏓᏲᎯᎲ ᏥᎨᎲ ᏑᏕᏘᏴᏓ ᏥᎨᎲ Ꮎ ᎣᎩᏅᏌ, ᏍᎩᎾ Jim --ᎣᎦᎵ,ᏍᏓᏴᏅ ᏧᏪᏅᏒ ᏃᏊ ᏧᎾ,ᏓᏂᏐᏗ ᎣᎨᏅᏒ ᎣᏍᏓ ᏂᏓᏮᏅᏁᎸ Ꮎ ᏏᏓᏁᎸ --ᏓᏂᎾᎥ Ꮎ ᎠᏥᎾ, ᏓᏩᏃᏢᏅ ᎣᎩᏅᏌ, ᏦᎩᏃᏢᏅ ᏧᏬᏚᎯ, ᎣᏍᏓ ᏙᎩᏂᏢᏅ Jim ᎨᎴ “ᏗᏇᏅᏒ ᏍᎩ ᎢᏕᎾ!” ᎤᏛᏅ “ᎭᏩ” ᎣᏍᏙᏎᎸ ᏂᎦᏓ, these Avon bottles ᏚᎲ ᎫᎫ, ᏂᎦᏓ,
segments.transliteration: danisdayohihv tsigehv sudetiyvda tsigehv na oginvsa, sgina Jim --ogali,sdayvnv tsuwenvsv noquu tsuna,danisodi ogenvsv osda nidawvnvnelv na sidanelv --daninav na atsina, dawanotlvnv oginvsa, tsoginotlvnv tsuwoduhi, osda doginitlvnv Jim gele “diquenvsv sgi idena!” udvnv “hawa” osdoselv nigada, these Avon bottles duhv gugu, nigada,
segments.translation: A year ago, during Christmas, we were at Jim’s and we ate. Just us, and Jim. Then after that, we went to the cemetery. We fixed up the graves of our family that was laying there. We made our own Christmas trees and decorated them pretty, and we put them on the graves. And Jim was with us. “Let’s go to my house,” he said. “Alright,” we said. He had all of the Avon bottles.

segments.speaker: lucy-anderson
segments.translation: They were pretty.

segments.speaker: emma-falling
segments.text: ᏙᏳ, ᏚᎲ ᏥᏈᏍᏙᎲ, ᏚᎲ ᎯᎳ ᎢᎦ box ᏕᏣᏩᏛᎲ? ᏦᎢ...ᏅᎩᎴ ᏱᎦ? ᎧᎵ
segments.transliteration: doyu, duhv tsiquisdohv, duhv hila iga box detsawadvhv? tsoi...nvgile yiga? kali
segments.translation: He had a lot. How many boxes did you find? Three or four full boxes?

segments.speaker: lucy-anderson
segments.translation: Two.

segments.speaker: emma-falling
segments.translation: Full. He gave them to me.

segments.speaker: lucy-anderson
segments.text: “ᎮᏍᏗ, ᎩᎶ ᏯᏩᏚᎵ ᏄᏓᎴ ᏧᏫᏗ” ᏦᎩᏃᏎᎸ ᏙᎩᏂᏁᎸ Ꮟ ᏓᎩᎭ, ᏓᏟᏍᏗᏅ, ᏍᏊ ᎮᏍᏗ, ᏳᏔᏅ ᏓᏟᏍᏓᏅ ᏍᏊ
segments.transliteration: “hesdi, gilo yawaduli nudale tsuwidi” tsoginoselv dogininelv si dagiha, datlisdinv, squu hesdi, yutanv datlisdanv squu
segments.translation: “I don’t want anyone else to take them,” he told us. He gave them to us and I still have them. And they have stuff in them, too! He didn’t use them, they have something in them, too.

segments.speaker: emma-falling
segments.translation: Yeah, he gave us a bunch of stuff.

segments.speaker: lucy-anderson
segments.text: ᎠᏕᎳᎰᏍᎬᏛ ᏧᏢᎬ ᎮᏍᏗ,Ꮕ ᎰᏩ ᎪᏍᏗ, ᏳᎾᎥ’ᎲᎧ?
segments.transliteration: adelahosgvdv tsutlvgv hesdi,nv howa gosdi, yunav’hvka?
segments.translation: I guess he was realizing he was sick. He hardly had anything.

segments.speaker: emma-falling
segments.text: Ꮎ ᏕᎦᏂᏢ ᏍᏊ Ꮎ ᎮᏍᏗ, ᎣᏍᏓ ᎤᏮᏁᎸ ᏱᎨᎮ y’know ᎦᏍᎩᎶᏭ ᎬᏅᎯᏓ, --ᎦᏍᎩᎶ ᎥᎾ --ᎦᏟᎰ ᎠᏓᏍᏓᏴ,Ꮧ ᏍᏊ Ꮭ ᏳᏓᏍᏓᏴᏅ ᎤᏲ ᏄᏛᏅ ᎠᏎᏅ...
segments.transliteration: na deganitlv squu na hesdi, osda uwvnelv yigehe y’know gasgilowu gvnvhida, --gasgilo vna --gatliho adasdayv,di squu tla yudasdayvnv uyo nudvnv asenv...
segments.translation: And his beds, they weren’t made up. He had a chair. A long chair. That’s where he slept. And the kitchen, he didn’t even cook. He was living bad.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: I would like to go visit him.

segments.speaker: emma-falling
segments.translation: M-hm.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Y’all said Jim Bluebird.

segments.speaker: emma-falling
segments.translation: His friend has a phone.

segments.speaker: lucy-anderson
segments.text: ᏂᎪ’Ꮈ ᎯᎢ... Ꮎ ... ᏦᎢᏛ 3 or 4 years-Ꮓ ᏙᎲ? Ꮎ ᏦᎢ car accidents ᎾᏩᎵ,-- ᏔᎵ, car accidents ᎾᏩᎵ,ᏍᏓᏁᎸ uh huh ... ᎾᏍᏊ ᎯᎢ ...the last one. I had three back surgeries. Ꮎ ᏥᏐᎯ ...my neck surgery...ᎠᎭᏂ, Ꮭ ᏯᏩᏅ,Ꮤ, ...spine ᏣᎾ,ᏗᎲ ᎭᎴ Ꮪ...ᎭᎴ snapped ᏄᎵ,ᏍᏔᏅ ᎠᎭᏂ, ...Ꮟ ᏃᏊ ᏥᎩ, ᎠᎩᏄᎸᎲᏍᎪ --ᎣᏍᏓ ᎪᎱᏍᏗ ᏯᏩᏛᏁ,Ꮧ ᏳᏓᎭ ᎠᎩᏬᏂᎯᏍᏗ ᏍᏊ ᎠᎩᏄᎸᎲᏍᎪ ᎠᏎᏅ, ᎤᎾ ᏧᏓᎴᏅᎲ ᏒᎯ, ᏍᏊ ᎦᎾᎦ,Ꮨ ᏥᏩᏪᏙᎸ ᏃᏊᎴ ᏥᎬᎩᏁᎸ ᏅᏬᏘ, ᏎᎦᏨ ᏯᎩᎩᏢᏅ ᏑᏕᏘᏴᏓ,ᏛᏃ December last year ᏙᎲ? No, year before. Yeah, year before December ᏥᎨᎲ this December [a] year ᏥᎨᎲ Ꮩ --ᎠᎩᏢᏅ all—all summer-Ꮫ Ꮭ ᎰᏩ ᎪᎱᏍᏗ, ᏯᏩᏛᏁᎸ ᎠᎩᏄᎸᎲᏍᎪ ᎣᏍᏓ --ᎠᏩᏂᎩᏍᏗ ᏥᏅᎬᏭ, ᎩᎵ ᏥᎩ, ᏃᏊ ᏥᎩ, ᏓᏤᏝ
segments.transliteration: nigo’lv hii... na ... tsoidv 3 or 4 years-no dohv? na tsoi car accidents nawali,-- tali, car accidents nawali,sdanelv uh huh ... nasquu hii ...the last one. I had three back surgeries. na tsisohi ...my neck surgery...ahani, tla yawanv,ta, ...spine tsana,dihv hale du...hale snapped nuli,stanv ahani, ...si noquu tsigi, aginulvhvsgo --osda gohusdi yawadvne,di yudaha agiwonihisdi squu aginulvhvsgo asenv, una tsudalenvhv svhi, squu ganaga,ti tsiwawedolv noquule tsigvginelv nvwoti, segatsv yagigitlvnv sudetiyvda,dvno December last year dohv? No, year before. Yeah, year before December tsigehv this December [a] year tsigehv do --agitlvnv all—all summer-dv tla howa gohusdi, yawadvnelv aginulvhvsgo osda --awanigisdi tsinvgvwu, gili tsigi, noquu tsigi, datsetla
segments.translation: Three or four years ago I had two car accidents. And also, the last one, I had three back surgeries. My neck surgery – I don’t know... they call it spine – almost snapped. Even now I have a hard time doing things, even talking. Sometimes I can’t talk. That’s where it all began. Yesterday, I went to the doctor, and they gave me some more medicine. I had a hard time going to sleep. It’s been a year ago, December last year, wasn’t it? Or the year before? Yeah, the year before! It was December. It was a year ago. This December, it was a year ago. I slept! I didn’t do anything all summer. I could hardly walk. I kept falling down. I’m just now feeling better.

segments.speaker: emma-falling
segments.translation: Jim was helping her get to the doctor.

segments.speaker: lucy-anderson
segments.text: ᎥᎥ ᏂᎪ’Ꮈ ᎦᎾᎦ,Ꮨ Ꭶ--ᎾᎴ ᏱᎩ, ... ᎦᎶᏇᏗ ᏗᏓᎾᏅ ᏬᏍᏕᏙᎰ ᎾᎮᎾ, Harp’s-Ꭲ ᏗᎩᎸᏫ,ᏍᏓᏁᎸ ᏥᎨᎲ
segments.transliteration: vv nigo’lv ganaga,ti ga--nale yigi, ... galoquedi didananv wosdedoho nahena, Harp’s-i digilvwi,sdanelv tsigehv
segments.translation: He always took me to the doctor or we went to the store at Locust Grove. I used to work at Harp’s.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: The one in Salina?

segments.speaker: lucy-anderson
segments.translation: Uh-uh. Locust Grove.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Oh, Locust Grove.

segments.speaker: lucy-anderson
segments.translation: I work for 14 years…

segments.speaker: emma-falling
segments.translation: Yeah, 14 or 15.

segments.speaker: lucy-anderson
segments.text: ᏍᎩᎦᏚᎴ ᏱᎦ, ᎪᎯᏓ, ᏓᎩᎸᏫ,ᏍᏓᏁᎸ ᎥᎾ -- ᏥᏐᎯ -- ... How do you say it?
segments.transliteration: sgigadule yiga, gohida, dagilvwi,sdanelv vna -- tsisohi -- ... How do you say it?
segments.translation: Or 15 years. And that’s when I…How would you say it?

segments.speaker: emma-falling
segments.translation: You were doing things that caused you to hurt your back.

segments.speaker: lucy-anderson
segments.text: ᎥᎾ ᏧᏓᎴᏅᎲ ᏃᏊ ᏥᎩ, ᏦᎢ ᏳᏩᎦ,Ꮣ, ᎣᏍᏓ ᏄᏅᏁᎸ ᏥᏐᎯ ... Ꮎ ᏥᎩᎵ,ᎨᏂ, ᏌᏊ ᏳᏩᎦ,Ꮣ, ᏌᏊ... ᏙᏳ ‘ᏍᎦᏍᏗ ᎾᏮᏁᎸ ᎠᎭᏂ,
segments.transliteration: vna tsudalenvhv noquu tsigi, tsoi yuwaga,da, osda nunvnelv tsisohi ... na tsigili,geni, saquu yuwaga,da, saquu... doyu ‘sgasdi nawvnelv ahani,
segments.translation: That’s when it started. They have already fixed my back three times. And my neck. One time, it was really hurting me.

segments.speaker: emma-falling
segments.translation: It was here in town. Where she got hit.

segments.speaker: lucy-anderson
segments.translation: M-hm!

segments.speaker: emma-falling
segments.text: It was a freak accident, ᏙᎲ? ᏌᏊ ᎠᏍᎦᏯ, ᎠᏗᏟᏒ Ꮎ ᎠᎬᏱ ᏗᏢᏍ ᎦᏩᏛ?
segments.transliteration: It was a freak accident, dohv? saquu asgaya, aditlisv na agvyi ditlvs gawadv?
segments.translation: It was a freak accident, ain’t it? There was a man driving by… Was it his front wheel?

segments.speaker: lucy-anderson
segments.translation: M-hm.

segments.speaker: emma-falling
segments.translation: …and his front wheel came off and it hit her.

segments.speaker: lucy-anderson
segments.text: Right on my door. ᏍᏓᏲᏒ ᎠᏮᏂᎸ
segments.transliteration: Right on my door. sdayosv awvnilv
segments.translation: Right on my door. It hit me real hard, too.

segments.speaker: emma-falling
segments.translation: He lost his car, too.

segments.speaker: lucy-anderson
segments.text: ᏂᎦᏓ, it just totaled it. ... ᎾᏍᏊ ᏔᎵᏁ 4 years ago ᏐᎢ, ᏍᏊ accident ᏥᎾᏩᎵ,ᏍᏓᏁᎸ ᎥᎾ McClaine Cemetery --ᏦᎩᏂᎸᏫ,ᏍᏓᏁᎸ ᎮᎾ, ...I’m one of the head... (board members) board member ᎤᎾ... ᎤᎾ ᎣᏥᏅᎦᎵᏍᎪ ... ᎯᏍᎩᏛ ᏃᏥᎠ, ᏂᎦᏓ, ᎤᎾ’Ꮫ Memorial Day ᏗᎩᎸᏫ,ᏍᏓᏁ--ᏓᎩᎸᏫᏍᏓᏁᎸ ᎤᎾ ᎠᏕᎳ ᏕᏥᎩᏏᏙᎲ, ...y’know donations and stuff... ᏃᏊᏛ ᏥᎦᏘᏴ...
segments.transliteration: nigada, it just totaled it. ... nasquu taline 4 years ago soi, squu accident tsinawali,sdanelv vna McClaine Cemetery --tsoginilvwi,sdanelv hena, ...I’m one of the head... (board members) board member una... una otsinvgalisgo ... hisgidv notsia, nigada, una’dv Memorial Day digilvwi,sdane--dagilvwisdanelv una adela detsigisidohv, ...y’know donations and stuff... noquudv tsigatiyv...
segments.translation: Just totaled it. The second time, four years ago, when I had an accident, at McClain Cemetery, we were working and I’m one of the head board members. That’s where we were cleaning, five or six of us. Memorial Day, that’s where I used to work collecting money for donations and stuff. That’s when I was waiting…

segments.speaker: emma-falling
segments.translation: To turn in.

segments.speaker: lucy-anderson
segments.translation: To turn in.

segments.speaker: lucy-anderson
segments.text: ᎩᎶ just ᏚᎦ,ᏢᏍᏔᏅ he was going 80 mph ᎠᏮᏂᎸ ᎠᎢ ᏗᏢ ... ᎠᎢ: ᏂᎦᏓ, ᏓᎩᏲᏍᏓᏁᎸ car
segments.transliteration: gilo just duga,tlvstanv he was going 80 mph awvnilv ai ditlv ... ai: nigada, dagiyosdanelv car
segments.translation: And a car come by going 85mph and hit me from behind. He tore up my car.

segments.speaker: emma-falling
segments.text: ᎠᏤ ᏍᏊ ᏙᏆᎴᎳ ᎤᎲ ... ᏍᎩᎾ Jimson ᎤᏍᏕᎵᎲ
segments.transliteration: atse squu doqualela uhv ... sgina Jimson usdelihv
segments.translation: She had a brand new car, too. And that’s why Jimson was helping her.

segments.speaker: lucy-anderson
segments.text: ᎯᎢᏃ ᎯᎢ ᏥᎨᎲ 3 years ago ᏃᏊᎴ ᏥᎬᏮᏂᎸ ᏍᎩᎾ, ᏥᎧᏁᎮᏍᎬ ᎾᎯᏳ ᎬᏳᎴᏅᎲ ᎡᏍᎦ, ᎾᏩᎵ,ᏍᏓᏁᎸ Ꮎ Ꮭ ᏍᏊ ᏳᏓᎭ Ꮭ ᎣᏍᏓ, ᏱᎨᎰ ᎠᎩᎦ,ᏖᎾᏍᏗ ... ᎠᎢ ᏂᎦᎵ,ᏍᏗᎰ ᎠᏎᏃ, --ᎪᎯᎢᎦ ᏍᏗ ᏓᏤᏝ ᏅᏬᏘ ᎮᎾ, ᏥᏩᎩᎩᏒ ᏒᎯ,
segments.transliteration: hiino hii tsigehv 3 years ago noquule tsigvwvnilv sgina, tsikanehesgv nahiyu gvyulenvhv esga, nawali,sdanelv na tla squu yudaha tla osda, yigeho agiga,tenasdi ... ai nigali,sdiho aseno, --gohiiga sdi datsetla nvwoti hena, tsiwagigisv svhi,
segments.translation: About three years ago, I got hit again. Like she was saying, that’s when my health problems started. Sometimes even looking around my sight is... Like it’s doing this.” [gestures]. But today, it’s a little bit better. I went and got some medicine yesterday.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Oh yeah? That’s good.

segments.speaker: emma-falling
segments.text: ᎠᏯ ᎨᎲ Ꮎ ... ᎦᏚᏏᏴ ᎠᏎ ᎠᏓ (ᏧᏂᎸᏅ,Ꮧ,/ᏧᏂᎸᏈ,Ꮧ,) ᏧᏂᏢᎩ ᏗᎩᎸᏫᏍᏓᏁᎸ Hillcrest --ᏅᎩᏍᎪᎯ, ᎾᏕᏘᏱ ᏂᎨᏒᎾ ... ᏦᎢ ᏱᏅᏓ, ᎠᎩᎷᎳ, ᏅᎩᏍᎪᎯ, ᏧᏕᏘᏴᏓ, ᏳᎵ,ᏍᏙᏗ ᏓᎩᎸᏫᏍᏓᏁᎸ ᎥᎾ Ꮎ ... Ꮎ ᎮᎾ ... “volunteers” ᏥᏓᏃᏎᎰ...
segments.transliteration: aya gehv na ... gadusiyv ase ada (tsunilvnv,di,/tsunilvqui,di,) tsunitlvgi digilvwisdanelv Hillcrest --nvgisgohi, nadetiyi nigesvna ... tsoi yinvda, agilula, nvgisgohi, tsudetiyvda, yuli,sdodi dagilvwisdanelv vna na ... na hena ... “volunteers” tsidanoseho...
segments.translation: Me. Over there, Gadusi, I worked at the hospital. Hillcrest. 40 years – little less, I lack about three months to make it 40 years – I worked there. The volunteers they’re called…

segments.speaker: lucy-anderson
segments.text: ...ᏧᏂᏢᎩ, ᏳᏂᎷᏨ, ...ᎠᏲᏁᎦ Ꮭ ᎠᏂᏬᏂᏍᎩ y’know ᏣᎳᎩ ᎯᎢ ᏥᏩᏂᏯ
segments.transliteration: ...tsunitlvgi, yunilutsv, ...ayonega tla aniwonisgi y’know tsalagi hii tsiwaniya
segments.translation: …when some sick people come. They don’t speak English. If they’re Cherokee speakers…

segments.speaker: emma-falling
segments.translation: …they call me to come help them.

segments.speaker: lucy-anderson
segments.translation: She has helped the doctors at Hillcrest.

segments.speaker: emma-falling
segments.text: Cohlmia ᏣᏓ, ᎠᎨ office ᏧᏬᏢ George Cohlmia or “Cohlmeal” ᏓᏃᏎᎰ ᎠᎭᏂ ... He’s a...
segments.transliteration: Cohlmia tsada, age office tsuwotlv George Cohlmia or “Cohlmeal” danoseho ahani ... He’s a...
segments.translation: Cohlmia, he has an office. George Cohlmia. Here they call him “Cohlmeha.” He’s a…

segments.speaker: lucy-anderson
segments.translation: Heart doctor.

segments.speaker: emma-falling
segments.text: Heart doctor...surgeon y’know ᏍᎩᎾ --ᎤᎪᏛ ᏥᏍᏕᎸᏗ, ᏛᎵ,Ꮟ ᎥᎾ Hillcrest-Ꭲ ᏥᏚᎸᏫ,ᏍᏓᏁᎠ, ᎥᎾ ... ᎩᎳ, ᎠᎭᏂ, ᏤᎲ ᎪᎯ ᏥᎩ, ... ᎤᎪᏗ ᏥᏍᏕᎸᏗ, -ᎪᎯᏗ ᏍᎩ ᎾᏩᏛᏁᎸ Hillcrest-Ꭲ ᏃᏊᎴ Ꮎ ... ᏌᏊ ᏳᏩᎦ,Ꮣ, an award ᏥᎬᎩᏁᎸ ... a free trip to San Antonio...
segments.transliteration: Heart doctor...surgeon y’know sgina --ugodv tsisdelvdi, dvli,si vna Hillcrest-i tsidulvwi,sdanea, vna ... gila, ahani, tsehv gohi tsigi, ... ugodi tsisdelvdi, -gohidi sgi nawadvnelv Hillcrest-i noquule na ... saquu yuwaga,da, an award tsigvginelv ... a free trip to San Antonio...
segments.translation: Heart doctor…surgeon, y’know. I helped him a lot at Hillcrest. He used to work there at Hillcrest and now he’s here. And I helped him a lot there, too. I have done that a long time. One time, they gave me an award for a free trip to San Antonio.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Well, I’ll be…

segments.speaker: emma-falling
segments.text: ᎦᏥᏍᏕᎸᎲ ᎤᎪᏗ ... ᎤᎪᏗ ᎦᏥᏍᏕᎸᏗ, ᎠᏂᏣᎳᎩ, ᎢᎾ ... ᎠᏂᎦᏴᎳ ᏳᏂᎷᏣ, ᏏᏓᏁᎸ ᎾᏁᎸᎾ ᏱᎩ, ᏃᏊ ambulance ᎩᎶ ᏳᏘᏂᏃᏢ ᏍᎩᏃ ᎬᎩᏯᏂᏍᎬ ᎤᎪᏗ ᏍᎩ ᎾᏩᏛᏁᎸ ... and uh... ᎾᎿ ᏣᎩ,ᏍᏆᏛ ᏓᎩᎸᏫ,ᏍᏓᏁᎲ ᏣᎩ,ᏑᎵᎪᏨ Ꮎ ᎠᏂᎦᎾᎦ,Ꮨ, ... Ꮎ Cherokee Nation ᎥᎾ I guess they contracts with Hillcrest ᎠᏂᎦᎾᎦ,Ꮨ, ᏍᎩᎾ ᏗᎿᏬᏍᏙᏗ--blanket ᏚᏂᏅᏁᎸ ᎠᏂᎦᎾᎦ,Ꮨ, ... ᏌᏊ ᎦᎾᎦ,Ꮨ, ᎠᎩᏅᏁᎸ ᏍᎩᎾ blanket Ꮭ... He didn’t deserve it. He thought I should have it. So he gave me his blanket. I still have it.
segments.transliteration: gatsisdelvhv ugodi ... ugodi gatsisdelvdi, anitsalagi, ina ... anigayvla yunilutsa, sidanelv nanelvna yigi, noquu ambulance gilo yutininotlv sgino gvgiyanisgv ugodi sgi nawadvnelv ... and uh... nahna tsagi,squadv dagilvwi,sdanehv tsagi,suligotsv na aniganaga,ti, ... na Cherokee Nation vna I guess they contracts with Hillcrest aniganaga,ti, sgina dihnawosdodi--blanket duninvnelv aniganaga,ti, ... saquu ganaga,ti, aginvnelv sgina blanket tla... He didn’t deserve it. He thought I should have it. So he gave me his blanket. I still have it.
segments.translation: I have helped a lot of them, the Cherokee speakers. When the older ones came, and nobody from the family was with them. When the ambulance brought someone they always called for me. I’ve done a lot of that. And when I finished my work, I quit my job. The doctors, Cherokee Nation, they do contracts with Hillcrest doctors. They gave the doctors blankets. One of the doctors gave me his blanket – he said he didn’t deserve it. He thought I should have it, so he gave me his blanket. I still have it.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Really?

segments.speaker: emma-falling
segments.translation: Yeah.

segments.speaker: lucy-anderson
segments.translation: She has helped a lot of people, Magadel(a).

segments.speaker: emma-falling
segments.text: Yeah. ᎾᎿ ... ᏃᏊᎴ ᎠᏧᏣ ᎠᎩ,ᏢᏤᎸ ...high school...ᏣᏯᎥ ᎤᎴᏅᎡᎸ ᎤᏢᎬ ᎾᎯᏳ, ᏓᏩᎴᏅᎲ ᎪᎱᏍᏗ, ᎠᏎ ᎪᎱᏍᏗ, ᎠᏩᏛᏁ,Ꮧ ᎠᏯ, ...to keep my mental health... Ꮎ --ᎠᏂᏥᎸᏍᎩ ᎣᏍᏓ, ᏂᏕᎬᏁᎲ Ꮎ...
segments.transliteration: Yeah. nahna ... noquule atsutsa agi,tlvtselv ...high school...tsayav ulenvelv utlvgv nahiyu, dawalenvhv gohusdi, ase gohusdi, awadvne,di aya, ...to keep my mental health... na --anitsilvsgi osda, nidegvnehv na...
segments.translation: My boy got sick on me. It started when he was in high school. He got sick. And I felt like I had to do something to keep my mental health. I would arrange flowers…

segments.speaker: lucy-anderson
segments.translation: Like Memorial flowers…

segments.speaker: emma-falling
segments.text: ᎾᎴ ᏱᎩ ... Christmas, Easter, or for decoration for the home. ᏥᏈᏍᏙᎲ ᏓᏬᏢᏅ ᎠᏂᏥᎸᏍᎩ, ᎠᏩᏌᏭ ᎣᏍᏓ, ᏂᏕᎬᏁᎲ Ꮭ ᏱᏓᏩᏕᏠᏆᎥ Ꮎ Hobby Lobby-Ꮽ ᏩᏪᏙᎸ ᎦᏥᎦᏙᏍᏗᎲ ᏂᏓᏅᏁᎲ ᎥᎾᏭ ᏓᏩᏕᏠᏆᎥ ᏍᎩᎮᎾ, ᏥᏈᏍᏙᎲ ᎠᏂᏥᎸᏍᎩ, Ꮎ Hillcrest ᎣᏍᏓ, ᏂᏗᎨᏥᏴᏁᎸ ᎪᎯ ᏥᎩ, Ꮎ ... ᏗᏓᏂᏐᏗ ᏗᏢᏗ ᎠᏂᏥᎸᏍᎩ, ᏕᎪᏢᏍᎪ
segments.transliteration: nale yigi ... Christmas, Easter, or for decoration for the home. tsiquisdohv dawotlvnv anitsilvsgi, awasawu osda, nidegvnehv tla yidawadetloquav na Hobby Lobby-wu wawedolv gatsigadosdihv nidanvnehv vnawu dawadetloquav sgihena, tsiquisdohv anitsilvsgi, na Hillcrest osda, nidigetsiyvnelv gohi tsigi, na ... didanisodi ditlvdi anitsilvsgi, degotlvsgo
segments.translation: Christmas, Easter, or for decoration for the home. I made a whole bunch of flowers. I didn’t go to school to learn it, I just went to Hobby Lobby and watched them do it. That’s when I made a whole bunch of flowers for Hillcrest. Now, I make flowers to put on the graves.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: You make them.

segments.speaker: lucy-anderson
segments.translation: She’s got a whole lot of real pretty ones. Do you still have some [pictures]?

segments.speaker: emma-falling
segments.translation: Yeah, I think so.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Do you sell them?

segments.speaker: emma-falling
segments.translation: M-hm. A black woman…

segments.speaker: lucy-anderson
segments.translation: …she lives in Tulsa.

segments.speaker: emma-falling
segments.text: ᎥᎥ ‘Ꮲ ᏁᎵ,ᏍᎪᎯ, ᏑᏓᎵ ᏳᏕᏘᏴᏓ, ᎠᎦᏴᎵᎨ ᎠᎬᎿᎨ ᏍᎩᎾ ᎠᎩᎾᏝᎥ ... ᎠᎩᎾᏝᎣ ᎣᏍᏓ, ᏂᏕᏥᏴᏁᎰ ᎦᎵᏆᏍᎪᎯᏴ ᏑᏓᎵᏥ,ᏊᎴ ᏱᎩ, ᏕᎪᏢᏍᎪ
segments.transliteration: vv ‘tlv neli,sgohi, sudali yudetiyvda, agayvlige agvhnage sgina aginatlav ... aginatlao osda, nidetsiyvneho galiquasgohiyv sudalitsi,quule yigi, degotlvsgo
segments.translation: She’s about 86. An old black woman. She hires me to make flowers for her. I probably make 70 to 600.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Oh man!

segments.speaker: emma-falling
segments.text: Ꮟ I’ll show you. ᎠᎭᏂ ᎢᎦᏓ Ꮟ ᏓᎩᎾ
segments.transliteration: si I’ll show you. ahani igada si dagina
segments.translation: Wait. I’ll show you. I still have some [pictures].

segments.speaker: lucy-anderson
segments.translation: She makes a whole bunch of pretty ones.

segments.speaker: emma-falling
segments.translation: I sell a lot of them, but not for myself…

segments.speaker: lucy-anderson
segments.translation: …that woman you're helping.

segments.speaker: emma-falling
segments.text: yeah ᎠᏮᏈᏴᎡᎰ ᎠᏎᏃ ᏕᎪᏢᏍᎪ ᎠᏩᏌ, ᏂᎦᏓ, ᏧᎾ,ᏓᏂᏐᏗ ᏏᏓᏁᎸ
segments.transliteration: yeah awvquiyveho aseno degotlvsgo awasa, nigada, tsuna,danisodi sidanelv
segments.translation: …yeah, she pays me. But I make a whole bunch of them for the cemetery, or for family.

segments.speaker: lucy-anderson
segments.translation: She brings them, she brings them.

segments.speaker: emma-falling
segments.text: Durbin ᎮᎾ, ᏍᏊ ᏧᏲᎱᏒ ᏦᎢᎭ ᏥᏓᏬᏢᏅ ᏌᏊ ᎯᎢ ᏗᎧᎾ,Ꮧ ᏌᎪᏂᎨ ᎠᏂᎩᎦᎨ ᎤᏂᏁᎦᏅ ᎠᏂᏲᏍᎩ ᎤᏴᏅ ᏥᎩ, Ꮎ ᏔᎵ, ᏔᎷᏣ ᏕᎦᏢ,Ꮫ ᏥᏓᏬᏢᏅ ᏧᏂᏲᎱ-- ...let’s see... ᎯᎢᏛ ᎣᏂ ᎠᏬᏢᏅ ᎨᎵ ᎯᎠ
segments.transliteration: Durbin hena, squu tsuyohusv tsoiha tsidawotlvnv saquu hii dikana,di sagonige anigigage unineganv aniyosgi uyvnv tsigi, na tali, talutsa degatlv,dv tsidawotlvnv tsuniyohu-- ...let’s see... hiidv oni awotlvnv geli hia
segments.translation: But Durbin, when he died, I made three of them. One of them was this big [gestures]. It was red, white, and blue. Because he was a veteran. I made two baskets out of the flowers. This is the one I made last.

segments.speaker: lucy-anderson
segments.text: See? ᏧᏃᏚᏛ When it’s in-person—when you see them in person...they’re beautiful.
segments.transliteration: See? tsunodudv When it’s in-person—when you see them in person...they’re beautiful.
segments.translation: See? They are real pretty. When you see them in-person…they’re beautiful.

segments.speaker: emma-falling
segments.text: ᎾᏍᏊ Ꮷ--...cemete--ᎩᎶ ᏳᏲᎱᏌ, ᎤᏓᎭ ᎬᎩ,ᏛᏛᎲᏍᎪ ᏗᏬᏢᏗ
segments.transliteration: nasquu tsu--...cemete--gilo yuyohusa, udaha gvgi,dvdvhvsgo diwotlvdi
segments.translation: Also, when somebody dies I get asked to make flowers.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Yeah?

segments.speaker: lucy-anderson
segments.translation: She makes them real quick.

segments.speaker: emma-falling
segments.text: Uh huh. ᏃᏊᏅ ᎠᎦᏴᎵᎨ ᏫᏥᏯᏛᏛᎲᏍᎪ ᏍᎩᎾ, ...let’s see... Ooh, I can’t find those others, sis. Gosh...ᏧᏬ-- Ꮎ ... ᏐᏫᏂᎳ ᏧᏲᎱᏒ Ꮎ ... Covid ᎠᎬᏱ --ᏧᎷᏨ ᎩᎳᏫ, ᎢᎪᎯᏓ,Ꭷ ᏍᎩ ᏄᎵ,ᏍᏓᏁᎸ ᎤᏲᎱᏒ ᎠᎵ,ᏣᏙᎲᏍᎨ--ᎠᎵ,ᏣᏙᎲᏍᎬ ᎦᎶᏇᏗ ᏥᎨᎲ ᎥᎾ Cornerstone Church Ꭳ’ᎢᏂᎳ, Ꮟ ᏓᎩ,ᏘᏯ ᎪᎯ ᏥᎩ, ...
segments.transliteration: Uh huh. noquunv agayvlige witsiyadvdvhvsgo sgina, ...let’s see... Ooh, I can’t find those others, sis. Gosh...tsuwo-- na ... sowinila tsuyohusv na ... Covid agvyi --tsulutsv gilawi, igohida,ka sgi nuli,sdanelv uyohusv ali,tsadohvsge--ali,tsadohvsgv galoquedi tsigehv vna Cornerstone Church o’inila, si dagi,tiya gohi tsigi, ...
segments.translation: I just ask that old lady. Let’s see…Ooh, I can’t find those others, sis. Gosh…they’re prett… When Sowinila died, right when that Covid came. He got that Covid right away and he was a preacher at Locust Grove. Cornerstone Church – our sister is the pastor there now…

segments.speaker: lucy-anderson
segments.text: ᎩᎳᏫ, ᎢᎪᎯᏓ, ᏧᏢᏥᏢ week...week and a half-Ꮫ ᎢᎪᎯᏓ, ᏥᏭᏴᏢ ᎦᎾᎦ,Ꮨ
segments.transliteration: gilawi, igohida, tsutlvtsitlv week...week and a half-dv igohida, tsiwuyvtlv ganaga,ti
segments.translation: He got sick right away. And he was in the hospital for about a week and a half.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: That’s when he died?

segments.speaker: lucy-anderson
segments.translation: M-hm. He was 61 years old.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Just that old?

segments.speaker: lucy-anderson
segments.translation: Three years ago.

segments.speaker: emma-falling
segments.text: *Sure wish I could find it. The one I just did for her.*
segments.transliteration: *Sure wish I could find it. The one I just did for her.*
segments.translation: Sure wish I could find it. The one I just did for her.

segments.speaker: lucy-anderson
segments.text: Ꮎ ᏍᏊ ᏧᎳᏫ,ᏍᏗ ᎤᎾ ᏍᏊ ... ᏕᎪᏢᏍᎪ ᎤᎾ ᏧᏫᏗ ᏍᎩᎾ
segments.transliteration: na squu tsulawi,sdi una squu ... degotlvsgo una tsuwidi sgina
segments.translation: Also, the church, she makes flowers to take over there.

segments.speaker: emma-falling
segments.text: ᏥᏈᏍᏗ,Ꮫ ᏴᏫ ᏂᏕᏥᏴᏁᎰ Ꮎ ᏍᏊ ...oh shoot I wish I could find it... Ꮎ ᎣᏂ ᏥᏲᏢᎾᏁᎸ ...[a] heart. I can’t find it. Maybe it’s on Daniel’s. ... heart. ᎯᎢ ᏱᎩᏓ, ᏔᎵ, ᎢᎦ ᏓᏬᏢᏅ ...it’s...ᏌᏊ ᎤᏬᏚᏨ ᏂᏥᏴᏁᎸ ... ᎢᎾ ᏗᏓᏂᏐᏗ ᎠᏎᏃ ᎩᎳ ᏱᎪᎯᏓ ᏴᏫ, ᏓᏂᏃᏍᎩ ... ᎩᎳᏫ ᏱᎪᎯᏓ ᏱᏓᏂᏃᏍᎩᏍᎪ ᎠᏂᏥᎸᏍᎩ
segments.transliteration: tsiquisdi,dv yvwi nidetsiyvneho na squu ...oh shoot I wish I could find it... na oni tsiyotlvnanelv ...[a] heart. I can’t find it. Maybe it’s on Daniel’s. ... heart. hii yigida, tali, iga dawotlvnv ...it’s...saquu uwodutsv nitsiyvnelv ... ina didanisodi aseno gila yigohida yvwi, daninosgi ... gilawi yigohida yidaninosgisgo anitsilvsgi
segments.translation: I give the flowers to a lot of people. Shoot, I wish I could find it. The last one I made for him was a heart. As big as a heart. I can’t find it. Maybe it’s on Daniel’s. It was a heart this big [gestures]. I made two of them. One of them, I made it real pretty for him. There at the cemetery, the people steal them. They sure steal them flowers fast.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: You mean the ones in the cemetery?

segments.speaker: emma-falling
segments.text: ᎥᎥ ... ᎥᎾ ᏲᏤᏙ ᎢᎦ ᏙᎦᏂᏝᎣ ᏙᏥᏁᏍᎪ ᎩᎳ ᏱᎪᎯᏓ, ᏴᏫ ᏯᏂᎷᎦ ᏓᏂᏃᏍᎩ, ᎠᏂᏥᎸᏍᎩ, Ꮎ ᏍᏊ ... Louise Ꮎ Chris, Durbin ᎤᏍᏓᏴᎲᏍᎩ, ᏄᎵ,ᏍᏔᏅ ᎢᎦ ᏥᏲᏢᎾᏁᎰ Bell-Ꭲ ᎨᎵ ᎢᎾ ᏧᎾ,ᏓᏂᏐᏗ ᏥᏲᏢᎾᏁᎸ ᎤᏥ ᎦᏂᏌᎲ ᎯᎢ ᏱᎩᏓ, ᏂᏥᏴᏁᎸ ᎤᏪᏙᎸ ᎦᏳᎳ ᎩᎶ ᎤᏃᏍᎩᏓ, ᎨᎲ ooh! --ᎤᏂᏁᎩᎵ,Ꮧ ᎪᎯ ᏥᎩ,
segments.transliteration: vv ... vna yotsedo iga doganitlao dotsinesgo gila yigohida, yvwi yaniluga daninosgi, anitsilvsgi, na squu ... Louise na Chris, Durbin usdayvhvsgi, nuli,stanv iga tsiyotlvnaneho Bell-i geli ina tsuna,danisodi tsiyotlvnanelv utsi ganisahv hii yigida, nitsiyvnelv uwedolv gayula gilo unosgida, gehv ooh! --uninegili,di gohi tsigi,
segments.translation: M-hm. The only time we have them there is while we’re there. Then we take them off. They can steal them real quick. I made flowers for Louise. Chris, Durbin’s wife, used to be – I make flowers for them, too. They have a cemetery at Bell. That’s where her mom is buried. So, I made flowers for her. So, I made a big [gesture] flower for her, and when she went back somebody had already stolen it. People are no good nowadays.

segments.speaker: lucy-anderson
segments.text: ᎩᎳᏫ ᏱᎪᎯᏓ ᎪᎱᏍᏗ ᏯᏂᏫᏓ, Ꮭ ᎪᏍᏗ ᏱᎦᏁᎳ, ᎾᏅ,ᏍᏊ ᏧᎾ,ᏓᏂᏐᏗ Ꮎ ᎡᏧᎳ ᎣᏍᏓ--...we’re caretakers... --ᏓᏃᏎᎰ
segments.transliteration: gilawi yigohida gohusdi yaniwida, tla gosdi yiganela, nanv,squu tsuna,danisodi na etsula osda--...we’re caretakers... --danoseho
segments.translation: They’ll steal something and not even care. Both of the cemeteries – we’re caretakers, they call them.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Y’all look after them?

segments.speaker: lucy-anderson
segments.text: ᎥᎥ ᎣᏍᏓᎦ,ᏎᏍᏗ ᏂᎪᎯᎸ ᎣᎨᏙᎰ ᎾᏍᏊ ᏣᎩ,ᏢᏥᏢ ...when I had surgery... ᎠᎩᏄᎸᎲᏍᎬ ᎣᏍᏓ, ᎾᏩᏛᏁ,Ꮧ ᎪᎯ ᎯᏍᎩᎢᏁ...this Memorial Day... ᏂᎦᎵ,ᏍᏔᏅ ᎣᏍᏓ, ᎡᎵᏭ,Ꮓ ᎪᎱᏍᏓ, ᎾᏩᏛᏁ,Ꮧ ᎨᎲ ᎾᏅ ᎠᎬᏱ ᏗᏢ Memori--ᏧᎾ,ᏓᏂᏐᏗ ᎠᏐᏴ ...we put American flags on each one of those poles.
segments.transliteration: vv osdaga,sesdi nigohilv ogedoho nasquu tsagi,tlvtsitlv ...when I had surgery... aginulvhvsgv osda, nawadvne,di gohi hisgiine...this Memorial Day... nigali,stanv osda, eliwu,no gohusda, nawadvne,di gehv nanv agvyi ditlv Memori--tsuna,danisodi asoyv ...we put American flags on each one of those poles.
segments.translation: We look after them. I go there all the time. Then I got sick when I had surgery, I couldn’t do anything. But this…fifth…this Memorial I was able to do something. There is a fence at the cemetery and we put American flags on each one of those poles.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Oh, yeah? Well, I’ll be...

segments.speaker: lucy-anderson
segments.text: And we cleaned it... ᏂᎦᏓ ᎣᏥᏅᎦᎵᏍᎪ ᎣᏧᏖᏏᏍᎪ ᎣᏍᏓ,
segments.transliteration: And we cleaned it... nigada otsinvgalisgo otsutesisgo osda,
segments.translation: We clean everywhere and pick up stuff.

segments.speaker: emma-falling
segments.text: ᏃᏊᎴ ᏍᏊ ... Ꮎ ᏙᏱ ᎤᏁᏓᏍᏗ ...ᎠᏓᏁᎸ Ꮎ Cherokee Nation Ꮎ grant money ᏗᏙᎩᏁᎸ ᎤᏅ,ᏙᏗ ... ᎣᏍᏓ ᏄᏅᏁᎸ ᎠᏂᎨᏳᏣ, ... Ꮎ mirrors ᏄᏅᏂ,Ꮫ ᏃᏊᎴ ᎪᎱᏍᏗ ᎣᎩᎲ ᎩᎶ ᏂᎦᏓ, ᎤᏃᏍᎩᏐᏅ
segments.transliteration: noquule squu ... na doyi unedasdi ...adanelv na Cherokee Nation na grant money didoginelv unv,dodi ... osda nunvnelv anigeyutsa, ... na mirrors nunvni,dv noquule gohusdi ogihv gilo nigada, unosgisonv
segments.translation: Also, there is a bathroom building. Cherokee Nation gave us grant money for them to use to fix the bathroom up. The girls’ bathroom, they put up mirrors, and everything else we had, somebody stole it.

segments.speaker: lucy-anderson
segments.text: ᎾᏍᏊ Ꮎ ᎦᎶᎯᏍᏗ ᎩᎶ ...kicked it in... ᏄᏓᎴᏃ ᎠᏎ ᎣᎬᏂ,ᏙᏗ ᏃᎦᎵ,ᏍᏓᏁᎸ
segments.transliteration: nasquu na galohisdi gilo ...kicked it in... nudaleno ase ogvni,dodi nogali,sdanelv
segments.translation: Also, somebody kicked in the door. We had to put a new one on.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: Yeah, ᏙᏳ,Ꮫ ᎢᎾ, ᏚᏓᎴᎿᏓ ᏏᎾ, ᎡᏘᏴ ᏥᎨᎲ ... ᏕᎦᏛᏏᏗᏒ
segments.transliteration: Yeah, doyu,dv ina, dudalehnada sina, etiyv tsigehv ... degadvsidisv
segments.translation: There is a lot of difference today than it was years ago when we were growing up.

segments.speaker: lucy-anderson
segments.translation: There really is.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: Ꮭ ᏍᎩ ᎢᎦ ᎡᏍᎦ ᎡᏙᎯ, ᏱᎨᎮ ᎾᎯᏳ ... Ꮭ ᏱᎬᏥᎦᏫ,Ꮓ ... Man, ᏙᏳ ᏍᏊ ᎤᏬᏚᏨ ᏍᎩᎾ yeah!
segments.transliteration: tla sgi iga esga edohi, yigehe nahiyu ... tla yigvtsigawi,no ... Man, doyu squu uwodutsv sgina yeah!
segments.translation: There wasn’t as much wrongdoings back then. …Man! That’s really pretty.

segments.speaker: emma-falling
segments.text: That’s one of the crosses ... ᎠᏯᏛ ᎯᏛ ... ᏔᎵ, ᏓᏬᏢᏅ ᎯᎢᏳᏍᏗ --ᏦᏍᏓᏓᎸ ᏧᏂᎳᏫᏍᏗ ᎦᎶᏇᏗ ᏓᎦ,ᏘᏴ ᎢᎾ ᏂᏚᏮᏂ,Ꮣ, ... Oh! ᎯᎢᏛ ᏥᎻ, ᏦᏍᏗᏃᎮᎠ, ᎯᎠ ᏥᎻ,
segments.transliteration: That’s one of the crosses ... ayadv hidv ... tali, dawotlvnv hiiyusdi --tsosdadalv tsunilawisdi galoquedi daga,tiyv ina niduwvni,da, ... Oh! hiidv tsimi, tsosdinohea, hia tsimi,
segments.translation: That’s one of the crosses …I made two of them. My sister at her church in Locust Grove, where she’s a pastor. That’s where she has them. Oh! This is Jim, that’s we were talking about. [Shows Guy a picture]. This is Jim.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Oh, Jim.

segments.speaker: emma-falling
segments.translation: Jimson Bluebird.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: I would like to go visit him.

segments.speaker: emma-falling
segments.text: ᏍᎩᎾ ... ᏍᎩᎾ ᏗᎾ,ᏓᏅᏟ, ᏣᏂᏂᏏᎲ ᏗᏥᏲ--ᎣᏍᏓ -ᏕᎨᏥᏴᏁᎸ ᎠᏂᏥᎸᏍᎩ,
segments.transliteration: sgina ... sgina dina,danvtli, tsaninisihv ditsiyo--osda -degetsiyvnelv anitsilvsgi,
segments.translation: When they buried his brother, I made all the flowers for them.

segments.speaker: lucy-anderson
segments.translation: He’s standing by his grave. [Pictured)

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Yeah.

segments.speaker: emma-falling
segments.text: Did I show you the cross? Okay. I couldn’t remember. But...but... ᏍᏆᎳ--ᎠᏮᏌᏭ ᎾᏩᏕᎶᏆᎥ Ꮭ ᎩᎶ ᎠᏪᏲᏅ ᏱᎩ, ᎠᏎᏅ Ꮎ ᎠᎦᏴᎵᎨ ᎩᎶ ᎤᏍᏕᎵᏍᎩ, ᎤᏩᏌ, ᏕᎪᏢᏍᎬ ᎠᏂᏥᎸᏍᎩ, ᎩᎶ ᎤᏃᏎᎴ ᏍᎩᎾ, ᎦᏛᏁᎲ ᏧᏝᏃᎮᏗ ᏛᎩ,ᏓᏁᎸᏎ
segments.transliteration: Did I show you the cross? Okay. I couldn’t remember. But...but... squala--awvsawu nawadeloquav tla gilo aweyonv yigi, asenv na agayvlige gilo usdelisgi, uwasa, degotlvsgv anitsilvsgi, gilo unosele sgina, gadvnehv tsutlanohedi dvgi,danelvse
segments.translation: Did I show you the cross?! OK. I couldn’t remember. I learned how to do this on my own, nobody taught me. The old lady was making flowers and nobody was helping her, and somebody told her that I was doing this, she called me.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Oh. She talked to you/called you?

segments.speaker: emma-falling

segments.text: Yeah, yeah. ᏍᎩᎾᎾ Boy... ᎠᎩᏄᎸᎲᏍᎬ ᎦᏥᏲᎵᏤᏗ ᏳᏍᏗ ᏍᎩᎾ ᏥᏓᏂᏬᏂᏍᎬ ᎠᏎᏅ ᎨᏒ ᎠᏩᏕᎳᎰᏒ ᏳᏍᏗ ᎨᎲ --ᏚᎾ,ᏓᎴᎬ ᎣᎩᏬᏂᎯᏍᏗ, Ꮎ “Ꮭ...Ꮰ...Ꮯ...Ꮱ...Ꮲ” Ꮎ ᎣᏥᏪᏍᎬ ᎠᏯ, ᎠᎭᏂ, ᎢᏤᎯ,--ᎢᏕᎯ, ᎾᏃ ᎥᎾᎾ ᏗᏢ, ᎠᏁᎯ, Ꮭ ᏍᎩ ᏳᏍᏗ, ᎾᏂᏪᏍᎬ ᎾᎿᏃ like ... “ᎠᏓᏠᏍᏗ” ... “ᎠᏓᏦᏍᏗ,” ᏯᎾᏓ,
segments.transliteration: Yeah, yeah. sginana Boy... aginulvhvsgv gatsiyolitsedi yusdi sgina tsidaniwonisgv asenv gesv awadelahosv yusdi gehv --duna,dalegv ogiwonihisdi, na “tla...tlo...tli...tlu...tlv” na otsiwesgv aya, ahani, itsehi,--idehi, nano vnana ditlv, anehi, tla sgi yusdi, naniwesgv nahnano like ... “adatlosdi” ... “adatsosdi,” yanada,
segments.translation: Yeah, yeah, those ones. Boy, those are the ones I don’t understand at all. But I learned what the difference is, how we talk. Those, “tla, tlo, tli, tlu, tlv” – we use these sounds here. But over there, they don’t use them. Like, “adatlosd(i)” they say, “adatsosd(i).”

segments.speaker: lucy-anderson
segments.translation: Huh.

segments.speaker: mitch-holcomb
segments.text: ᏍᎩᎮᎾ, ᏍᎩ ᏥᎦᏗᏍᎬ ᏍᎩ ᏣᏅ,ᏗᏍᎬ Ꮎ “tl” sound ... “Ꮳ”ᏭᎢᎦ ᎠᎾ,ᏗᏍᎪ ... ᏙᏳ ᎢᎦ ᎠᏩᏦᏍᏓᏁᎲ ᏥᎨᎲ ᎠᏂᏬᏂᎲ ᎩᎵᏛ ᎠᏩᏕᎳᎰᏒ ᏍᎩᏳᏍᏗ ᎾᏅᏂ,ᏗᏍᎬᏃ ᎧᎵᏃ ᏧᎴᏅᎲ ᎣᏍᏓ, ᎦᏥᏲᎵᏤᎲ ᏳᏍᏗᎲ ᎠᏂᏬᏂᏍᎬ yeah.
segments.transliteration: sgihena, sgi tsigadisgv sgi tsanv,disgv na “tl” sound ... “tsa”wuiga ana,disgo ... doyu iga awatsosdanehv tsigehv aniwonihv gilidv awadelahosv sgiyusdi nanvni,disgvno kalino tsulenvhv osda, gatsiyolitsehv yusdihv aniwonisgv yeah.
segments.translation: They don’t use the tl-sound. All they say is “tsa.” It was really hard to understand them until I noticed they weren’t using that sound. Then, I could understand them well. Yeah…

segments.speaker: lucy-anderson
segments.translation: How cool!

segments.speaker: mitch-holcomb
segments.text: ᏱᏣᎦ,ᏎᏍᏔᎾ, yeah... ᏱᏣᎦ,ᏎᏍᏔᎾ, ... ᏳᏓᎭ ᏱᏂ,ᎬᏫ, gah... ᎩᎳ ᏱᎪᎯᏓ ...you go... “Haw...ᏙᎨ ᏍᎩ ᏂᎬᏪ” then you think back and change that sound “oh! ᏍᎩᏕ ᏂᎬᏪ!”
segments.transliteration: yitsaga,sestana, yeah... yitsaga,sestana, ... yudaha yini,gvwi, gah... gila yigohida ...you go... “Haw...doge sgi nigvwe” then you think back and change that sound “oh! sgide nigvwe!”
segments.translation: If you pay attention, they say something and you don’t understand, then you think back, “You change that sound. Oh! That’s what they said.”

segments.speaker: lucy-anderson
segments.translation: Yeah, that’s what happened to me, too!

segments.speaker: mitch-holcomb
segments.translation: Yeah.

segments.speaker: lucy-anderson
segments.translation: Yeah.

segments.speaker: emma-falling
segments.translation: Yeah.

segments.speaker: mitch-holcomb
segments.translation: Yeah.

segments.speaker: emma-falling
segments.text: ᏍᎩᏛ ᏃᎩᎾᎵ,ᏍᏓᏁᎰ ᏳᏓᎭ Ꮎ ᏌᏊ ᎠᎨᏳᏣ ᎤᏂᎪᏓ’Ꭱ ᏦᎦᏕᎶᏆᎡ ᎡᏧᎳᎭ Chiloccoo Ꮎ North Carolina ᎠᏁᎯ, ooh!’Ꮫ Ꮎ Nancy Blackfox ᎢᎦ ᎦᏣᏄᎵ, ᎦᏬᏂᏍᎬ ᎣᎩᏄᎸᎲᏍᎬ ᎣᎨᎵ;Ꮧ
segments.transliteration: sgidv noginali,sdaneho yudaha na saquu ageyutsa unigoda’e tsogadeloquae etsulaha Chiloccoo na North Carolina anehi, ooh!’dv na Nancy Blackfox iga gatsanuli, gawonisgv oginulvhvsgv ogeli;di
segments.translation: That’s what happens to us, sometimes. There was one girl, a lot of us went to school together at Chilocco. They lived in North Carolina. That one, Nancy Blackfox, she talked real fast. We couldn’t understand.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: ᎾᏛ ᏍᏊ ᏥᎩ, ᎤᏴᏜ, ᏗᏢ, ᎠᏣᎳᎩ ᎠᏂᏬᏂᏍᎩ, ᏃᏊᎴ ᎯᎢ ᏗᏢ, ᏍᏗᎩᏓ, ᏚᏓᎴᎿᏓ,
segments.transliteration: nadv squu tsigi, uyvdla, ditlv, atsalagi aniwonisgi, noquule hii ditlv, sdigida, dudalehnada,
segments.translation: Also, the speakers from the North and the ones that live down here, they’re kinda different.

segments.speaker: emma-falling
segments.translation: M-hm, they’re different.

segments.speaker: lucy-anderson
segments.text: ᏍᎩ --ᏥᏃᎩᏪᏎᎲ Grandma ᏥᎨᎲ “ᏚᎾ,ᏓᎿᏓ ᎠᏂᏬᏂᏍᎬ” ᏣᏓ “ᏄᏓᎴ ᏓᏅ,ᏗᎰ”
segments.transliteration: sgi --tsinogiwesehv Grandma tsigehv “duna,dahnada aniwonisgv” tsada “nudale danv,diho”
segments.translation: That’s what Grandma used to tell us. “They talk different, they use different sounds.”

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: ᏌᏊ ᏳᏩᎦ,Ꮣ, ᎮᎾ, ᎠᎩ,ᏍᏓᏴᎲᏍᎩ, ᏣᎦᏛᏛᎲᏍᎬ “ᎭᏢ ᏣᏁᏎ -ᏣᏘᏟ;Ꮧ?” ᎦᏪᎮᎸ “ᏣᏘᏟ;ᏗᎩ? ‘ᏙᎲ ᏳᏍᏗ ᏍᎩᎾᎾ?” “Your blouse!” ᎠᎪᏎᎴ ᏍᎩᎾ ... ᏃᏊ ᎪᎯᏴ ᏥᎩ, “ᎭᏢ ᏣᏁᏎ ᏣᎿᏬ?” ᏴᏓᏛ
segments.transliteration: saquu yuwaga,da, hena, agi,sdayvhvsgi, tsagadvdvhvsgv “hatlv tsanese -tsatitli;di?” gawehelv “tsatitli;digi? ‘dohv yusdi sginana?” “Your blouse!” agosele sgina ... noquu gohiyv tsigi, “hatlv tsanese tsahnawo?” yvdadv
segments.translation: One time, somebody asked my wife, “Where did you get your blouse?” “Tsatitli,digi? What is that?” she said. “Your blouse!” they said to her. And then nowadays they say, “Where did you get your shirt?”

segments.speaker: emma-falling
segments.translation: That’s right.

segments.speaker: lucy-anderson
segments.translation: That’s right.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: ᎡᏘᏴ ᏥᎨᎲ ᏍᎩᎾ, “ᎭᏢ ᏣᏁᏎ ᎠᏘᏟ;Ꮧ,?” ᏯᎾ,ᏓᏙᏌ, ᏥᎨᎲ ᏍᎩ ᎢᎦ ᎮᎾ, ᎢᎩᏲᎱᏎ ᎠᏣᎳᎩ, ᎭᏫᏂ, ᎦᏬᏂᎯᏍᏗ ᎨᏒ ᎠᏂᎦᏴᎳ,Ꮓ ᎾᏁᎲᎾ ᏥᎩ, ᏣᏅ,Ꮤ, ᏧᎾᏂᎩᏓ, ᏴᏓ Bluebird ᏥᏗᏃᎮᏍᎬ ᎡᎵᏭ...ᎡᎵᏭ ᎡᏘᏴ ᎤᏂᏬᏂᎯᏍᏗ, ᎡᎵ ᏱᎦᏬᏂᎯ,
segments.transliteration: etiyv tsigehv sgina, “hatlv tsanese atitli;di,?” yana,dadosa, tsigehv sgi iga hena, igiyohuse atsalagi, hawini, gawonihisdi gesv anigayvla,no nanehvna tsigi, tsanv,ta, tsunanigida, yvda Bluebird tsidinohesgv eliwu...eliwu etiyv uniwonihisdi, eli yigawonihi,
segments.translation: “Where did you get that blouse?” They’d say back then. We are really losing the old Cherokee words. Now that the old ones are gone. That Jim Bluebird you talked about, he can probably speak that old language.

segments.speaker: emma-falling
segments.translation: That’s what they say.

segments.speaker: emma-falling
segments.translation: Yeah, that’s how he speaks.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Really?

segments.speaker: lucy-anderson
segments.text: ᎤᏬᏚᏨ ᏱᎦᏬᏂᎯ, ᏙᏳ, ᏣᏚᎵ Ꮳ,ᏛᎪᏗ ᎦᏬᏂᏍᎬ ᏙᏳ, ᎣᏍᏓ’Ꭱ ᎯᏯᏛᏗ ᏳᏅ,Ꮤ,
segments.transliteration: uwodutsv yigawonihi, doyu, tsaduli tsa,dvgodi gawonisgv doyu, osda’e hiyadvdi yunv,ta,
segments.translation: He speaks real pretty. If you really want to hear him speak, go [see him]. If you ask him something, he’ll know.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: I would like to go visit with him.

segments.speaker: emma-falling
segments.text: He’s over at the nursing home-Ꭲ go ahead.
segments.transliteration: He’s over at the nursing home-i go ahead.
segments.translation: He’s over there at the nursing home – go ahead.

segments.speaker: lucy-anderson
segments.text: L: *You got paper? Write his name down.*
segments.transliteration: L: *You got paper? Write his name down.*
segments.translation: Yeah, you got paper? Write his name down.

segments.speaker: emma-falling
segments.text: You can get his phone number... Jimson ᏫᏃᏎᎸ
segments.transliteration: You can get his phone number... Jimson winoselv
segments.translation: You can get his phone number if you go tell Jimson.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: ᎯᎢᏃᎲᏃ ᏥᏕᏓᏝᏃᎲᎳ ... ‘ᏙᎲ ᏍᏕᎵ ᏕᏍᏓᏅ,Ꮫ ᎨᎲ Ꮎ ᏴᏛ ᎯᎢ ᏥᏓᎾ,ᏕᎶ,ᏆᎠ, ᏧᏂ,ᏍᏗ ᏗᏂᏲᏟ, ᎠᏣᎳᎩ, ᎤᏂᏬᏂᎯᏍᏗ ᏗᎾ,ᏕᎶ,ᏆᏍᎩ, ᏣᏂᏯ ‘ᏙᎲ ᏍᏕᎵ ᏂᎯ ᎨᎲ ᎣᏏᏭᎨ ᏍᎩ ᏥᎾᎾᏛᏁᎠ,?
segments.transliteration: hiinohvno tsidedatlanohvla ... ‘dohv sdeli desdanv,dv gehv na yvdv hii tsidana,delo,quaa, tsuni,sdi diniyotli, atsalagi, uniwonihisdi dina,delo,quasgi, tsaniya ‘dohv sdeli nihi gehv osiwuge sgi tsinanadvnea,?
segments.translation: This conversation we’ve had, what do you all think in your mind about these little children learning the Cherokee language? The students that are here, what do you all think – are they doing alright?

segments.speaker: lucy-anderson
segments.text: --ᏣᏅ,Ꮤ ᎦᎵᎡᎵᎦ, ᏥᏂᏣᏛᏁᎠ, ᏓᎩᏲᎱᏎᎳ, ᎮᎾ, ᎪᎱᏍᏗ, ᏕᏗᏬᏂᏍᎬ ᏗᏕᏲᎲᏍᎬᎾ, ᏥᎩ, ᏗᏂᏲᏟ, ᎯᎢ
segments.transliteration: --tsanv,ta galieliga, tsinitsadvnea, dagiyohusela, hena, gohusdi, dediwonisgv dideyohvsgvna, tsigi, diniyotli, hii
segments.translation: I am really grateful for what you all are doing. We are going to lose our language if we don’t teach the kids.

segments.speaker: emma-falling
segments.translation: It really begins with the kids.

segments.speaker: lucy-anderson
segments.translation: It will disappear.

segments.speaker: emma-falling
segments.text: ... ᏧᏂ,ᏍᏗ ᎬᏩᏓᎴᏅ, Ꮩ ᎮᎾ ᎮᏍᏗᏅ ᎠᎯᏗ ᏱᎩ ᎠᏕᎶ;ᏆᏍᏗ ... Ꮭ ᏯᏩᏅ,Ꮤ, ᏳᏍᏗ ᎠᏁᏲᎲᏍᎪ ᎠᎭᏂ, Ꮭ ᏯᏩᏅ,Ꮤ, ᎾᎾᏛᏁᎲ ... ‘Ꮩ...
segments.transliteration: ... tsuni,sdi gvwadalenv, do hena hesdinv ahidi yigi adelo;quasdi ... tla yawanv,ta, yusdi aneyohvsgo ahani, tla yawanv,ta, nanadvnehv ... ‘do...
segments.translation: Really, it begins with the children. But they need to start when they are babies because it’s not easy to learn [the language]. I don’t know what they are teaching them here, I don’t know what they are doing.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: ᏣᎳᎩᏛ ᎤᏂᏬᏂᎯᏍᏗ ᏃᏊᎴ ᏧᏃᏱ,ᏍᏗ ᎪᎱᏍᏗ, ᏴᏓ ᏥᏗᏃᎮᏍᎬ ᎩᎳ ᎢᏳᏍᏗ, ... ᎾᏃ ᏴᏓ “ᏗᎵ,” ᏥᏓᏗᎰ Ꮎ “skunk?” ᏍᎩ ᏳᏍᏗ, yeah.
segments.transliteration: tsalagidv uniwonihisdi noquule tsunoyi,sdi gohusdi, yvda tsidinohesgv gila iyusdi, ... nano yvda “dili,” tsidadiho na “skunk?” sgi yusdi, yeah.
segments.translation: They’re learning to speak Cherokee and name things they can say. What we were talking about a while ago. Like, we say “dil(i)” – Skunk, stuff like that.

segments.speaker: lucy-anderson
segments.text: yeah ᎣᏍᏓ,Ꮫ ᏣᏅ,Ꮫ ᎣᏍᏓ, ᏂᏣᏛᎾ ... ᎦᎵᎡᎵᎦ,
segments.transliteration: yeah osda,dv tsanv,dv osda, nitsadvna ... galieliga,
segments.translation: Yeah. You all are doing real well. I’m glad.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: ᎠᏯᏍᏊ ᎦᎵᎡᎵᎪ ᏍᎩᏛ ᏥᎾᎾ,ᏛᏁᎠ, ᏥᏩᎦ,ᏘᏅᏒ ᎤᏂᎬᏫᏳ ᎠᏂᏣᎳᎩ, ᏕᎩᎧᎲ Ꮭ ᏍᎩ ᎢᎦ ᏧᏂᎸᏫ,ᏍᏓᏁᎲ ᏱᎨᎮ ᎠᏣᎳᎩ, ᎤᎬᏩᏟ;
segments.transliteration: ayasquu galieligo sgidv tsinana,dvnea, tsiwaga,tinvsv unigvwiyu anitsalagi, degikahv tla sgi iga tsunilvwi,sdanehv yigehe atsalagi, ugvwatli;
segments.translation: I am grateful, too, that they are teaching. The Cherokee leaders that we had years before, they didn’t do as much work for the language like they are today.

segments.speaker: lucy-anderson
segments.text: ᎾᎯᏳᎧ ᏳᎾ,ᎴᏅᎲ ooh!...ᏳᎪᏓ, ᏯᏂᎠ, ᏗᏂᏲᏟ, ᏳᎪᏓ, ᏳᏂᏬᏂᎯ, ᏃᏊ ᏥᎩ,
segments.transliteration: nahiyuka yuna,lenvhv ooh!...yugoda, yania, diniyotli, yugoda, yuniwonihi, noquu tsigi,
segments.translation: Yeah, they should’ve started back then with the children. There would be more of them speaking nowadays.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: ᎠᏎᏃ, Ꮭ ᏍᎩ ᎢᏴ ᏱᏓᏓᏅ,ᏖᏍᎬ ᎾᎯᏳ ᏙᏳ, ᏍᎩᎾ
segments.transliteration: aseno, tla sgi iyv yidadanv,tesgv nahiyu doyu, sgina
segments.translation: But we weren’t thinking ahead like that.

segments.speaker: emma-falling
segments.text: Uh-uh. ᎠᏯᏅ ᏱᎦᏅᎢᏌᏗ, ᎦᏲᏟᎲ ᎠᏂᏬᏂᏍᎬ ᏣᎳᎩ,
segments.transliteration: Uh-uh. ayanv yiganvisadi, gayotlihv aniwonisgv tsalagi,
segments.translation: Uh-uh. It is our fault that there are not very many Cherokee speakers.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: ᎣᏍᏓᏛ ᏱᎦᏅ,Ꮦ ᏱᏗᏗᏅᏫᏍᏓᏅ ᎮᎾ, ᎤᏂᎬᏫᏳ ᏥᏕᎩᎧᎲ ᏍᎩ ᏳᎾ,ᏛᏁ,Ꮧ
segments.transliteration: osdadv yiganv,te yididinvwisdanv hena, unigvwiyu tsidegikahv sgi yuna,dvne,di
segments.translation: If we were thinking right, we would’ve told our leaders that we had then, for them to do this [speak Cherokee].

segments.speaker: emma-falling
segments.text: ᎢᎦᏛ ᏍᏊ ᎠᎾ,ᏕᎰᏍᎨ ᎤᏂᏬᏂᎯᏍᏗ ᏣᎳᎩ, ᎮᏍᏗᏅ ᎠᏂᏲᏁᎦ,--ᎠᏂᏲᏁᎦᎭ ᏗᏢ, ᎤᏂᏬᏂᎯᏍᏗ ᎤᎾ,ᏚᎵᏅ Ꭸ--Ꭱ--ᎢᎦᏓ ᏍᎩ ᏄᎵ,ᏍᏔᎾ, ᎠᎾ,ᏕᎰᏍᎪ ᏌᏊ ᏳᏩᎦ,Ꮧ Ꮎ ... ᎡᏥ ᏥᎨᎲ Tuscon ᎣᎨᏅᏒ ᎾᎾ ᎠᏍᏆᏂ ᏗᏢ, ᏬᎨᏙᎸ Old Mexico across... ᎡᎳᏗ, ᏬᎩᎶᏒ ...we crossed over... ᏙᏳ,Ꮕ ᏥᏈᏍᏗ, ᎠᏂᏍᏆᏂ, ᏥᏚᎾ,ᏓᎿᏅᏃ ᎤᏂᏍᏆᏂᎭ ᎠᏂᏬᏂᏍᎪ ᏂᎦᏓ, ᏍᏓᏱ Ꭺ!ᏍᏗ, ᎠᏛᏗ ᎨᎰ Ꮭ ᏳᎾ,ᏚᎵᎰ Ꭺ!ᏍᏗ, ᎢᎦᏴ ᏚᏂᎬᏩᎵ,Ꮫ Ꭺ!ᏍᏗ, ᎨᏣᏃᏎᏗ “Haw!” Mom-Ꮫ “ᏙᏳ,Ꮫ ᎤᏁᎵ,Ꮧ, --ᏄᎾᏛᎾ, Ꮭ ᏍᏊ ᎨᎦᏝᏃᎮᏗᏛ ᎠᏣᎳᎩ, ᎬᏗ ᏗᏂᏬᏂᎲ ‘Ꮩ ᏛᎾᏛᏁᎵ?” ᎤᏛᏅ ᏣᎳᎩᎭ ᎣᎩᏂᏬᏒ ᎡᏝᏪ ᏄᎾᎵ,ᏍᏓᏅ (ᎤᏂᏰᏥᏍᎬ)
segments.transliteration: igadv squu ana,dehosge uniwonihisdi tsalagi, hesdinv aniyonega,--aniyonegaha ditlv, uniwonihisdi una,dulinv ge--e--igada sgi nuli,stana, ana,dehosgo saquu yuwaga,di na ... etsi tsigehv Tuscon ogenvsv nana asquani ditlv, wogedolv Old Mexico across... eladi, wogilosv ...we crossed over... doyu,nv tsiquisdi, anisquani, tsiduna,dahnanvno unisquaniha aniwonisgo nigada, sdayi go!sdi, advdi geho tla yuna,duliho go!sdi, igayv dunigvwali,dv go!sdi, getsanosedi “Haw!” Mom-dv “doyu,dv uneli,di, --nunadvna, tla squu gegatlanohedidv atsalagi, gvdi diniwonihv ‘do dvnadvneli?” udvnv tsalagiha oginiwosv etlawe nunali,sdanv (uniyetsisgv)
segments.translation: There were a bunch of them who didn’t want to speak Cherokee, out of shame. They just wanted to speak English. That’s what happened to some of them, they were ashamed. One time, my mother and us, we all went to Tucson. We went to Mexico. Old Mexico we walked and crossed over. There were a lot of Mexicans had stores there and all they talked was Spanish. It was hard to talk to them. They didn’t want to tell us the price of things. My mom said, “Haw. They’re not doing things right. They don’t want to talk to us, let’s just talk Cherokee and see what they’re going to do.” So, we talked Cherokee and they all got quiet. [laughter]

segments.speaker: lucy-anderson
segments.text: ᎾᎿ ᏧᏂᎳᏫ,ᏍᏗ ᏥᏤᏅᏒ ᎾᎿ Ꮎ ... somebody’s wedding ... tell them!
segments.transliteration: nahna tsunilawi,sdi tsitsenvsv nahna na ... somebody’s wedding ... tell them!
segments.translation: How about the time y’all went to church…somebody’s wedding…tell them!

segments.speaker: emma-falling
segments.text: This is just a story ... same time we were on our way to Tuscon ... Albuquerque ᎣᎦᎴᏫᏍᏔᏅ ᎥᎾ’Ꭱ ᎣᏍᏗᏁᎳ --ᎪᎯᏓ, ᏥᎨᎲ Ꮎ taxi ᎮᎾ, ᏧᎲ ᎤᏩᏌ, taxi service ... ᏍᎩᎾ ᎣᎦᏦᏔᏅ ᏍᎩᎾ ᏓᏤᏢ ᏙᏆᎴᎳ, ᎣᎩᎲ ... yellow cab ... (ᎤᏂᏰᏥᏍᎬ)
segments.transliteration: This is just a story ... same time we were on our way to Tuscon ... Albuquerque ogalewistanv vna’e osdinela --gohida, tsigehv na taxi hena, tsuhv uwasa, taxi service ... sgina ogatsotanv sgina datsetlv doqualela, ogihv ... yellow cab ... (uniyetsisgv)
segments.translation: This is just a story…same time, we were on our way to Tucson. We stopped in Albuquerque. My husband, way back then, he had a taxi. He had his own taxi service. That’s what we drove, cause that was the only good car we had. A yellow cab.

segments.speaker: lucy-anderson
segments.translation: Yellow cab!

segments.speaker: emma-falling
segments.text: ᎡᏥᏃ ᎣᏂ, ᏗᏢ Ꭳ’ᎢᏂᏣᎥ ᎾᏃ Albuquerque ... Old Town ... ᎤᏪᏘ, ᏗᎦᏚᎲ ᎤᎾ ᎣᎦᎴᏫᏍᏔᏅ ᏧᏂᎳᏫ,ᏍᏗ ᎠᏓᏁᎸ ᎥᎾ ᎠᎬᏱ ᏗᏢ ᎣᎦᎴᏫᏔᏅᏅ ᏴᏫ, ...there was a 50th anniversary... ᎨᎵᏛ ...celebration ᎨᎲ ... ᎥᎾᎾ
segments.transliteration: etsino oni, ditlv o’initsav nano Albuquerque ... Old Town ... uweti, digaduhv una ogalewistanv tsunilawi,sdi adanelv vna agvyi ditlv ogalewitanvnv yvwi, ...there was a 50th anniversary... gelidv ...celebration gehv ... vnana
segments.translation: Me and Mom were in the back. In Albuquerque – Old Town Uwet(i) Digaduhv – that’s where we stopped, at an old church, we stopped. Right at the building there was a 50th anniversary celebration.

segments.speaker: lucy-anderson
segments.translation: It was a big church.

segments.speaker: emma-falling
segments.text: Ꮎ ᏧᏂᎳᏫ,ᏍᏗ ᎾᏃ cab Larry ᎤᎾ ᎤᎲ ᏃᏭᏅ ᏴᏫ ᏛᏂᏄᎪᏨ ᏧᏂᎳᏫ,ᏍᏗ ᏙᏳ ᎤᏂᎵᎮᎵᎬ ᎪᎩᏂᎪᎲ ᏍᎩᎾ ᏏᏓᏁᎸ ᎠᏁᎵᎲ (ᎤᏂᏰᏥᏍᎬ) ᎤᏂᎷᏨ ᏙᏆᎴᎳ, ᎣᎩᏂᏠᏒ ...they were all from Colorado. They were all from somewhere else... ᎤᏣᏘᏂ, ᏥᏚᎾᎩᏓ, ᎨᎲ ᏴᏫ, ᎠᏁᏙᎲ ᎠᏲ ᎣᎪᎵ,ᏓᏁᎸ ᎾᎾ ... that was when I ... purple ᎨᎵ ᎠᏩᏌᏃᎲ ᎯᎢ ᏯᏖᎾ, ᎠᎭᏂ, ᏂᎬᏂ,Ꮫ ᎤᏩᏌ, ᏓᎶᏂᎨ ᎤᏌᏃᎲ ᏙᏳ,Ꮕ ᎣᏍᏗᏍᏆᏂ ᎮᎾ, ᏳᏍᏗ, (ᎤᏂᏰᏥᏍᎬ) ᏙᎩᏂᏁᎦᎸ y’know ᎤᏂᏍᏆᏂ, ᎢᏳᏍᏗ, ᏍᎩᎾ ᏳᏍᏗ, ᏚᏂᏁᎦᎸ ᏙᏳ ᎣᎪᎵ,ᏓᏁᎸ “ᏄᎳ! ᏕᏥᏴᎭ ᎢᏣᎵ,ᏍᏓᏴᎲᎦ!” ᎪᎪᏬᏎᎸ
segments.transliteration: na tsunilawi,sdi nano cab Larry una uhv nowunv yvwi dvninugotsv tsunilawi,sdi doyu uniliheligv goginigohv sgina sidanelv anelihv (uniyetsisgv) unilutsv doqualela, oginitlosv ...they were all from Colorado. They were all from somewhere else... utsatini, tsidunagida, gehv yvwi, anedohv ayo ogoli,danelv nana ... that was when I ... purple geli awasanohv hii yatena, ahani, nigvni,dv uwasa, dalonige usanohv doyu,nv osdisquani hena, yusdi, (uniyetsisgv) dogininegalv y’know unisquani, iyusdi, sgina yusdi, duninegalv doyu ogoli,danelv “nula! detsiyvha itsali,sdayvhvga!” gogowoselv
segments.translation: The church. Larry parked the cab there. The people came out of the church and they were so proud to see us. They probably thought we were one of them. [laughter] They all came to the car and we got out. We noticed they were all from Colorado. They were all from somewhere else – they came from somewhere else. We thought that was really funny. I was wearing a purple dress and it had a colored band across the dress and she had on a yellow dress. I guess, really, we looked like Mexicans. [laughter] Our skin was similar to the Mexicans ‘cause they have the same color skin. We thought that was really funny. And they said, “Hurry up! Come on in and eat!”

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Did you all go eat?

segments.speaker: lucy-anderson
segments.text: ᎾᏛ ᏍᏊ ᏌᏊ ᏳᏩᎦ,Ꮣ, Mama ᏙᏳ ᎤᏬᎵ,Ꮫ ... ‘Ꮲ ᎣᎨᏅᏒ ᎩᎶ ᎪᎱᏍᏗ, ... ᎤᎪᎲ Mama ᎪᎱᏍᏗ, ᎤᏩᎯᏍᏗ ᎤᏚᎵᎲ ᎠᎦᏛᏛᎲᏅ ᎤᏓᎿᏅ “ᎯᎳ ᎤᎬᏩᏟ;Ꮣ?” ᎪᏍᏗ, Ꮎ ᎤᏓᎿᏅ Ꮭ ᎪᏍᏗ, ...y’know didn’t take—pay attention to her... “Haw!” ᏣᏓ, “ᏂᎦᏛ ᏍᎩ ᏥᎵᏃᎮᏗ, ᎠᏯ ᏥᎩ, ᏍᏊᏅ president-Ꭲ ᏍᏊ--(ᏣᎳᎩ, ᎬᏗ, ᎤᏔᏅ) “ᏍᎩ --ᏱᏥᎵᏃᎮᏓ, --Ꮭ ᏍᎩ ᏱᏂ,ᎦᎦᏛᎦ, ᏥᎿᏛᏁᎠ,” ᎠᎪᎮᎸ ᏣᏗᎲ
segments.transliteration: nadv squu saquu yuwaga,da, Mama doyu uwoli,dv ... ‘tlv ogenvsv gilo gohusdi, ... ugohv Mama gohusdi, uwahisdi udulihv agadvdvhvnv udahnanv “hila ugvwatli;da?” gosdi, na udahnanv tla gosdi, ...y’know didn’t take—pay attention to her... “Haw!” tsada, “nigadv sgi tsilinohedi, aya tsigi, squunv president-i squu--(tsalagi, gvdi, utanv) “sgi --yitsilinoheda, --tla sgi yini,gagadvga, tsihnadvnea,” agohelv tsadihv
segments.translation: One time, Mom, it was real funny – we went somewhere – and Mom saw something good, and she wanted to buy it. She asked the store owner, “How much does it cost?” They were not very friendly, y’know. They didn’t pay attention to her. “It don’t matter who it is – even if it’s the president, (he was speaking Cherokee) I would not treat them like you are treating me,” she said to them.

segments.speaker: emma-falling
segments.translation: My mom was funny.

segments.speaker: lucy-anderson
segments.translation: She always had something to say right away.

segments.speaker: emma-falling
segments.translation: She did.

segments.speaker: lucy-anderson
segments.text: “President ᏍᏊ ᏳᎷᏣ, ᏱᏥᏰᎶᎦ ᏚᏯ,” ᏣᏓ, (ᎤᏂᏰᏥᏍᎬ) “Ꮭ ᏱᎦᎦᏕ’Ꭳ,” ᏣᏓ,
segments.transliteration: “President squu yulutsa, yitsiyeloga duya,” tsada, (uniyetsisgv) “tla yigagade’o,” tsada,
segments.translation: “Even if the president showed up, I would feed him beans.” She said. [laughter] “I would not be ashamed.”

segments.speaker: emma-falling
segments.text: John Kennedy-Ꮫ ᏙᏳ --ᎤᎸᏉ’Ꮧ, ᏥᎨᎲ “ᏥᎸᏉᏗ John Kennedy,” ᏣᏗᎰ ᎾᎾ Truman ᏙᏳᏛ ᏍᏊ ᏧᎸᏉᏗ ᏥᎨᎰ
segments.transliteration: John Kennedy-dv doyu --ulvquo’di, tsigehv “tsilvquodi John Kennedy,” tsadiho nana Truman doyudv squu tsulvquodi tsigeho
segments.translation: She really liked John Kennedy. “I really like John Kennedy,” she would say. And that Truman, she really liked him, too.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: ᎡᏘᏴᏛ John Kennedy ᏥᎨᎲ ᏗᎾ,ᏓᏅᏟ, ᏧᎶᎯᏍᏔᏅ Twin Oaks
segments.transliteration: etiyvdv John Kennedy tsigehv dina,danvtli, tsulohistanv Twin Oaks
segments.translation: A few years ago, John Kennedy’s brother came through Twin Oaks.

segments.speaker: emma-falling
segments.text: oh yeah ᏝᏍ ᎤᏩᏌ, John Kennedy-Ꮽ ᏱᎨᏎ? Ꮎ ᏗᎾ,ᏓᏅᏟ,Ꮫ ᏍᏊ ᏧᎷᏣ,--ᏧᏪᏙᎸ
segments.transliteration: oh yeah tlas uwasa, John Kennedy-wu yigese? na dina,danvtli,dv squu tsulutsa,--tsuwedolv
segments.translation: Oh yeah. It wasn’t just John Kennedy himself? His brother came by, too.

segments.speaker: lucy-anderson
segments.text: John Kennedy did, too...ᏙᎲ? ᎦᏅᏓᏗ ᎮᎾ,
segments.transliteration: John Kennedy did, too...dohv? ganvdadi hena,
segments.translation: John Kennedy did, too. Because I remember.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: ᏗᎾ,ᏓᏅᏟ, ᎤᏩᏌ, ᏥᎪᎥ ᏧᎶᎯᏍᏔᏅ ᎠᏂ-Peter’s ᏧᏁᏅᏒ ᏧᎶᎯᏍᏔᏅ Ꮎ ᏥᏚᏝᏃᎮᏔᏂᏙᎴ ᏧᎦ,ᏖᏃᎵᏙᎴ yeah... ᎾᏃ ᏍᏊᏃ ᏍᏗᎩᏓ,Ꮓ ᏧᏍᏕᎵ;Ꮧ ᏳᏍᏗ ᏄᎵ,ᏍᏔᏅ Robert Kennedy ᏥᎨᎲ ᎢᏗᏣᎳᎩ,Ꮓ ᎠᏎᏃ, Ꮭ ᎪᎯᏗ ᏱᎨᎮ ᏥᏕᏰᏥᏲᎸ
segments.transliteration: dina,danvtli, uwasa, tsigov tsulohistanv ani-Peter’s tsunenvsv tsulohistanv na tsidutlanohetanidole tsuga,tenolidole yeah... nano squuno sdigida,no tsusdeli;di yusdi nuli,stanv Robert Kennedy tsigehv iditsalagi,no aseno, tla gohidi yigehe tsideyetsiyolv
segments.translation: I just saw his brother when he came by. He stopped by the Peters home. He talked to them, and he looked around. I think that’s when he first started to help support us Cherokees, Robert Kennedy. It wasn’t for a long time after that he got shot.

segments.speaker: emma-falling
segments.translation: That’s right.

segments.speaker: lucy-anderson
segments.translation: That’s right.

segments.speaker: emma-falling
segments.translation: That’s right, I remember that.

segments.speaker: lucy-anderson
segments.translation: It got bad for all of us, after that time.

segments.speaker: emma-falling
segments.text: Robert Kennedy ᏥᏫ,ᏥᎪᎥ Ꮎ airport-Ꭲ ᏥᏚᎷᏨ ᏥᏩᏪᏙᎸ yeah.
segments.transliteration: Robert Kennedy tsiwi,tsigov na airport-i tsidulutsv tsiwawedolv yeah.
segments.translation: I saw Robert Kennedy at the airport when I went there.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Well… I appreciate it, I appreciate it.

segments.speaker: lucy-anderson
segments.translation: Yeah me too!

segments.speaker: emma-falling
segments.translation: Did we do good?

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Y’all did good! You all took us places.

segments.speaker: emma-falling
segments.translation: We probably sounded funny.

segments.speaker: lucy-anderson
segments.translation: Or bad. [laughs]
